on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, commissioner, thank you, mr davies, for having facilitated the work on this report. if we are talking about carbon capture for underground storage - what we have called ccs - we must recognize that the objectives set - as has already been said here - have not been achieved. those 12 major projects that were set in 2007 for 2015 are not going to be realised, mainly because of a financing problem and a basic mistake: because we have put everything - the financing - on the emissions market and on carbon - and you all know what has happened to that. does the fact that we are lagging behind, that the united states has gone ahead of us - as well as china and canada - mean that we have to abandon this technique? i don't think so, not at all. it is a technique which is obviously not a panacea - no one has said so - in the fight against climate change, but it is a complementary technique which does not compete with renewable energies, which accompanies them and which, of course, is the only one known in some respects, because controversy is generated when we talk about the production of thermal energy, but no one can deny that it is the only known method for reducing emissions in the steel, metal and cement industries, as has also been said here. so why does my group support this report? because we consider it balanced, because we consider it necessary - it is the basis for relaunching this technique - and, of course, because it asks the commission to study new forms of financing, to continue to collaborate with other states in order to share the experience gained in order to make progress as they have made progress. and of course it would also be good if we looked at how the european coal and steel research fund can be used to demonstrate or to do pre-commercial demonstrations of carbon capture. i do agree that all this must be done in the strictest respect for environmental standards, that we must not lower our standards and that we must of course also require companies to meet their responsibilities without any mitigation. it is one thing for technology to be necessary, the only one known to some industries, and another for it to serve as an alibi, alongside the crisis, to mitigate liability. we would disagree on that; otherwise, yes. our vote is in favour of the project.
mr president, i would like to express my satisfaction at this report, which, unlike other reports on energy policy, is a report that looks at the future of energy realistically. as the rapporteur has said, coal is an energy source which will continue to be used. so let's make it green or cleaner. we can't deny this technology because it's about coal, and we're demonizing coal. let's make it green! we have that potential in europe and we must take advantage of it. in some regions of europe - like mine, in asturias - this debate, this technology of co2 storage and capture, is looked at with great hope because it is a very important niche of employment for regions that are in industrial decline and whose jobs are in danger. some members of this parliament have visited and seen the professionalism with which two plants are working, two co2 capture plants, the one at la pereda in mieres and the one at ciuden in ponferrada. and i think it is worthwhile for the european commission to continue to invest in this technology, to do so in the short and long term, that is to say, to provide security and guarantees so that this technology can be exported throughout the european union. that europe can take the lead in the world market for a technology in which we are innovative, we are competitive and we have a great future, because we can convert our fossil fuels into clean energy through the use of them.
mr president, mr hodei is a european citizen, a 23-year-old basque man who, thanks to his own efforts and to various community programmes, acquired training and experience and began working as a computer engineer in belgium. on october 19th, he disappeared without a trace in the centre of antwerp. police found his cell phone, credit cards and documents in the hands of criminals. their parents, from the basque country, want to convey their pain and anguish today and call on the police and the belgian institutions, as well as europol, to continue working until they clarify an improper event in a large european city. they also ask us to push for the urgent transposition of the directive on the protection of victims of crime, because they know how important it is to be able to participate in criminal proceedings in any country of the union. finally, they are encouraged to encourage closer cooperation at european level to investigate disappearances, because the certainty of death is hard, but the uncertainty in which they have lived since 19 october is dying every day.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission would like to thank the rapporteur, mr winkler, for his valuable report on smart specialisation. we share the conclusions of the report. i cannot touch on all these conclusions in this short presentation, but let me highlight two which are particularly relevant for this moment in time, in preparation for the next programming period (2014-2020). firstly, priority-setting and new forms of governance. we have noticed that the ex-ante conditionality linked to the research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation in the cohesion policy regulations has already led to a new quality and dynamic in horizontal inter-ministerial cooperation and to closer involvement by universities and businesses in the development of regional strategies, partnership agreements and operational programmes. but i would like to thank you in particular for emphasising that the smart specialisation conditionality is not a statutory formal obligation. only through real commitment to economic transformation and real partnership between administration, business, academia and civil society can we kick-start the microeconomic engine and mobilise the innovation potential of all the regions. our ambition is for every euro spent on cohesion policy in the next seven years to be strategically targeted and result-oriented. this is why smart specialisation strategies are one of the main pillars of the reformed cohesion policy. we are guided by the conviction that you cannot dictate innovation, you can only cultivate it. research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation provide for a new economic rationale for public-private partnerships and operationalising. this should be a game-changer based on a new culture of cooperation and governance – what we call an entrepreneurial discovery process. secondly, concerning the step-up advice. your report highlights the positive impact of the advice that we provide to help with this process, in particular through the smart specialisation platform managed by the commissionʼs institute for prospective technological studies in seville. the platform now has 160 regions registered from all the european union member states plus norway, and 14 countries registered at national level which cooperate with this platform. platform activities will be continued and stepped up for two more years. the institute will in future intensify and fine-tune its mapping of the emerging smart specialisation areas. this is essential in assisting the regions in identifying possible cooperation partners for more trans-regional activities. it will also manage the two pilot projects of this parliament: the one on widening participation in horizon 2020 and the one on smart specialisation in greece. in addition, the directorate-general for regional policy has already signed more than 100 contracts to provide specific smart specialisation advice to countries and to regions. international organisations like the oecd and the world bank have recognised the importance of smart specialisation in economic development and are becoming engaged in supporting some central and east european countries. the commission is of the opinion that the concept of smart specialisation will help europeʼs regions to strengthen their innovation capacity and their ability to reap the benefits of innovation for economic growth and also for jobs.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to thank the alternative rapporteurs for their cooperation. i would also like to thank the two directorates-general of the commission involved for their support in clarifying my doubts and, of course, what i want to do is to congratulate the commission on this initiative and to raise this debate which, at the moment, is not really urgent but which responds to the need for the european union to have the possibility of establishing health systems based on electronic communication and the exchange of clinical data. health systems in the european union are facing major challenges as a result of population growth, including ageing, patient mobility - not just of patients but of health professionals - and increasingly limited health budgets. i am convinced that ehealth can be the means of improving the quality and efficiency of healthcare in the european union, by making the work of healthcare professionals easier, improving access to healthcare for people living in remote areas and reducing waiting times and also the repetition of diagnostic tests. it is essential that the views of health professionals and patients, who will be the main actors in the system, be taken into account. it is also essential that both patients and healthcare professionals believe in the benefits of ehealth and for this we must provide them with legal certainty as regards data protection. if the implementation of ehealth services in the future is to be technically successful, it is necessary to achieve technical standardisation and interoperability of european health systems, as well as a definition at eu level of certification and authentication schemes. lastly - and very importantly - it is essential that our primary objective in developing these projects is the interest of patients, as we cannot forget that access to quality healthcare is a recognised fundamental right.
i would like to thank you, mr president, for the work you have done on this report, which i would like to stress is committed to equality and to which i would add four nuances. the main potential users of health services are the elderly, vulnerable and those with literacy and digital access problems, and overcoming this reality requires intervention to eliminate these problems in these groups, as well as a profound cultural transformation of health organizations. the digital health effort should be comprehensive and incorporate other related or complementary care systems, such as social care services. respect for the principle of subsidiarity, because in almost all of europe the powers and provision of health services are decentralised and there are very innovative, regional or local experiences, which are a reference in the field, such as the 'e-prescription', the health council or telecare in the basque country. finally, i also respect linguistic diversity, because good communication is essential for good care in the health service.
mr president, commissioner, the right to quality health care is a recognized fundamental right. the future ehealth action plan should therefore focus its efforts and scarce resources on two objectives: ensuring better access to health services and greater equality among european citizens, ending inequalities and comparative injustices and strengthening patients' rights. to achieve this, it is necessary to involve and support healthcare professionals, patients and their organisations in the implementation of this action plan, to cooperate and coordinate with the different european systems, and to preserve the human and patient-centred dimension, taking into account the ageing of the european population. finally, i would like to call on the authorities of the government of my country - spain - to rectify and stop the privatisation of health care, which is aimed at defending the exclusive interests of business, to the detriment of the rights of patients. i therefore ask the president of my country - mr rajoy - to concentrate his efforts on improving and strengthening the public health system, which is the heritage of all spaniards and which should not be questioned or left in private hands. we are strengthening the pillar of the welfare state and social cohesion.

in writing. − against. the purpose of the proposal is to update the rules on the definition, description, presentation and labelling of aromatised wine products (e.g. vermouth, sangria, vinglögg, glühwein etc.). it also adds a chapter on geographical indications (gis), establishing a procedure for application and decision for protection of aromatised wine products. more specifically, the regulation aims at adapting the definitions and criteria for production in the light of technical developments and in accordance with wto requirements, at updating certain sales denominations, and at aligning the current regulation to the new comitology rules (delegated and implementing acts). the compromise will be supported by the big groups, but we voted against. generally speaking, the whole issue of ‘aromatized wines’ is not very pleasant from a green perspective; it is all about requirements on how much alcohol, sugars, sweeteners, colours etc. can be added to a certain product in order to be able to market it with terms such as ‘aromatised wine product’, ‘aromatised wine’, ‘aromatised wine-based drink’, ‘aromatized wine-product cocktail’, etc.

in writing. - i voted against this report because it continues the absurd bet on carbon capture and storage technology which has proved to be a complete failure. this technology was authorised by the eu through directive 2009/31, as it considers this technology as a key mechanism to reduce emissions. since then no plant has been developed, as this technology is excessively expensive and has incalculable long-term costs. with the problems that are currently being generated by injection technologies such as gas storage (for example the castor project in valencia) or fracking, continuing to bet on technologies of this type is justifiable only in the interests of the lobbies, since these "solutions" generate very serious environmental problems. because the commitment to reduce emissions must be real and based on a change in the development model, i voted against this report.
in writing. - my support for this own-initiative report on the development and implementation of carbon capture and storage (ccs) is because, in order to reduce emissions in europe, all available and complementary measures must be taken into account. the support for renewable energy is clearly still the ultimate objective of my group. but support for ccs, as well as investment in r&d&i to develop new technologies to reduce emissions during the transition to a low-carbon economy with renewables at its core, remains vital for europe. the report also stresses that the political and economic support of states remains the ultimate requirement for the development of ccs, since it is up to them to decide whether or not to use the technique in their respective emission reduction strategies. it is a balanced and realistic report, which accepts the potential of the ccs to reduce emissions, but which does not forget that our ultimate objective must be to support renewable energy.

in writing. − in favour. since the adoption of the first e-health action plan in 2004, the commission has developed targeted policy initiatives such as its recommendation on cross-border interoperability of electronic health record systems (2008/594/ec), its communication on the benefits of telemedicine for patient healthcare systems and society, and the establishment of the e-health network following directive 2011/24/eu (cross-border healthcare). progress has been made, but the promise of e-health remains to a large extent unfulfilled. important hurdles are: lack of awareness of, and confidence in e-health solutions; lack of interoperability; limited large-scale evidence of cost-effectiveness; lack of legal clarity for mobile applications and lack of transparency regarding the utilisation of data collected by such applications; inadequate or fragmented legal frameworks including the lack of reimbursement schemes for e-health services; high start-up costs involved in setting up e-health systems; regional differences in accessing ict services, and limited access in deprived areas. greens/efa amendments mainly focus on the recognition of the role of regional authorities and on preserving linguistic diversity. most of them were adopted in envi.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to promote the improvement of fraud control systems in the food chain. there have been many scandals in the european union over the past few years in the food sector because of the lack of adequate control systems. these control systems have not been adequately resourced, especially as agri-food companies have grown in size, complexity and diversification of the components of the products they bring to market. to prevent this kind of fraud, which endangers the health of european citizens, it is necessary to ensure the homogeneity of the control systems, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. this report was decided upon as a reaction to the horsemeat scandal, and to numerous other cases of fraudulent food labelling and other food frauds which impacted the eu food chain, such as the marketing of battery cage eggs as organic eggs, road salt in foods etc. different types of food fraud include adulteration, substitution, tampering and counterfeiting. the economic gain of fraud is further enhanced by the often ineffective sanction regime due to relatively low sanctions and large differences between member states’ practices. we have tabled amendments e.g. regarding country of origin labelling (the wording in the envi report weakens our amendments, but we agreed in the light of the overall compromises), mislabelling of fish species, shorter food chains, the necessity of action by member states in order to address issues raised by the fvo, the importance of official controls, which can never be replaced by industry-driven initiatives, the responsibilities of retailers, the need for establishing unannounced inspections as standard inspections, and the need to publish inspection results, e.g. in the form of a rating system. our amendments were almost all adopted.
in writing. - a few months ago, following the horse meat scandal, i put a parliamentary question (e-001617/13) on fraud in the food chain and mislabelling of products. i therefore warmly welcome the adoption of this report, which is in line with one of my concerns. as the report points out, food is safer than ever, and yet consumer confidence is at an all-time low as a result of a number of specific cases - which we must not allow to happen again under any circumstances. respect for consumer rights must be a key element of our policies, which is why we must act in the area of monitoring the correct labelling of food throughout the food chain and apply strict sanctions in the event of incorrect information on the contents of food.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to promote the development of labour inspectorates in the member states as a means of ensuring that labour legislation is enforced in the member states. labour regulations need an institutional structure to ensure compliance; without sufficient human resources to ensure labour inspections, regulations governing labour inspections cease to be an effective right. at european level, the lack of resources devoted to inspections has led to an increase in illegal working conditions, breaches of contracts, work in the shadow economy, etc. it is essential that the member states allocate the necessary resources to these inspection services to combat this. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. in pursuance of having effective labour inspection in monitoring the application of labour law, europe needs more than soft law to ensure that employment in member states will be decent, stable, healthy and safe. this report tries to draw attention to the urgent need for legally binding measures to enforce the protection of workers and the employment and the implementation of fundamental labour and social rights. this has to start by strengthening fundamental labour and social rights in the single market and by working to promote fair competition and workers’ rights. this principle must be laid down in primary eu legislation adopting a social progress protocol to safeguard basic social rights from any negative consequences of national reforms and austerity measures.

in writing. − i abstained. the europe 2020 strategy on smart, sustainable, and inclusive growth highlights the need for ‘inclusive growth’ which, amongst other things, empowers citizens through employment, investing in skills, fighting poverty and modernising labour markets and social protection. employee financial participation (efp) offers a tangible means of developing these themes by involving workers more in the decision-making of the companies they work for, helping to strengthen good governance, and ensuring a share of the financial benefits of a successful business. the involvement of workers in corporate governance like this can develop their opportunities to access meaningful lifelong learning within employment: efp often develops long-term thinking – as workers become more involved with decision-making and financial rewards they will develop longer-lasting relationships with their employers, giving employers more incentive to invest in training opportunities for their workforce. it is too confused for the greens.

in writing. − i voted in favour. social security systems in europe should help to provide protection against risks and low incomes, as well as to reduce inequalities in the eu member states. however, because of persistent economic difficulties associated with the financial crisis, difficult issues regarding the financing of the systems need to be tackled. during the economic crisis, the public finances of eu member states have been reduced, while the number of people out of work and in need of social support has grown. moreover, the substantial rise in unemployment, together with declining wages, has caused revenue from social security contributions to fall, thus jeopardising the european social model. it should also be noted that because of pressure on national budgets and cuts in pensions and other social benefits, the most vulnerable people have been affected and have fallen below the poverty threshold. in an effort to overcome the crisis, while priority has been given to restructuring budgets, the social-policy dimension has not been sufficiently taken into account and member states have not paid sufficient attention to the social objectives on employment and education set in the europe 2020 strategy, particularly with regard to reducing poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. - the economic crisis has affected millions of workers, who have had to adapt to new, sometimes abusive working conditions, coupled with a considerable reduction in public spending, which has increased poverty and the risk of social exclusion in large parts of european society. this report highlights the need for the national authorities of the member states to improve and facilitate access to social security for all workers, recognising this right as fundamental and as the basis of the european social system. the aim is therefore to protect the rights of workers, especially the selfemployed, since in recent years, as a result of the new forms of employment that have emerged, they are undoubtedly the most socially unprotected, for example, because they do not have the same social conditions in cases of maternity or paternity. it is also necessary to harmonise the concept of selfemployed at european level and to prevent false selfemployed from damaging the social system. i believe that the initiatives in this report will help to prevent the creation of labour exploitation and to provide greater social protection for workers.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a change of approach in the field of plastic waste management and production. the report presents the need to reconsider the production of such products on the basis of the circular economy, which takes into account the entire lifetime of the product. this approach suggests that plastics should not only be managed as waste, but also that the need to produce less of these materials, which take hundreds of years to decompose if released into the environment, must be taken into account. without a policy to pursue reducing its manufacture and use, we will continue to flood our environment with plastics that do not decompose. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. the plastic industry in europe generates an approximate turnover of eur 300 billion per year and employs 1.54 million people but the data related to its waste remain unconsolidated, varying from 25 million tonnes generated in 2008 according to the european commission, to 13 million tonnes in 2010 according to eea. without reliable and comparable data on production, collection, sorting, recycling, recovery and disposal of plastics, it is difficult to shape a targeted and effective policy, especially as regards action against illegal flows of waste. it is evident that the environmental impact of plastic is still underestimated. as part of the ongoing ‘fitness check’ on waste stream directives, this green paper offers a timely opportunity to aim at a cohesive and ambitious legislative harmonisation. the first step should be, therefore, the creation of specific eu plastic waste legislation, with related targets as well as the rigid implementation of current rules.

madam president, since the 1970s the european institutions have adopted numerous directives with the aim of creating a single market in public procurement. we are now pushing for further reforms, but i must warn that, despite the energy expended, the results have not been positive. the markets are still very fragmented, the transposition of these rules in the member states is irregular, so that the entry into force of a rule overlaps with its reform, creating a great deal of confusion, aggravated by the fact that the number of administrations, bodies and companies required to apply them is high. as will be seen, this has a very serious impact on a first-rate legal asset, namely legal certainty. i am also sorry that the criteria applied by the luxembourg court are not always reflected in the reforms of the directives and that the excellent historical tradition of the public service concession system, which comes from french law, has been largely neglected.
madam president, i have signed the amendment which seeks to preserve the capacity of public administrations to contract outside the scope of this directive in order to keep non-profit-making third sector entities on the front line of social benefits. it is not a whim; it recognises a historical reality, as these organisations were pioneers in the provision of this type of service and bring efficiency, quality, knowledge and involvement. in addition, they encourage solidarity volunteering and exercise a basic awareness-raising task to spread problems that need, in addition to assistance support, the encouragement of society. failure to include their content in the agreement puts this network of efficient, committed, highly specialised and proven professionals at risk, and will be a step backwards for which the users of the services will pay. this is the most effective way of organising and providing social assistance and it promotes positive values which are necessary for european society. i am therefore sorry that we have not been able to give you the answer you are expecting from us today.

in writing. − in favour. the legal basis is the following: article 186 in conjunction with point (v) of article 218(6)(a) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). proposed act: council decision to be adopted only with parliament’s consent. the purpose is to renew the agreement on cooperation in science and technology between the ec and russia. the agreement was signed in brussels on 16 november 2000 for an initial period ending on 31 december 2002 and to be renewed by common agreement between the parties for additional periods of five years. by its decision 2009/313/ec, the council concluded the renewal of the agreement for a further period of five years which expires on 20 february 2014. with the proposed decision, the council is called upon to approve, on behalf of the european union, the renewal of the agreement for an additional period of five years. the content of the renewed agreement will be identical to the content of the agreement. budgetary implications: the indicative budgetary implications are estimated at eur 550 000 in commitments for 2014-2019.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it seeks to improve the security specifications against counterfeiting, it gives the commission the power to withdraw the coins proposed by the various member states. this is a technical report which seeks not to introduce any significant change in the rates or characteristics of the different euro coins in circulation. it merely introduces the ability to revise these specifications for security reasons in the fight against counterfeiting and fraud. however, these measures introduced by the report go beyond the commission's powers by overriding the sovereignty of the member states in decisions concerning their currencies. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. council regulation (ec) no 975/98 on denominations and technical specifications of euro coins intended for circulation, which is adopted on the legal basis of article 128 of the tfeu (enabling the council to adopt on a proposal from the commission measures to harmonise the technical specifications of euro coins after consulting the european parliament and the european central bank (ecb)) has been substantially amended several times. the new regulation was to have superseded the various acts incorporated in it. in the framework of its opinion the ecb recommended introducing certain changes with regard to the technical specifications set out in the table contained in article 1 of regulation (ec) no 975/98 as well as in annex i to the draft codified text. since the proposed redrafting for that annex would imply certain substantive amendments, and would therefore go beyond straightforward codification, it was considered necessary to transform the codification of regulation (ec) no 975/98 into a recast in order to incorporate the necessary amendments. in brief, the proposed substantive amendment consists of a replacement of all existing values relating to the thickness of euro coins with new values.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it includes a proposal for the liberalization of trade with the countries of the association of southeast asian nations (asean). this agreement continues the usual line of the european union's foreign policy, allowing the boost to trade flows with the said regional bloc. the report lists social and environmental problems that are occurring in asian countries, but it is reluctant to point out the responsibility of trade relations with the eu. although the problems of these countries are mentioned if the trade prospects with the eu are maintained, the negative impact of this trade cannot disappear in the future of these relations. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − in favour. the report aims to raise appropriate attention to eu-asean relations, which have undeservingly often been upstaged by eu relations with china, japan and india. this situation prevails despite the fact that asean’s purchasing power and size of economy is already comparable to china’s and asean’s political star is on the rise. similarities between the eu and asean carry considerable potential for synergies and mutual learning processes. the report tries to explore how enhanced economic ties can be matched with a more adequate socio-political and institutional framework and relations. the report also presents ideas on how bilateral region-to-region relations could be lifted to a new level. the assessment and recommendations are presented in the context of the ongoing ambitious internal integration process within asean, the emerging political powers and the democratic challenges such as those confronted by the next asean chair burma/myanmar with its rapid transformation and evolution towards democracy.
in writing. − the so-called ‘tachograph regulation’ (ec) no 3821/85’ requires that all vehicles need tachographs installed, to which the ‘social regulation’ (ec) no 561/2006 applies. the commission published its amending proposal on 19 july 2011. in difficult and lengthy trilogue negotiations, the present compromise was agreed that we can accept. to illustrate, here is the compromise as well as the most radical counter-proposals: compromise: block exemption for lorries lighter than 7.5 tonnes operating within a radius of 100 km from the base of an undertaking not working in the transport business (non-professional drivers) and limited further exemptions. greens/efa: scope from 2.7 tonnes and 50 km radius with no further exemptions. parts of epp+ecr: from 10 tonnes, 200 km and many more exemptions.
mr president, i voted in favour of the three reports by mr juvin and mr tarabella, not forgetting mr panzeri, which are necessary to improve the current rules on public procurement, to put an end to the shortcomings of the procedure and to prevent undesirable situations. this directive has taken decisive steps in the right direction, such as reducing payment to suppliers, especially in times of crisis, bordering on economic suffocation, or the best offer, which does not have to be the lowest price, but an offer that respects the environment. it promotes corporate social responsibility by supporting social and environmental objectives, ensuring decent employment and social inclusion; improves access for smes and, above all, combats favouritism and nepotism; makes transparency and accountability the backbone of the whole process to avoid over-costing and abuse and, above all, makes the use of public money a responsible and effective use.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it is a commitment to privatisation and liberalisation of public sector concession award at european union level. the lack of common procurement rules in the member states has justified the european commission's proposal on this subject. the proposal was strongly opposed by almost all political groups; although the level was lowered, the criterion of introducing the principles of the common market in the management of public procurement was maintained. the final proposal includes many improvements, but europe needs an agenda to get public services back on track. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − in favour. the exclusion of water services is a major success not only for the greens but also for european democracy as it results both from our work within the parliament and from the mobilisation of civil society which led to the first ever successful european citizens’ initiative, showing that convergent actions inside and outside parliament can contribute to real policy changes. the main reasons for our opposition have now disappeared, in particular with the exclusion of water services and with a reasonable solution for public-public cooperation. although we are still not convinced that this directive brings any added value, we suggest acknowledging the success achieved and support the final text.
i would like to say, mr president, that i am one of the 40 signatories of the amendment to this report by mr tarabella, because we were missing an amendment so that all those social non-profit organizations which are involved in the disability sector - in particular in spain, in my region, the balearic islands, and also in other regions of spain - and which, with the efforts of parents, have set up day centres and residences for disabled people, can guarantee the quality of the service they provide. the permanence of the service is very important for all these groups: the psychologist, the pedagogue and the technical team must always be the same and their continuity must be guaranteed. to apply this directive to them too strictly and have them go through the competitive phase would be pointless and would destroy many years of very good work, of exemplary work by the entities in the balearic islands and the rest of spain.
i would like to congratulate mr president and say to all the citizens of europe that the right to take account of aesthetic and environmental quality in public and contracting has finally been recognised. we have seen many buildings destroyed, we have seen many works of art destroyed precisely because contracts have been made at the lowest price. this means that we have prevented skilled people, companies with the ability, with the technical knowledge, from destroying works of art. i understand that both cities and architecture require knowledge, an understanding of the work, and this is good news for europe's historical heritage. and so i think we should recommend that when countries transpose this directive they take into account that cultural heritage is a value that cannot be 'built' and that aesthetic and quality values are above money.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it represents a substantial improvement in the rules on public procurement, it retains clauses which can be avoided by economic operators through subcontracting. the report contains important developments in the field of public procurement; until now, award was based only on price and this report introduces that contracts should also be awarded according to the objectives of society, for example by giving priority to small and medium-sized enterprises, respect for labour rights in contracting companies, etc. however, price remains the main variable and the conditions set can be avoided through subcontracting. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in favour. the outcome is satisfactory because it brings more opportunities for sustainable procurement procedures: social and environmental award criteria, life-cycle cost instead of lowest price, possibility of using sustainability labels. in terms of simplifying the rules, the outcome could have been better, but we have ensured enough room for manoeuvre for public authorities and at least avoided the worst risks which would have made local public-public cooperation much more uncertain. in order to adopt the directives the text of the compromise must be unchanged; therefore we will table no amendment and we recommend voting in favour of both reports.
in writing. - i welcome the fact that parliament has adopted the new community rules on public procurement and concessions. this will bring transparency, security and flexibility to public procurement and also give public authorities more freedom to choose the best tender, not necessarily the lowest, but the most appropriate one taking into account the particularities of each concession. the new measures will make it easier for both bidders and contractors to reach joint solutions on tenders, ensure that citizens' money is allocated more efficiently and avoid abuse and discrimination in such tenders.
in writing. - i am in favour of the new regulatory package, but i warn that the results of so many reforms of the public procurement directives are not positive: markets remain fragmented, the transposition of these rules in the states is irregular, the entry into force of a rule overlaps with its reform, and all this creates a great deal of confusion which endangers legal certainty. i regret that some of the criteria applied by the luxembourg court of justice are not always reflected in the reform of the directives and i also regret that traditional french law has not been given the support it deserves in all these reforms.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it continues to introduce the neoliberal line pursued by the european commission, which seeks to promote the privatisation of essential public services. this report includes provisions allowing for the privatised management of public services which have proven to be more efficient under a public management system. the proposal contained in this report is an encouragement to privatisation, an impulse which the governments of the member states will take advantage of to propose the outsourcing of these fundamental services, namely water, energy, transport and postal services. without an explicit defence of the need for the public nature of these services, i cannot support this report. that is why i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. − in favour. the modernisation of the public procurement directives should strike a balance between simplification of the rules on the one hand and, on the other, sound, effective procedures related to innovative, sustainable award criteria, while also securing a higher rate of sme participation and making wider use of e-procurement. the aim should be to exploit the potential of public procurement to the full within the single market in order to foster sustainable growth, employment and social inclusion. given that public procurement makes up quite a substantial proportion of the economy (accounting for an estimated 19 % of eu gdp), the successful revision and enforcement of public procurement rules would do much to revitalise investment in the real economy and overcome europe’s economic crisis. parliament welcomes the commission proposals, which, in its view, put forward some interesting new principles and ideas. they need, however, to be improved in order to achieve the best possible result.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a strategy of privatising public services in all regions of the european union. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's energy sector is not left behind by the current crisis. it is a neo-colonial manoeuvre to impose conditions on european companies for access to public contracts in third countries, a blackmail manoeuvre using access to the common market as a weapon. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. − against. we tabled a rejection amendment: this regulation harmonises the rules regulating access to eu public procurement on the basis of the openness-by-default principle, thereby ruling out the possibility to intervene at local level on the basis of other principles and instruments. this underlying principle is not acceptable since it rules out the possibility to use public procurement for strategic purposes, besides purely offensive goals. by introducing this principle, the eu would, yet again, be the exception as compared to all other countries. moreover, the eur 5 million threshold poses problems with respect to smes: under the threshold it would not be possible to adopt any restriction whatsoever, but that is the relevant market for smes. it therefore appears that this is an instrument mostly at the service of the eu’s big industrial groups.
in writing. - i voted against this report because, because of the amendments proposed by the more conservative groups, it has become an instrument for solving the problems arising from the introduction of genetically modified organisms. if there is contamination of honey with pollen from gm crops, consumers should have the right to be informed of this type of contamination. with this report, pollen is now considered a natural component and therefore should not be included in the labelling, thus allowing this type of contamination with gm crops not to be labelled. the fact that it allows this pollution to spread and conceals the harmful effects of gmos is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − against. this vote is a sting for european beekeepers and consumers. the ecj ruled in 2011 that honey contaminated with genetically modified pollen would have to be labelled as such under eu legislation. in response, the commission presented a revision of eu legislation on honey, proposing that the presence of gm pollen in honey would not need to be indicated on the label, turning the ruling on its head. we regret the failure of a majority of meps to overturn this proposal. with eu countries importing honey from gm producing countries and two of the main eu honey-producing member states (spain and romania) having authorised the production of this gm maize, honey contaminated with gm pollen will increasingly be available on our shop shelves. honey containing gm pollen should be labelled as such, both to provide certainty for consumers and beekeepers. regrettably, a majority of meps were swayed by an intense lobbying campaign, led by honey importers. the vote is a slap in the face for european consumers and beekeepers, who have again and again spoken out in favour of transparent labelling rules.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european commission proposal and not in favour of the report of parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi), given that parliament's committee on agriculture and rural development was in favour of the commission proposal and that the vote of the envi committee had not been unanimous. i would have sought a consensus solution: to indicate the percentage of pollen contained in honey (if it has too much, it degrades its quality and is a consumer fraud). it is also essential to take measures to deal with the problem of coexistence of crops, and this requires compliance with the necessary identification of gm crops, which is not complied with in all member states.

mr president, commissioner, we are talking about respect for the fundamental right to free movement of persons, but it is impossible to take it seriously enough if we do not also talk about its context and background. and the context is that of a crisis such as the european union has never known, a crisis in which demagogy, populism and rabid euro-phobia are galloping on the backs of the suffering of the weakest, a crisis which affects all rights and freedoms, and of course affects the free movement of persons, which is subject to an unprecedented attack by irresponsible approaches. you have spoken of the abuses of the social benefits system, but also of the feeling of abuse, and we must also attack that feeling, that presumption of abuse which in many cases has no correspondence with reality, which is agitated by irresponsible and opportunistic speeches, as well as by media which lack the truth. the commission's proposal is to be accompanied by a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. and it must also be said that, in this context of crisis, the culture of hatred of the different and the other, the exploitation of scapegoats and a cruel and darwinian competition for scarce social resources have been unleashed, which has led many governments - including my own - to cut social benefits. last episode: the withdrawal of the health coverage card to those who leave for a few months three months the country and move to another in search of job opportunities. so it is a very serious situation and we have an opportunity to rescue europe, the best europe: the elections in may 2014. the european parliament has been a key player in the process of european integration, and it is the only institution in the world which has been able to do so.
mr president, the end of the moratoriums on free movement for bulgarian and romanian workers is another step in the construction of the european project and in the equalization of all community citizens. we cannot ask third countries for reciprocity and equal treatment if we are not the first to do so, and bulgaria and romania are rightly european and community. free movement is without doubt one of the great achievements of european citizenship. if capital, services, goods, goods and, of course, ideas circulate, how can it be that people do not move freely? we do not want such an important freedom to be violated, and that, mr president, is not incompatible with your defence. it is in no way compatible with that defence, nor with taking action against possible irregularities or abuses. we have worked hard to build what we are today and we cannot allow extremist and populist speeches to take shape and ignite national debates. the economic crisis we are going through cannot be a pretext for limiting rights, but must be an incentive to strengthen our economies and to face the challenges we have to face. the fact is that 14 million european citizens contribute in some way to the revenue of the community budgets of the 28 member states, and that is an irrefutable truth.
mr president, the maltese government's programme to bring in investment in exchange for citizenship is unacceptable. firstly, from the point of view of european security, it may open the door to the development of criminal activities such as money laundering. secondly, at community level it would mean access to european citizenship with rights and all that this entails, breaking the existing rules and breaking the trust between member states. it would also mean recognising that the right to citizenship is a commodity that can be bought and sold, and not a commodity that sustains the vitality of the union. no single state can invade the civil codes of the other 27 or the community law of all of them.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, commissioner de gucht is unfortunately not available for tonight’s joint debate on the future of two of our older free trade agreements – with mexico and chile. i am therefore pleased to represent the european commission. to start with mexico: the eu is the country’s second-largest export market after the us and its third-largest source of imports. the volume of trade flows between the eu and mexico has been continuously increasing in the past 10 years. recent reforms in mexico have created interesting perspectives for european companies in areas such as telecommunications and energy. the commission is firmly in favour of further developing trade and investment relations with mexico and is currently discussing with its mexican counterparts how to do so. there is now a consensus that the upgrade should cover the eu-mexico agreement as a whole and that an eu-mexico joint working group should be established to that effect. a first meeting of the subgroup on trade took place last october in brussels. the parties considered the potential for modernising the agreement in the area of tariffs, trade in services, intellectual property rights (including geographical indications), rules of origin/trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary measures and technical barriers to trade. a second meeting is foreseen in february in mexico city, where the parties will continue exploring the possibility for modernising the agreement. key areas for discussion will be government procurement, competition, investment protection, trade and investment in energy, trade defence instruments, dispute settlement and sustainable development. on the basis of these two meetings, a joint vision report will be produced to take stock of the situation. in the meantime, the commission has launched an evaluation of the effects of the trade pillar of the current agreement and the effects of a possible modernised agreement in a number of areas, including those mentioned in the honourable member’s question. the study will examine the social and economic impacts, both in mexico and in the eu, especially with respect to employment, wages, household income, labour standards, poverty reduction and human rights. it will also assess the environmental impact and, in particular, whether it has contributed to the greening of the economy. the study will also aim to quantify all remaining trade barriers, especially non-tariff ones, and assess the extent to which they could be addressed in a modernised agreement and the related social and environmental impacts. a decision by the commission to recommend opening negotiations will depend on the outcome of these exploratory talks with mexico, on the completeness and the level of ambition of the joint vision report, and on the results of the evaluation study. if a modernisation of the agreement is decided, the commission would be in favour of considering possible improvements to the financial services chapter and including a sustainable development chapter with clear legally binding commitments. turning to chile, the bilateral trade relationship is based on a highly successful agreement. since the entry into force of the trade part of the eu-chile association agreement on 1 february 2003, bilateral trade has grown by 128 %, reaching eur 18.1 billion in 2012. between 2004 and 2011, eu exports of services to chile increased by 128 %, while imports increased by 87 %. the eu also remains the leading source of foreign investment in chile, with 21.5 % of total foreign direct investment flows in 2012. based on this context, the commission believes that both parties have a strong interest to further develop trade relations. the trade pillar of the eu-chile association agreement includes a wide-ranging and novel set of provisions with respect to other trade agreements entered into separately by the parties at the time. for example, there is a high level of protection for names used in geographical indications, while provisions in the sanitary and phytosanitary field go beyond world trade organization rules. overall, it is a comprehensive agreement which has been implemented in a satisfactory manner to the mutual benefit of both parties. the independent ex-post evaluation of the trade pillar of the agreement, which was finalised in 2012, broadly validates this. however, the commission considers that the trade pillar of the agreement could be modernised in, for example, the areas of services, investment, rules of origin, trade facilitation, public procurement, technical barriers to trade, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, trade defence instruments and sustainable development. in this context, the commission welcomes the chilean non-paper entitled ‘a proposal for the modernisation of the eu-chile association agreement’ submitted during the eu-chile association committee meeting in october 2013. it contains an important trade component, which is still under assessment by the commission and the external action service. it is positive that chile signals its readiness to discuss areas not covered by the evolution clauses on agriculture and services. for its part, the commission would also be in favour of including a sustainable development chapter with clear legally binding commitments and of considering improvements to the financial services chapter, especially in the light of updated eu legislation on banking. at this stage of the process, further in-depth work between chile and the eu is necessary. we are still in a very preliminary phase and look forward to continuing work with chile, as well as to consulting member states, the european parliament and stakeholders to better identify specific areas of interest for the european union.
on behalf of the ppe group madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the first thing i would like to say is that these agreements are not free trade agreements: they are association agreements. these are the first agreements concluded by the european union with the specific character of being fourth generation agreements with third countries. the first generation was based on agro-industrial cooperation, the second on scientific and technological cooperation, the third on the democratic clause and the fourth on the progressive and reciprocal liberalisation of trade. these two agreements, for which i had the privilege of being rapporteur in the european parliament, are a success story. the commissioner reminded us of the spectacular increases that the agreement with chile produced - more than 230% in the first five years of its validity - and the agreements and the spectacular increases in the exchange of goods and services, and also in investment, in the case of mexico, which represent or have represented an accumulated stock of more than 80 billion euros. but as mr moreira reminded us, the circumstances of more than a decade ago, when these agreements were negotiated and concluded, have changed substantially. the world is a completely different place and today the european union is negotiating agreements with the united states, canada, japan, new vice-president of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, safety at sea and the protection of the environment are the two pillars of eu maritime safety legislation. after the erika and prestige accidents, the commission acted to abolish sub-standard shipping and make the prevention of environmental damage to marine waters a priority. liability for damage to the environment caused by shipping accidents has also been reinforced. eu member states are now required to impose penalties, including criminal sanctions, for ship-source pollution. it is also compulsory for any ship entering an eu port or flying a member state flag to have adequate insurance cover for maritime claims. the general environmental liability directive defines environmental damage as a ‘measurable adverse change’ or ‘impairment’ of biodiversity, land and water resources. that is independent of any traditional damage, such as damage to property, economic loss or personal injury. under the scope of the directive, the terms ‘environmental’ and ‘ecological’ damage are synonymous. there is no distinction made between environmental damage in general and ‘pure ecological damage’. allow me to elaborate on the international regime. the 1992 civil liability convention establishes the strict liability of the ship owner for any oil pollution damage, including damage to the environment. the liability limits were revised in 2003 and increased by 50 %, and special compensation funds were created to address pollution damage from oil spills. these funds compensate victims of oil pollution when the civil liability convention fails to cover their claims, in part or in full, and even when no liability for that damage arises under the convention. since 2008, compensation has included any measures for re-establishing a biological community in areas affected by an oil spill. the cost of post-spill studies is covered, and the funds can also facilitate the hiring of experts to advise on environmental recovery. the total amount available under this regime for compensating oil spill pollution damage is close to one billion euros. the international conventions prohibit any additional compensation claims being made using national or regional laws. once an accident falls under the scope of the civil liability convention and the funds conventions, compensation can only be claimed under the terms of these conventions. it cannot be combined with the environmental liability directive. the commission is now studying the effectiveness of the environmental liability directive and is focused on analysing data on accidents that have occurred over the last ten years in eu waters. it will report later in 2014. any further decision must be well-informed – either to work within the international regime and push for amendments within it, or to extend the scope of the environmental liability directive, abolishing the possibility of presenting claims under the international conventions.
on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, the truth is that the erika judgment is historic and we would like to see all the proposals we are putting forward concerning a european fund and the extension of environmental responsibility to the seas adopted. because three years after the sinking of the erika, in 2002, the prestige broke apart off the galician coast. i still remember that the present spanish prime minister spoke of plasticine hills, but the reality is that the accident involved 63 000 tonnes of plasticine, which caused the disaster of 2 900 kilometres of coastline, with 1 137 polluted beaches, 450 000 square metres of rock surface impregnated with plasticine - more than 500 tonnes in the deep - in a region also dedicated to fishing and seafood, the death of more than 200 000 birds, plus the illnesses of the volunteers, and, in total, 14 000 people affected. finally, ten years later, the prestige judgment - a judgment of hundreds of thousands of pages, delivered, it is true, in a court overtaken by circumstances and without the shipowner or the operator having been located, who have disappeared, as those responsible in the maritime sector usually do - has told them that there is no criminal or civil liability, that is to say, no one pays. the 14 000 people affected will not be held responsible for anything, since there will be no one left to pay; in other words, yes, spanish citizens will have to pay for all the disasters. that is why, mr kallas, i hope that we will recover the proposal from the european fund which the council rejected in 2000 and that we will be able to extend civil liability to maritime aspects as well. it is time that the sea ceased to be a no-man's land, where no one is responsible, where no one is responsible for such profound ecological, economic and social damage and that the council therefore took up its responsibility.

the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european digital single market is certainly one of the priorities we have set ourselves during this parliamentary term in order to complete the european single market. we could say that this legislature has been the one of europe's digital awakening. during these four and a half years we have succeeded in making the digital environment, for the first time in europe, an opportunity: an opportunity to complete the single market, an opportunity to get out of the crisis, adapting our trade, our economy, our companies and even our consumers to the new digital age, to regain competitiveness, which has undoubtedly been weighed down too much in recent years in europe compared to our main competitors, an opportunity to reactivate the labour market and, in this sense, an opportunity to bring young people - our young people - into the european labour market. in this legislature we have developed various initiatives which have made a great step towards the consolidation of a true digital single market in europe. the commission's internal market and consumer protection committee has made it a priority to make the digital single market a reality. in this regard, resolutions such as the one on the completion of the internal market for electronic commerce, adopted in september 2010, or on the completion of the digital single market, adopted in december 2012, set out the roadmap for its effective achievement. this roadmap was endorsed by this house in its resolution on completing the digital single market in july last year. during this time, we have held monthly meetings in the single market task force of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection since its creation in january 2011, and its conclusions have fed into the content of the abovementioned resolutions. but all that has been done so far would be incomplete if we did not complete the circle with the important report which we shall put to the vote tomorrow. the distribution and delivery of goods purchased online is the high point of the e-commerce chain. having an integrated single market for delivery services for the growth of e-commerce is not only fundamental, but is one of the pillars on which both consumers' and businesses' confidence in the digital single market must be built. it is vital to have pan-european delivery services that enable consumers and businesses, especially smes trading on the internet, to get goods sold or purchased to their destination quickly, safely and at affordable prices. in the report we call for a number of fundamental measures and reforms which need to be undertaken in the sector to improve the existing situation. i would like to thank the good cooperation i have had with the alternative rapporteurs and their excellent willingness and desire to reach compromise agreements on the various subjects, which has resulted in the unanimous approval of this report in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. i would just like to add, in conclusion, that i believe that the path we have travelled in this legislature should not end here. there are many areas where further progress will be essential and many challenges still to be addressed. the next commission and the next parliament must take stock of all that has been done in this legislature and bring it to the goal of completing the digital single market. it's a dream we all want to see fulfilled. let me conclude, as i have done so many times in this house, and i will not tire of repeating it, by saying that the way out of the crisis is also digital.

member of the commission. - mr president, i thank the members for the quality of this debate and for the unanimity which has been achieved as a result of the work you have carried out on the basis of the proposal i made to you and also on the basis of the work of the lithuanian presidency. ladies and gentlemen, i would like to remind you that i proposed this text on behalf of the european commission in july 2012, which means that you have done a lot of good work in a relatively short time - a year and a half - on a very sensitive subject. let me say a few words, mr president, in reply to some of the members, although i cannot mention all of them, but i would like to make a few points. i shall first answer mr vlasák on the costs of transposition for management companies. this is naturally a subject which we have examined during the discussions and in the impact study. we believe that these costs should not be too high. mr vlasák spoke about the dispute settlement procedures. these apply only to multi-territorial licences and therefore not to all companies. as far as complaint procedures are concerned, they are obviously part of the life and constraints of a well-organised and well-managed management company. mrs verheyen mentioned the compatibility or possible overlap of this directive with the services directive. i mean that the directive you are about to adopt is neutral - i insist - in relation to the services directive. the scope of the latter directive will therefore not change. mr masip hidalgo, all the member states are obviously obliged to implement this directive in a consistent and correct way. the commission shall provide for procedures to ensure that this implementation is properly carried out. we'll be watching it carefully. mrs ţicău was referring earlier to the work that has to be done by the member states: as we do with all texts, we will be in dialogue with the member states and with the collective management societies themselves to ensure that the implementation of the directive is monitored effectively and quickly. i would also like to say something about a sensitive subject for me: mrs castex, mrs thun und hohenstein and mrs kammerevert mentioned the fact that this consultation, which was scheduled for a very short period of two months, was proposed in only one language - english. i can understand that very well. i did it to myself for all the reasons you can imagine. we were prisoners, constrained by the timetable of a consultation we wanted to hold to show the willingness of the commission on a subject that must be listened to. therefore, we have indeed launched this consultation in one language. i would like to mention two points, not to excuse but simply to explain, beyond the question of the timetable. we, together with mrs kroes and mrs vassiliou, have decided to extend the deadline by one month because we understood that the fact that this consultation was open only in one language created constraints and created difficulties for all those who wished to reply or consult in another language. the second thing i want to say to those members who have legitimately spoken on this issue is that the replies are welcome and will be received in all the official languages. of course, the questions are in english, but we have given an extra month to understand and answer them, and, again, the answers can be given in all the official languages of the european union. i thank you for your understanding of this matter and i agree that ideally we should have done this consultation in several languages. i would also like to express my thanks on behalf of the european commission to those of you who have spoken in this debate and even before, to underline the quality of this text, which is the result of a long and intensive work by your rapporteur, the fictitious rapporteurs and the competent committees, on the basis of the text i had proposed to you. this text has been consolidated and improved in the council and especially here. this is a good encouragement, ladies and gentlemen, at a time when we have not exhausted the copyright issue, which i myself have said must be respected. authors must be paid fairly and promptly, but copyright must also - i repeat - live with its time, our time today, which is the time of the internet and the single market. in conclusion, i would like to thank marielle gallo personally and publicly for the work she has done with great skill, as you all have indicated. mrs gallo can be proud of her work and the method she has put in place - ms castex underlined this - which has been to work with everyone and listen to everyone, to finally reach a unanimous dynamic compromise on an extremely sensitive subject. it's a good example of this cooperative, inclusive, open, transparent approach that we need to use on this issue of copyright in particular and intellectual property in general. the commission will continue to apply this method, and i thank mrs marielle gallo very much for setting such a good example in this text.
mr barnier, the vice-president who is chairing this sitting is responsible for all things multilingual and i would point out to him that in that capacity i have been in contact with three or four senior officials in the field from different countries who have expressed to me their concern and protest at the fact that we are working in one language. it does not matter whether there is a one-month or six-month extension because what we are doing is putting some countries and some artists in a discriminatory situation compared to others. i would point out that this is an extremely worrying development in the commission's way of working, and i have no choice but to pass it on to you because i know that you are particularly sensitive to this matter and it is appropriate that this should be noted in today's agenda.
