the rapporteur. - mr. president, i won't go into too much detail. i would simply like, since we have not had the opportunity or the opportunity to have a small debate on something that may interest you, to thank everyone for the work on this report, and especially the members of the court of auditors, whom i personally represent in their newly re-elected president, mr caldeira, who has over the years developed a whole series of significant reforms to make the court of auditors a more refined, efficient and effective instrument, better responsive to the demands of its main clients, which are the commission and parliament, but above all to the objective of providing citizens with elements of confidence that at least someone is monitoring the implementation of the european budget. i think we have tried in this report to go further, to bring about, in a certain way, creative elements to solve or attempt to solve the devastating problem of the negative sdr exercise by improving the results of the court of auditors' audits by putting it in a framework closer to the requirements of the real debate on european policy. and i also believe that we have improved - as mr lehne's appointment today proves - the criteria for the appointment of candidates. i therefore ask you, if you can, to support amendment no 1, which is a resolution that improves even on what we had done in committee. sorry to interrupt.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to facilitate the inclusion of all the world's territories in the kimberley process certification system. this report is due to the fact that greenland is an autonomous territory, but does not have the status of a country, which prevents its accession to the kimberley process. this process is intended to control the origin of diamonds, to ensure that they are not diamonds from conflict zones and that the proceeds of trade in these raw materials cannot be used to finance conflicts in the territories where they are mined. the report proposes to regulate the trade regime for diamonds between greenland and the eu so that greenland can participate in the kimberley process. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - greens welcome the kimberley process as such, and we also welcome each country willing to join and effectively implement the rules. we also support the creative solution the commission has found linking greenland to the eu certification system through the association of greenland as an oct. the kimberley process certification scheme is a voluntary government-led initiative to stop the trade in rough diamonds that fuel conflict. it is guaranteed by government control of the implementation of the scheme, which has been operational since 2003. the kp has 54 members, representing 81 countries. participants in the kimberley process undertake to only import/export diamonds from other kimberley process participants. this is proven by an accompanying kimberley process certificate that is issued by a kp participant. the eu is a participant in the scheme. any rough diamond shipment imported/exported to any eu member state is sent to one of the six union authorities for verification, and only afterwards is sent back to its destination and introduced to free eu circulation. greenland is not part of the union territory, but it is included in the list of overseas countries and territories (oct) for its rich mining potential. since receiving autonomy over its mining sector in 2011, it wants to diversify its economy in this direction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to facilitate the inclusion of all the world's territories in the kimberley process certification system. this report is due to the fact that greenland is an autonomous territory, but does not have the status of a country, which prevents its accession to the kimberley process. this process is intended to control the origin of diamonds, to ensure that they are not diamonds from conflict zones and that the proceeds of trade in these raw materials cannot be used to finance conflicts in the territories where they are mined. this report proposes the participation of greenland in the aforementioned process once the trade regime for diamonds between greenland and the eu has been clarified. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to delay the implementation of the single euro payments area (sepa). the various payment systems in the european union were to migrate to this single payment area by 1 february, the date from which european banks could not make transfers or debit accounts in systems that did not meet the sepa conditions. most banks have not adapted to the system and without the extension of this deadline there would be problems in the financial system. the commission, in a last-minute proposal, has put forward this six-month delay in the implementation of sepa. in order to avoid the disruption that the move to sepa may cause, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. for reasons of urgency it is justified to proceed to the vote before the expiry of the deadline of eight weeks laid down in article 6 of protocol no 2 on the application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a boost to the international implementation of the 1977 torremolinos international convention for the safety of fishing vessels. the convention was never applied globally because not enough countries ratified it, but the torremolinos protocol of 1993 has been applied in the european union since 1997. the 2012 cape town agreement on the implementation of the protocol seeks to remove restrictions that have prevented the participation of countries with large fishing fleets in the protocol. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it seeks to extend the scope of these safety standards so that they improve the working conditions of fishermen in all regions of the world.
in writing. - in favour. the cape town agreement of 2012 on the implementation of the provisions of the torremolinos protocol of 1993 relating to the international convention for the safety of fishing vessels, 1977 was adopted in october 2012 during a diplomatic conference convened by the international maritime organization (imo). this agreement should enable the implementation of the torremolinos international convention for the safety of fishing vessels signed in 1977 and its protocol of 1993, which never entered into force as a result of an insufficient number of states ratifying the convention and its protocol. the torremolinos convention and its protocol of 1993 lay down safety standards, such as life-saving appliances, radio communication, fire protection, machinery and electrical installations, as well as specific requirements for seagoing fishing vessels of 24 metres in length and over.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains good descriptive information on the trends in the application of european union law in the member states, it does not sufficiently condemn the failures and inaction of both the member states and the european commission. the report shows a trend towards fewer infringement proceedings being brought against member states, but non-compliance has continued to increase. the implementation of eu law is essential in certain areas to oblige states to implement key legislation, and although this report notes the failures, it is not enough. i have therefore been unable to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. the lisbon treaty introduced a number of new legal bases intended to facilitate the implementation, application and enforcement of eu law. article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union defines the right of good administration as the right for every person to have his or her affairs handled impartially, fairly and within a reasonable time by the institutions. according to article 298 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), in carrying out their missions, the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union shall have the support of an open, efficient and independent european administration. according to the legal service of the european parliament, the eu pilot, an online platform used by the member states and the commission to clarify the factual and legal background to problems arising in relation to the application of eu law does not have any legal status and according to the framework agreement on relations between the european parliament and the european commission, the latter has to make available to parliament summary information concerning all infringement procedures from the letter of formal notice, including on a case-by-case basis, and may only refuse access to personal data in the eu pilot.
in writing. - abstention. immunity to be raised in a case of civil proceeding, which was brought with no justification after the criminal one based on the same facts.
in writing. - in favour. immunity should be waived as the case does not fall within the scope of ziobro’s political activities as an mep and instead concerns activities of a purely national nature.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it improves the living conditions of many european citizens who have migrated from one member state to another within the european union. the report deals with the simplification of the acceptance of certain official documents by the institutions of all the member states. until now, official translation and authentication of all official documents was required. this imposes huge costs on many citizens who must even return to their home countries just to be able to prove the veracity of an official public document in their home state. this report obliges the member states to accept certain official documents with lower accreditation requirements; that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - we cannot expect the free movement of persons and goods to be complete without establishing simple but wide-ranging bureaucratic mechanisms to facilitate the establishment of individuals and businesses in other member states. the european parliament has therefore adopted this proposal for a regulation, which lays down guidelines for validating the authenticity of public documents from another member state, which does not imply acceptance of their content. documents such as civil status or intellectual property rights, or certificates of disability or educational records will therefore be more easily recognised under this simplified system. in addition, the introduction of multilingual forms at eu level complements the previous rules perfectly. linguistic pluralism is a reality in the european union, and we must therefore include it in the legal framework.
in writing. - this regulation is a further step towards harmonising existing eu legislation with the globally harmonized system (ghs), a united nations system for the identification of hazardous chemicals which informs users of the associated risks by means of symbols and standard phrases appearing on packaging, labels and safety data sheets. the adoption of this regulation has led to the need for technical adaptation of the five directives (92/58/eec, 92/85/eec, 94/33/eec, 98/24/ec and 2004/37/ec) containing references to chemical classification and eu labelling legislation. it is also very positive that all the political groups have agreed to the compromise reached.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because i think it will help to manage dangerous chemical compounds more safely.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to amend the legislation in force at european union level to provide better protection for workers against the risks of the use of certain substances in workplaces. the report aims to amend the relevant directives to adapt the legislation to the globally harmonized system of classification and labelling of chemicals. this legislative implementation of the agreement does not imply any reduction in the scope of the current directives but rather an improvement in the implementation of the treaties and therefore in the safety conditions of european workers; that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. regulation (ec) no 1272/2008 of the european parliament and of the council on classification, labelling and packaging (clp) of substances and mixtures aligns the existing eu legislation to the ghs, which is a united nations system for identifying hazardous chemicals and informing users about the related hazards by means of standard symbols and phrases on packaging labels, and safety data sheets. following the adoption of this clp regulation, a need emerged to make technical changes to the five directives (92/58/eec, 92/85/eec, 94/33/ec, 98/24/ec and 2004/37/ec) containing references to eu chemical classification and labelling legislation. the alignment of the references and terminology of the five directives to correspond to that of clp regulation does not call for any changes to the scope or level of protection provided by these directives.
in the case of the european parliament, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rights of the citizens of the union are protected. this new standard should stimulate the development of online music services at european level. it also ensures better protection of artists' rights and speeds up the collection of their profits. this directive will enable users to access copyrighted content throughout europe. it's a clear sign that copyright can be easily adapted to the internet. copyright plays an essential role in the digital economy.
in writing. - the directive addresses the issue of collective rights management and how to facilitate the licensing of copyright and related rights in europe. parliament succeeded in improving the draft from the commission – which was already not bad in itself. among the improvements obtained which were important to us are: better transparency and control of management; annual individual statement on conflicts of interest by persons exercising the supervisory function and managers of cmos; better and more transparent management of the money, including of investment of rights revenue and the incomes arising from it; the possibility for authors to licence their work for non-commercial use; better distribution of amounts due.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a good organization of the rights and duties of collective management organisations for copyright at crossborder level within the european union. the report arises as a need to improve regulation in the area of online use of multi-territorial licences in the eu context. the rights of collective management organisations are more concisely defined, giving a greater role to their users and seeking to prevent excesses by such organisations. the report also stresses the need to take account of the union's cultural diversity in the development of cultural policies. it is because all these measures can give a boost to the music industry in the eu that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. article 167 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union requires the union to take cultural diversity into account in its action and to contribute to the flowering of the cultures of the member states, while respecting their national and regional diversity and at the same time bringing the common cultural heritage to the fore. collective management organisations play an important role in the promotion and preservation of cultural diversity, enabling rightholders to be remunerated for uses which they would not be in a position to control or enforce themselves, including in non-domestic markets. moreover, they play an important social and cultural role as promoters of the diversity of cultural expressions, by enabling the smallest and less popular repertoires to access the market.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it seeks to regulate the sanctions applicable to market manipulation operations, it constitutes the consolidation of a fanatical gamble to protect market mechanisms even though it has been shown that they are behind the cause of the economic crisis we are facing. i am against any kind of fraud, whatever the means by which it is perpetrated, but i think this report falls short and is also committed to ensuring the integrity of the eu's financial markets and to increasing investor protection. i believe that this type of fraud should be penalized, not to preserve the integrity of the sector and investors, but to prevent fraud by them. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. the market abuse directive (‘mad’) is concerned with criminal sanctions for ‘market abuse’ as defined in the regulation and the market abuse regulation (‘mar’) defines market abuse, provisions for detecting and preventing it and for setting administrative sanctions. the gravity of market abuse crimes merits the application, where appropriate, of criminal penalties for insider trading, market manipulation and improper disclosure of information. the introduction of a directive aimed at harmonising criminal sanctions regimes for market abuse across the eu is essential to ensure the effective implementation of eu financial services legislation. it also enlarged the scope in relation to the previous regime, to cover things like commodity derivatives and new trading venues added in the mifid directive and regulation, recently negotiated in trilogues. the regulation adds a significant innovation to the current market abuse framework by providing a detailed list of infringements that must be sanctioned, a detailed list of measures and sanctions that must at least be available to the competent authorities and criteria for the application of sanctions. the proposal for a regulation makes it clear that these sanctions must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

in writing. - in favour. it is not only that the european court of auditors, as an external auditor to the union’s institutions, may provide the legislators with a statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions in any given budgetary year, but also that the court is in a pre-eminent position to provide the legislator and the budgetary authority, especially parliament's budgetary control committee, with valuable opinions on results achieved by the union’s policies, in order to improve the performance and effectiveness of union-financed activities, identify economies of scale and scope, as well as spillover effects among the national policies of member states, and provide parliament with external assessments of the commission’s evaluation of public finances in the member states. the court should remain committed to independence, integrity, impartiality and professionalism, while building strong working relationships with its partners, particularly the european parliament and, more specifically, its committee on budgetary control, as well as the specialised committees, in the accountability process of the eu institutions.
in writing. - the role of the supreme audit institution of the european union must be established in a manner that is consistent with its role and its fundamental role in giving validity to the actual implementation of the union budget approved by the european parliament. beyond its relationship with other union institutions, such as the council, it has a direct commitment to european citizens as guarantor of public spending before them. the manner in which the new members of the court are appointed is therefore of fundamental importance. they must be the guarantors of the guiding principles of independence, integrity, impartiality and professionalism which they are expected to uphold and to which they must be subject as members of the court.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is another call to the member states to commit themselves to developing a clear definition of the principles of european law of subsidiarity and proportionality. this report reiterates the complaints made in previous years about the need to define these legal principles. the member states today often resort to a subjective interpretation of these principles in order to avoid competence and responsibility in certain policy areas. an appropriate negotiating process allowing for a single interpretation of these principles is not desirable, it is necessary in the interests of legal certainty at union level. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. - in favour. the unfair commercial practices directive 2005/29/ec aims to complete the internal market by removing barriers caused by differences between national laws on unfair commercial practices and ensuring a high level of consumer protection. it seeks to ensure that consumers are not misled or exposed to aggressive marketing and that any claim made by traders is clear, accurate and substantiated. this directive covers business-to-consumer (b2c) transactions, whether online or offline, involving goods and/or services. the purpose of this report was to respond to the commission communication assessing the application of this directive in the member states.
in writing. - the european parliament in plenary approved this report which calls on the commission to review the national implementation of the unfair commercial practices directive, the purpose of which is to ensure that consumers choose their shopping carts in full knowledge and without any abuse. there are disparities in implementation and transposition between member states, which jeopardises the effectiveness of the measure and compromises the entire single market by making transnational trade relations somewhat difficult. it is therefore necessary to remove this legal and operational uncertainty by ensuring the correct implementation of the directive, applying sanctioning measures where appropriate. these guarantees are not only for the benefit of consumers, who are the least protected since the rise of new technologies as a means of accessing trade, but also for the benefit of businesses, since all will be able to play by the same rules and smaller ones will be able to survive more easily in the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a commitment to the european union to begin to assess rigorously the differences between the legislative systems of the member states. the report calls on member states to thoroughly review the justice scoreboard for the last financial year 2013, with a view to putting in place measures to promote mutual understanding and cooperation between the different judicial systems of the member states. the report is intended to make progress towards a european union which makes it easier for citizens to use the justice systems in a country other than their own. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. this own-initiative report is a response to the commission’s 2013 eu justice scoreboard. it should be noted that this report focuses solely on civil, commercial and administrative law, where the judicial system has a particular importance for economic recovery. improving the quality, independence and effectiveness of judicial systems is a major goal of public policy at eu level and at national level. national justice systems play a key role in restoring confidence and delivering a return to growth. in the annual growth survey 2013 (ags), the commission underlined the importance of improving the quality, independence and effectiveness of national judicial systems, and of ensuring that claims can be settled within a reasonable time while promoting the use of alternative dispute resolution mechanisms. this should reduce costs for businesses and increase the member states’ attractiveness to foreign investors. the ags showed the need for a thorough evaluation and systematic review of the functioning of judicial systems in all member states, fully respecting the different national legal traditions.

in writing. - the report is very positive in that it captures the paradigm shift in the way energy is produced and consumed in the eu regions. it also highlights the possibility of making geographical (or territorial) changes to the energy grid and of promoting smart grids in disadvantaged regions such as islands, calling on member states and regions to invest in smart local grids through the use of the european structural and investment funds. as the rapporteur rightly says, the deployment of smart grids requires a stable, long-term policy framework so that their full potential can be exploited.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although i agree with much of what has been said about the search for a new model of energy production and distribution, it allows for the financing of private enterprises through the european union's structural funds. the report contains many bets on the use of smart grids in the energy systems supplying the member states of the union. these networks can allow for a reduction in needs by using systems in which energy consumers are, in part, their own producers. this reduces transport, which is one of the most energy-wasting phases in current systems. however, allowing private companies access to the structural funds may lead to multinational companies in the sector being able to monopolise these funds, which should be used for the needs of citizens. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. in times of increasing energy prices, climate change and socio-economic challenges, all regions in the eu will have to find ways of providing a stable and secure energy supply, which is affordable for all citizens, while respecting environmental and sustainability criteria. looking at different smart energy systems and smart grid initiatives we can see that there are already many solutions on the ground. some regions have transformed themselves from energy buyers to energy suppliers with a strong emphasis on renewable energies, thus providing a model of sustainable energy production that allows stabilising energy prices and making a profit at the same time. such examples include the region of burgenland in austria. güssing within burgenland was a previously poor and peripheral region which has transformed itself into a model of sustainability, generating all of its energy needs from renewable energy sources. islands, such as madeira in portugal, el hierro in spain, samsø in denmark, ikaria in greece, are also turning around a high percentage of energy needs, previously coming from fossil fuels, to now producing these same needs from renewable energy sources combined with smart infrastructure and storage choices.

in writing. - in favour. the parcel delivery market has grown rapidly as a result of increasing uptake of ecommerce. it is estimated that parcel delivery represents 20-40% of the total volume of delivery. cross-border delivery is considered an obstacle by 57% of retailers whilst 46.7% of consumers state that they are concerned about delivery in cross-border transactions. given the ecommerce is seen as the future of the internal market, end-to-end delivery infrastructure is fundamental and key to building consumer trust the commission considers the following three areas to be instrumental in creating an integrated eu parcel delivery market: (1) convenience, including innovative solutions for final-mile delivery, e.g. lockers, drop-off points in local shops, and tracking, also taking into account the universal service obligation; (2) cost, as consumers believe costs are too high yet operators say their margins are already tight; (3) interoperability and transparency along the delivery chain. this report is in response to a commission green paper launching a consultation on this matter.
in writing. - if the single market aims at removing barriers between trading partners, the emergence of the internet does nothing but facilitate this integration. the opportunities offered by the technological revolution in terms of exchange are amazing, allowing all businesses, in particular smes, to reduce transaction costs and facilitate the mobility of goods. however, its full potential is not exploited as consumers, losing direct contact with the seller, fear non-compliance and deception, and confidence in the method is not optimal. the report adopted today by the members of the european parliament therefore calls for the creation of a secure, transparent and reliable framework for online sales, with guarantees and trustworthy seals, flexible collection points and parcel tracking systems, which will enable both buyers and sellers to benefit from a favourable legal environment.

us soon - and i would like to express on his behalf my gratitude to the alternative rapporteurs, to the commission and to the greek presidency, and in general to all those with whom he has worked on his report up to now. the banking union is a historic project of the european union of enormous scale, an unprecedented milestone in the european financial sphere. we need it to sustain the single currency and to take advantage of the benefits of a common market, to respond to the crisis and to better integrate our increasingly interdependent economy in a globalising world; in the short term it is indispensable to break the vicious circle between bank debt and public debt, to have a single regulation to make financial reform more effective, to ensure faster debt reduction and credit recovery and to protect taxpayers. the single resolution mechanism is one of the three pillars of the banking union, alongside the single supervisory mechanism and the deposit guarantee scheme. the establishment of a single resolution mechanism is considered a priority as it should be carried out in parallel with the establishment of the single supervisor that we have agreed. the european parliament, as a co-legislator, is committed to achieving the banking union and fully assumes its responsibilities. in 2010, a large majority in parliament approved an own-initiative report by the current rapporteur, elisa ferreira, calling on the commission to submit legislative proposals for the establishment of a single rulebook, a single supervisor with intrusive powers and a common fund to facilitate the orderly resolution of financial institutions, funded by credit institutions according to their risk profile, which would allow the costs to be passed on to shareholders and creditors, protecting taxpayers and even depositors from the consequences of this process. since then, the european parliament has contributed to the building of the banking union, has established a single supervisory mechanism which will soon be fully operational, is looking forward to a future initiative on deposit guarantee and has fully committed itself to the union having a single resolution mechanism including a single fund before the end of its present mandate. there are important reasons for doing so. the first is that there is a window of opportunity: a political momentum that cannot be squandered. there is a large majority in the house that supports it and wants to avoid risks to a future that, by definition, is always uncertain. the single supervisory system we have established is incompatible if, after the european central bank has declared an institution to be unviable, it enters into a confusing and unclear system of national resolution structures. furthermore, a key principle of the financial reform is the assumption of losses primarily by shareholders and creditors: bail-in. this principle is agreed in the bank recovery and resolution directive, but its establishment is inconceivable without a single supervisory mechanism. the basic idea is that banks support banks. that is why we need an efficient and rapid european authority. if a bank can't be resolved in a weekend to avoid a withdrawal of funds, the system is too complicated. the slower and more inefficient, the more expensive it is in the end. we need a single resolution fund funded by industry and a single resolution mechanism, not a multiple resolution mechanism. instead, we want a transition to a single resolution fund, but not a sharing of funds. will the member states continue to respond at least for another ten years? we believe that the single fund should be operational from the outset, otherwise there will be more costs for the member states. and, furthermore, we want to ensure that similar banks with similar problems are treated in a similar way. if the banking resolution does not work, financial stability could well be jeopardised, with a loss of confidence in the european union, and of course the credibility of the european central bank. nobody said this was going to be an easy project. the european parliament assumes its responsibility as a co-legislator and expresses its willingness to negotiate in good faith with the council on the objectives set. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. but the european parliament will not support a bad solution. there are no technical reasons for not reaching a compromise if there is genuine political will to do so. that is why parliament is prepared to reach it and we say that this is a dance. and for a tango it always takes two to dance.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am grateful for the opportunity to discuss in the house our trade relations and their impact on our internal market. from an agri-food point of view, the european union is undoubtedly one of the most important players in international trade, as an exporter but above all as an importer. since the signing of the warsaw declaration on food trade in october 2011, all european institutions have a duty to ensure that european citizens, as consumers, enjoy the highest standards of quality in food and food products produced in the european union, and also in those imported. we have enough tools for this, which should be used and, if necessary, improved, but never ignored or eliminated. the european commission is the gatekeeper of our common home, which must assure all europeans that what enters our borders will never cause us a food or plant health problem. it is therefore necessary to respect scrupulously the trade agreements signed by both the european union and the member states: to respect them and to enforce their respect. in the recent reform of the common agricultural policy we have introduced an important clause: reciprocity with third countries. only by taking account of sustained and sustainable developments, in compliance with the agreements signed and the obligations required, will it be possible to meet our food needs with justice, equity and peace of mind for european consumers.

and the protection perspective, the commission brought forward a proposal for a directive regulating the entry, stay and rights of seasonal workers as long ago as 2010. it has been a long journey since then, and i want to thank the rapporteur, claude moraes, and co-rapporteurs sergio gaetano cofferati and alejandro cercas, for their work, as well as the eight council presidencies who have worked on this – from the belgians through to the current greek presidency. this directive will establish a fast-track procedure for the admission of non-eu seasonal workers. seasonal employment will be defined in the same way throughout the eu: it will concern activities that depend on the passage of the seasons and there will be a maximum time of stay. seasonal workers will now enjoy equal treatment with nationals in the host member states in terms of social security, employment and working conditions. member states are, of course, competent to determine on economic grounds how many migrants they admit, and they are also allowed to carry out labour market tests. this will ensure that third-country migrants fill real gaps in the labour market that cannot be filled by eu citizens and migrants who already reside legally in europe. we consider this to be a balanced compromise. we need harmonisation, and it would not have made any sense for all the member states to retain parallel schemes for seasonal employment. seasonal workers coming for periods of less than three months will also be covered by the directive and will have the same rights as seasonal workers staying a bit longer. the directive is also a tool for circular migration. it addresses the case of those migrants who come to the eu for a short period and then return to their country of origin at the end of the contract. facilitation to permit the re-entry of bona fide migrants is a good thing: we are helping to establish a good relationship between those who come to work and the employers who then know that they can trust these people. member state authorities can check that seasonal workers have access to appropriate accommodation. this is necessary, as we saw in rosarno, to prevent exploitation. in the end, what we have here is a good text, which was massively supported by the relevant committees in this house. it will protect vulnerable migrants from exploitation; it will increase transparency in sectors where irregular migration and exploitation have traditionally been too frequent; and it will clarify the procedures for employers who need workers during their busy seasons. a further important dimension is the fact that we are opening new avenues of legal migration to the eu. we know that it is very difficult to reach the eu in a legal way. with this directive, we are setting a good example of a legal channel, giving migrants an opportunity to seek and obtain work in a lawful manner. we can be proud of the work we have done. once again, i want to thank everybody involved.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is a very good one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr claude moraes, for his very good report. thank you all and thanks to that today we have a beautiful piece of legislation in a legislature in which, unfortunately, there has not been much legislation for workers. but there is one for this group of workers, who are probably the most in need of protection, the most vulnerable; we are seeing every day that they are more vulnerable and more prone to abuse. that is why the fact that we have achieved equal treatment in terms of working conditions and that they are now guaranteed freedom of association, trade union membership, the right to strike, all payments, access to social security, recognition of diplomas and the payment of their pensions is a huge advantage, which is linked to advantages in terms of housing; in short, to treat them with dignity, as human beings. i think we can be proud. i think the dignity with which these people are going to be treated dignifies us as well. i believe that a society measures its dignity by the dignity with which it treats the weakest and most vulnerable and these workers in agriculture and the tourist industry were being subjected on many occasions to ill-treatment and abuse. that is why, ladies and gentlemen, i think this is a great moment, because we are going to ensure that these workers have equal rights and also because in this way we will put a stop to the xenophobic and racist sentiments that arise when workers arrive with worse working and living conditions. because, in the end, equal treatment is the cornerstone of a migration policy that is not only fair but also intelligent, one that leads to dignified treatment and one that also leads to putting a stop to xenophobia and racism. let me quote a phrase that i like very much, because as kapuściński said, we are all in the same boat and all the inhabitants of our planet are each other for each other. with that sense of brotherhood and with that sense of dignity, the european union today is giving a lesson to the world and hopefully other pieces will follow that we need so that migration, instead of being a problem for many people, is a solution for all.
mr president, with the adoption of this directive we are going to solve issues which are closely linked to irregular migration, the fight against organised crime, the fraudulent labour market and the underground economy. it was necessary to create a legal framework to provide cover and protection for seasonal workers to prevent them from being treated as second-class workers. trafficking for the purpose of labour exploitation is a growing reality in most developed countries, which has become extraordinarily acute due to the economic crisis. the european union has a duty to ensure that the rights of the child are respected and that the rights of the child are protected. this directive is part of the 2005 legal migration policy plan and contributes to the effective management of migratory flows of a specific category such as temporary seasonal migration, and ensures decent living and working conditions for them, which will protect them from abuse. in addition, the possibility is given for unions and non-governmental organizations to file complaints on behalf of victims who are afraid to do so. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal, mrs malmström, and i also warmly congratulate claude moraes and my compatriot alejandro cercas and all the alternative rapporteurs on having achieved a virtually unanimous agreement. in doing so, you have contributed - and we will contribute - to protecting the most vulnerable migrants and ensuring that they are treated equally in the european labour market.
mr president, the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, which i have the honour of chairing, has cooperated with the committee on employment and social affairs, pursuant to rule 50, to bring this directive forward, which not only fulfils an objective proclaimed in the lisbon treaty, but something more important: it gives a chance to legal immigration, establishing equal treatment and improving the working conditions of at least one million seasonal workers, who are characterized by the precariousness and the temporary nature of their jobs, but above all by the low level of qualification required, usually due to their low pay and their social vulnerability. and so it is an affirmation of equal treatment which is absolutely necessary. and i believe that, in view of the development of what will come after the stockholm programme, the future ambitions with which we will have to work in the next legislature, the great challenge is to give a real chance to legal immigration, which is the best way to combat irregular immigration and, above all, the inhumane exploitation of workers and to restore dignity to work, which has been badly damaged in this crisis. why would you do that? this crisis management has been characterised by a biased and negative view of immigration as a threat to internal security. and it's not that. we are told that it is demographic reasons, because europe is ageing. they tell us that for economic reasons, because we need them. but above all, moral reasons, to live up to the values which the european union claims to proclaim once and for all.

in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report, although i agree with much of what is said in it, because i believe that no migrant can be considered illegal. the universal declaration of human rights recognizes the right to migrate for all people and this report continues to criminalize people who migrate in search of a better future. this report contains a large number of points which seek to improve the protection of the rights of undocumented migrant women in the member states, which is certainly a fundamental task and one which i fully share. however, this drive to improve the situation of migrant women cannot be at the expense of recognising the criminalisation of migrant people. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour, despite the fact that we lost some very good parts of the text we wanted in. as usual, the situation of undocumented migrant women is direr than that of men. they face a double discrimination due to their gender and legal status (or even a triple discrimination if one counts race). migrant women are more vulnerable to physical abuse in general, but undocumented ones are even more so because their legal status puts them in such a position where they cannot reach to the police or hospitals or shelters for help and their abuser knows this and exploits this situation. for example, there have been cases where unscrupulous landlords have exploited this vulnerability of undocumented migrant women and have physically and sexually abused them in exchange for providing them with a place to live. undocumented migrant women who find themselves in an abusive situation cannot even readily access women’s shelters. most state-run women’s shelters require some form of identification in order to receive the person, so the victims are left with the awful choice between remaining in the abusive situation or becoming homeless.
in writing. - a sensitive issue such as illegal or legal immigration cannot be left out of the interests of this parliament, especially if we understand the direct exponential relationship when we refer to the fact that undocumented immigrants are in this case women, which means that they are also a more vulnerable 'target' in the face of discrimination and the possibility of falling into the hands of criminal networks of human exploitation. the work must clearly be joint between member states and organisations directly linked to so-called 'civil society', while safeguarding the applicable union directives in this case. protection must be promoted so that these women not only have an adequate legal framework but also protection against possible abuse.
in writing. - i voted against this report because, although i share many of the points in it which improve the working conditions and rights of migrant seasonal workers in europe, this report is part of the basis for the criminalisation of migration. the report is presented as a great act of charity towards seasonal workers, but it is based on the view that migrants are labour at the service of agriculture, so that when they stop working in the areas of europe with the highest unemployment, where the majority of these workers reside, they will no longer have these rights. it is because of this underlying criminalization of migrants and because of the view that they are instruments at the mercy of the market needs that i have voted against this report.
in writing. - in favour. the 2005 commission communication on ‘a policy plan on legal migration’ provided for a proposal for a directive on the conditions of entry and residence of seasonal workers, considering that ‘seasonal workers are regularly needed in certain sectors, where many immigrants work illegally under precarious conditions’. the commission published its proposal in july 2010 in a package together with the proposal on intra-corporate transfers. the need for seasonal workers from outside the eu is a common phenomenon in most member states, and a framework at eu level for the management of this migration could provide real added value. in this respect, it is also noted that providing legal routes for migration can play an important role in reducing irregular migration and the exploitation that often accompanies it. it is also vital that this directive pay close attention to the need for equal treatment in the eu labour market, to ensure that pay and working conditions are not undermined. the rapporteur therefore welcomes this proposal in general, while noting that some areas need to be significantly strengthened.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the rapporteur's report calling for the repeal of regulation (ec) no 827/2004 prohibiting the import of products derived from bigeye tuna from bolivia, cambodia, georgia, equatorial guinea and sierra leone. the regulation dates back to the 1990s, when the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) was at the forefront of the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing, especially against those countries suspected of not respecting international rules and standards. much progress has been made in combating illegal fishing, but bluefin and bigeye tuna remain valuable species for which much remains to be done. i therefore agree with the adoption of this report today.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it establishes the possibility of implementing in the european union restrictive trade measures of a non-discriminatory nature against countries fishing for tuna and similar species, thus restricting the effectiveness of the iccat. there are several countries which do not properly apply international agreements concerning tuna fishing and therefore this report proposes to limit imports of atlantic bigeye tuna until the international agreements protecting these species are put into effect. this is a necessary trade sanction so that countries which do not comply with these international agreements will see that such non-compliance has serious trade consequences. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. the proposal from the commission concerns the repeal of regulation 827/2004, which prohibited the importation of bigeye tuna products from bolivia, cambodia, equatorial guinea, georgia and sierra leone. that regulation has its origins in the 1990s, in the glory days when iccat was at the forefront of the fight against iuu fishing, even before it was commonly referred to as iuu fishing. at the time, iccat was pioneering the use of innovative tools and was the first to impose import bans on countries that were suspected of allowing vessels flying their flag to disregard international rules and norms. it was also the first, or at least among the first, to establish blacklists of vessels that had been observed fishing illegally or extra-legally. this chapter of iccat’s history deserves a serious analysis, for it forms a critical part of the international campaign against iuu fishing, but that is beyond the scope of this simple report. initially, iccat took action against non-contracting parties, adopting resolutions that led to a number of import bans for various products (bluefin tuna, bigeye tuna, swordfish). then, confronted with accusations of bias for only acting against non-contracting parties, it began to act against contracting parties as well.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents an agreement which can be beneficial for both parties involved, while at the same time proposing an environmentally friendly and sustainable exploitation of the fishery resources present on the gabonese coast. the agreement will allow 35 european tuna vessels to fish in gabonese waters in return for fair compensation which has been accepted by both parties to the protocol. the protocol also provides for the development of tuna processing industries in gabon, so that jobs are created in the local economy and that this activity has a positive impact beyond the consideration. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. on the basis of the powers conferred on it by the council, the european commission has conducted negotiations with the gabonese republic with a view to renewing the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the gabonese republic. the previous protocol was in force between 3 december 2005 and 2 december 2011. after two rounds of negotiations, two issues remained to be settled. the first concerned the conditions governing suspension of the application of the protocol, at the initiative of one of the parties. the second related to the conditions governing the payment intended for sectoral support. the non-renewal of the protocol meant that eu fishing vessels were forced to cease fishing activities after 2 december 2011, since the ‘exclusivity clause’ provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement (fpa) remained in force. the protocol covered 40 vessels (24 purse seiners and 16 longliners). the member states affected were france, portugal and spain.
in writing. - i want to express my support for the ratification of the eu-gabon fisheries protocol, which has been provisionally applied since july 2013. this protocol means that the european fleet will return for three years to the most important fishing ground for the tuna fleet in the atlantic ocean off africa. after two years of absence following the breakdown of negotiations in 2011 due to differences over the human rights clause, the current protocol allows 27 purse seiners and 8 european longliners to fish. the fishing opportunities for surface longliners are not renewed, but the presence of tuna seiners, which are more selective, is foreseen for the first time. in the case of spain, a total of 22 tuna vessels (15 freezer vessels and 7 reelers) will benefit. the european financial contribution amounts to eur 1 350 000, of which eur 900 000 is linked to the 20 000 reference tonnes of access rights and eur 450 000 is to support the development of the gabonese fisheries sector. in addition, each shipowner shall pay a fee of eur 55 per tonne caught in the first year and eur 65 per tonne from the second year onwards. a national fee of eur 13 750 per year shall also be charged.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it presents a proposal for a decision which focuses on the most important social and environmental aspects of the island of greenland's relationship with the rest of the european union. greenland is now an overseas territory, governed by council decision 2006/526/ec which expired on 31 december 2006. this new proposal sets the framework for relations during the 2014-2020 period, and these relations now focus on aspects of civil society participation, educational and social programmes, etc., beyond the mere interest in the island's natural resources and emphasizing the protection of its delicate environment. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. greenland is one of 26 overseas countries and territories covered by part iv of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and listed in annex ii to the treaty. greenland is the largest island on the planet, but 81% of its surface is covered by ice. it has a population of 57 000 and its gdp is almost usd 36 000 per capita. the economy of this territory is principally controlled by the public sector and largely dependent on fishing, which accounts for 80% of its exports. greenland has a relatively high level of human development, but this is mainly due to financial support from denmark. furthermore, its population suffers from generally inadequate levels of education and professional training; there is not enough educational and professional guidance for young people and a high percentage fail to complete their schooling.

in writing. - in favour. unlike weapons of mass destruction and land mines, trade in conventional weapons has not been subject to any legally-binding global instruments. the arms trade treaty is intended to close this gap. after long negotiations, the treaty was adopted on 2 april 2013 through a resolution of the united nations general assembly. three states voted against the treaty (north korea, iran and syria) and 22 abstained (including china, india and russia, which could result in slow ratification and possibly incomplete implementation in these countries). the arms trade treaty establishes a common international standard for the regulation of international trade in conventional weapons and, to some extent, on ammunition, parts and components. it also aims to prevent and eradicate the illicit trade in these weapons.

in writing. - this proposal for a directive establishes that economic operators should be responsible for the conformity of lifts and safety components for lifts, according to their respective roles in the supply chain, in order to ensure a high level of protection of public interests such as health, safety and consumer protection, including a high level of protection of vulnerable consumers in cases where lifts are intended for the transport of persons, and fair competition on the union market. it is interesting to note how the european parliament puts the emphasis not only on economic operators but also on consumers/users of lifts. the contribution of parliament is also of vital importance as regards persons with disabilities, as it provides that the harmonised standards relevant to this directive should also take full account of the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, signed by the european union on 23 december 2010.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because it improves the safety and labelling requirements for lifts and safety components for lifts which are marketed in the various member states of the european union. this report addresses an objective need arising from the implementation of the common market: it is necessary to regulate both the safety conditions and the labelling requirements for products which may pose risks. the diversity of regulations may present certain risks for european consumers. the report deals in particular with the safety and adaptation of such products for disabled people. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - in favour. this report brings modifications to a proposal of the european commission recasting directive 95/16/ec on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to lifts. it was presented in november 2011 in the framework of the implementation of the new legislative framework (nlf) adopted in 2008 as ‘the goods package’ covering the complementary instruments, decision 768/2008 on a common framework for the marketing of products, and repealing council decision 93/465/eec and regulation 765/2008 setting out the requirements for accreditation and market surveillance relating to the marketing of products and repealing regulation (eec) no 339/93. the present proposal is part of a package aligning nine product directives to the nlf.
in writing. - in line with the new product regulatory framework (nrf), the directive 2009/105/ec on the manufacture and placing on the market of simple pressure vessels was discussed. the safety requirements discussed concern in particular materials, design standards, manufacturing procedures and the placing of products in service. their use must not jeopardise safety at any stage of the product's life cycle and in particular the risks of leakage and explosion must be preserved.

in writing. - the proposal for a new regulation deserves a very positive assessment as it aims to improve the clarification of the fundamental principles and the implicit rights of passengers which have given rise to many controversies between airlines and passengers in the past, as well as to improve and coordinate better the enforcement policies carried out at national level. the existing legislation in this area is incomplete and there is inconsistent application of the existing regulation by both carriers and national authorities, which causes confusion for passengers and industry. the main issues i would like to highlight are the definition of 'extraordinary circumstances', the right to compensation in case of delay, the right to change of route, the right to attention, missed connecting flights, rescheduling, delays on the runway, the partial ban on the 'no-show policy' and the right to information.
in writing. - in favour. the aviation industry has undergone significant changes in recent years, which are associated with an increase in the number of passengers and flights in the liberalised european market. however, this generally positive development has been accompanied, in a way, by the application of unfair practices and a reduction in the quality of services, with negative consequences for travellers. in addition, since the entry into force of the regulation in 2004, problems can be observed with respect to varied interpretations resulting from grey zones and gaps in the existing regulation, non-uniform enforcement across member states, and the difficulty experienced by passengers in enforcing their rights when air carriers are in breach of the legislation. parliament has already expressed its opinions on several of these points in the context of its resolutions adopted in 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to promote an improvement in the regulation of insolvency proceedings throughout the european union. the differences between the different laws of the member states open up a space for competitive advantages or disadvantages between companies from different countries of the union, as well as the possibility of fraud in multinational companies that can take advantage of the different laws of the member states. in this context, relative harmonization is both necessary and desirable in view of the implementation of the common market and greater economic integration in the eu. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - in favour. the commission’s proposal is an important initiative. parliament asked for in its report with recommendations to the commission on insolvency proceedings in the context of eu company law (2011/2006(ini)), adopted in plenary in october 2011. parliament’s observation in the report, namely that ‘there are certain areas of insolvency law where harmonisation is worthwhile and achievable’, is still valid today. it cannot be neglected that ‘disparities between national insolvency laws create competitive advantages or disadvantages and difficulties for companies with cross-border activities which could become obstacles to a successful restructuring of insolvent companies’.
in writing. - it is precisely in these times of economic crisis that the cases in which the competent judicial body can exercise its functions must be specially regulated in order to be able to carry out the corresponding procedures on this fact, whether it concerns a natural or legal person, an individual or a company. the aim of the regulation is also to resolve possible questions of jurisdiction which might arise in the application of the regulatory framework which the european union had already defined at the time, precisely in order to harmonise the arrangements relating to insolvency proceedings, especially between legal entities in different countries of the union. the regulation of the corresponding procedures, by means of the time limits set, will enhance the guarantee necessary for the correct application of the rule.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. - mr president, the last intervention in particular allows me to follow this logic in reacting to this very rich debate. i have six points to share with you. the first point is an assessment. any good policy is a good policy only if it is based on good assessment and if the lessons learned are taken into account. a reality check only works if you are ready to accept that there are other things that you could do better. i could offer you my own personal assessment. we have been focusing on benchmarks with ukraine, but that leaves no time and space for preparing for the implementation of an association agreement. those eleven benchmarks for ukraine to deliver on to create the conditions for signing the association agreement are also preconditions for the european union. many people are saying that ukraine made tremendous progress in 2013, working on those benchmarks. but working on the conditions to sign the association agreement and trying to build a consensus in this house and in the council did not provide us with enough space to prepare for the implementation of the association agreement and particularly the dcfta. if we had the time, there would be less space for so many misinterpretations of what the association agreement is about – or rather what it is not about. the second point concerns russia: our eastern european policy and the consensus there, as well as on the border between ukraine and russia and on the borders of our partners and russia. it was clear that the last summit between the european union and russia – and we will have a separate point to discuss this – made a step towards this, but we need dialogue with russia. our policy vis-à-vis our neighbours should also be a policy vis-à-vis the neighbours of our neighbours. the third point is that, if we were serious about reforming that part of europe, have we also been serious about choosing the most powerful instrument we have for the transformation of reforms? why did we win the nobel peace prize – for the association agreement? no. it was for enlargement and for breaking down the walls. the second point: plan. the only point which could work is the plan which the ukrainians might come up with through dialogue. no plan in brussels or moscow would succeed. the next point concerns strategy. our strategy – and we have a strategy – is not centred around sanctions. it is centred around engagement: engagement based on our values and principles. it has three clear stages. the first stage is de-escalation: stopping the spiral of violence and ensuring a minimum of stability and security. there have been a number of points that stakeholders in ukraine are trying to deliver on. but there is a second stage. the second stage is about the political process. it is about the platform for inclusive political dialogue to tackle the medium and long-term challenges of ukraine, and there are many. members have referred to most of them. in that second stage, the ukrainians will have to address issues such as constitutional change. they would need to address the issue of creating the conditions for free and fair elections, because the record of the previous elections is not good. the ukrainians have actually gone backwards rather than forwards. i am one who strongly believes that, for free and fair elections to happen in the ukraine, one has first to create the conditions before calling for an early election. but there is also a third stage, and that is one that you have debated many times. it is about the association agreement. it is about political association, and our programme of reforms for ukraine strengthen democracy and the rule of law. it is about the blueprint for economic reforms to bring investment and prosperity for ukraine, but it is also about people-to-people contact. it is about being visa-free. it is not because of us but, unfortunately, because of ukrainians that we do not see such progress on this particular issue, as we have seen, for example, in our relations with moldova. my fourth point concerns results. there are results showing that the strategy is working. we had a revocation of the package of undemocratic laws of 16 january. we had the resignation of the government, which was unable to handle the people’s aspirations in the maidan – and not only in kiev but in other maidans too. it is not perfect, but we have amnesty law. we have an observance by law enforcement agencies and the police of not using excessive force. the case of dmytro bulatov, the leader of automaidan, has clearly shown that, despite those results, there are other issues related to basic human rights that we need to observe – the fact that on ukrainian terrority we are witnessing the kidnapping and torture of people, and that there are still a number of people unaccounted for, is something which is very difficult to accept, and it needs to stop. another point when we are talking about results is that this is a race against time, because the more time it takes for the parties to establish a certain level of confidence and find a way out, the more time there is for extremism and radicalism and those elements which are not under control to grow throughout ukraine. that brings me to my fifth point: the bigger picture. the bigger picture concerns the future relationship between the european union and the european integration project, with its historical record, and another project which is in the making: the eurasian union. but it is a relationship which should be not based on the zero-sum game. the european union’s strength since its inception has always been in finding win-win solutions, even in seemingly hopeless situations. let us do our best to avoid backtracking from this approach. that brings me to the sixth and final point: the future. i believe the future needs to be about three things. it needs to be about us delivering on what this new neighbourhood policy has put forward as the main principle: that the relationship we are seeking is not only with the authorities but with the citizens of the country, and we should not fail them. secondly, we should not only talk about the sovereign decisions of the countries and their right to make sovereign decisions; we also need to help them to establish the conditions whereby they are free to make such decisions. finally, if we are all really serious about reform and transformation in this part of europe, let us be serious in choosing the strongest instrument we have, namely a european perspective.

russians over the heads of our partners – about them, without them. it is not about that. this is a general discussion; it is not a discussion about a specific association with a specific partner country. what we intend to discuss are the russian concerns that have been expressed, which i can summarise briefly. the first is that, as a result of an association agreement/dcfta, eu products would flood the markets of a partner country and that the partner country, having a free trade agreement with russia and the customs union, would start to flood the market of the russian federation and the customs union. the second concern referred to by the russian representatives is a scenario in which, allegedly, we would use our partner’s market to re-export eu products to the russian market and on behalf of the verts/ale group. – madam president, in december 2012 the united nations general assembly adopted a resolution on intensifying efforts to end female genital mutilation (fgm). the resolution calls for the development of a comprehensive strategy aimed at eliminating the practice. in europe, the european parliament estimates that half a million women – the equivalent of the population of malta – live with the consequences of the practice and another 180 000 are at risk every year. these estimates show how important it is for the eu to play its part in ending the practice. in that respect the commission action plan represents a key element of the european response to the calls and commitments made in the un resolution. the role of the european parliament will be to monitor progress on the implementation of the action plan to eliminate fgm. the action plan promotes a comprehensive and multidisciplinary approach. it reflects international human rights standards and insists on the need to focus on prevention. prevention of fgm means working for, and with, affected communities and in particular with young people. it means working on gender stereotypes and seeking to identify and overcome barriers to ending fgm within each community. prevention also means training professionals who are likely to be in contact with affected women and girls. but prevention does not mean prosecution. we need to move away from the criminalisation approach. there is to date no evidence and no research to prove the deterrent effect of prosecution on the perpetuation of the practice. yes, there is a need for legislation on fgm. there is a need for child protection measures and laws which acknowledge that fgm is an act that affects society as a whole. however, there is also a need to analyse the impact of prosecution on the female child. judicial procedures, prison sentences, large fines or long separations from the parental family may have a serious impact on the child’s well-being. it is crucial not to confuse prevention and prosecution and not to confuse understanding and fear. if we aim for long-term prevention, we first need to work on changing the belief systems and social norms of those affected by fgm. working towards ending fgm is therefore a long-term goal which requires long-term vision. communities need to be involved in the development of such a vision and we need data, in particular on prevalence, in order to monitor and evaluate the impact of existing measures and develop relevant policy responses. as meps, we should commit to supporting those who are already working to end the practice, and i am very glad to see that the resolution we have adopted today will support the work of fgm campaigners in europe. those of us standing again in the forthcoming election campaign are seeking to be in the house over the next five years. already, however, we can show determination and continue fighting to prevent fgm by signing the pledge that the end fgm european campaign has put at our disposal.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it proposes a specific control, country by country, for access to the generalized system of preferences, subjecting such access to compliance with the main international conventions on sustainable development. in this context, the european commission may decide to adopt separate delegated acts to ensure access to the system for each country, requiring a case-specific analysis in the context of the specific situation of each applicant country. this would allow for a greater impact of the implementation of the main international agreements on sustainable development. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour. regulation (eu) no 978/2012 lays down the arrangements for the union’s generalised system of preferences (gsp), which is meant to help developing countries by making it easier for them to export their products to the eu. the gsp consists of a general arrangement and two special arrangements, including the special incentive arrangement for sustainable development and good governance (gsp+), whereby no duties are levied on imports of more than 6 000 tariff lines from the beneficiary countries. gsp+ is designed to work as a credible incentive for those countries which earnestly want to commit themselves to implementing core international conventions that are essential in the context of sustainable development.
in writing. - in the absence of adequate global commitment, europe's objective is to lead by example by minimising and stabilising greenhouse gas concentrations and reducing emission levels. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the establishment of a european environment agency. there is no doubt that a reduction in gas emissions is necessary and, in this context, it is essential to set emission limits, which may be more or less stringent. i believe that these needs must be met, but also taking into account other political needs, such as maintaining and boosting the competitiveness of our industries and enterprises, which must not be penalized in the global context.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution as it involves a necessary revision of the determination of the volumes of greenhouse gas emission allowances to be auctioned in the period 2013-2020. the system for calculating the abovementioned emission allowances that has been applied until now was ridiculous because the limits set were so outrageously high that they did not create any incentive for the different industries to reduce emissions, since the impact of the crisis and the decline in economic activity had produced a decrease in emissions making the previously set limits on emission allowances useless. the revision of these volumes is absolutely necessary for this instrument to be able to serve to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.

the european voluntary humanitarian aid corps. this support reflects the views of european citizens, whom you all represent. according to eurobarometer, 88[nbsp ]% of europeans are in favour of the creation of eu aid volunteers and look forward to seeing them established and in action. with the active engagement of parliament, the commission and the council we are now coming to the final stage of making their wish happen. as a result, by 2020 nearly 20[nbsp ]000 europeans will have taken part in activities benefiting people in need – and, as ms[nbsp ]striffler said, the numbers of such people are unfortunately growing – but also benefiting the volunteers themselves by helping them gain new skills and new experience. at this time of tight budgets we have worked hard to make sure that we provide value for money, that the eu aid volunteers complement existing schemes, and that this also helps the volunteers to advance their own development. most of them are young people and for them volunteering is also a way to become more competitive on tighter labour markets. we have carried out three rounds of pilot projects in which over 40 humanitarian organisations took part, providing valuable insights into what exactly is needed in standard setting, in training and in deployment for the programme to achieve its main goal: to be a platform where europeans live out our values, where
