on behalf of the ppe group mr president, madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr danjean, on the thorough report he has presented to us: a report which, as the high representative said, gives us the opportunity to examine what this legislature has been, what this comprehensive vision of the common foreign and security policy is and what it should be, and, as she said, at a very particular moment in our calendar, coinciding with the deepest crisis we have ever experienced, which has logically slowed down efforts in terms of external action. following his outline, the main challenges have occurred in our immediate scenario, in our southern neighbourhood, with the crises in libya, egypt and syria and their regional and international consequences and, of course, after the vilnius summit, with the crisis in ukraine. as the rapporteur is french, i would like to quote the opinion recently expressed by a professor at the institute of political science in paris, who says that the crisis in ukraine could make the european union find the narrative and the new impetus it is looking for since the fall of the berlin wall. but to do that we need to review our energy policy in the direction of less dependence; we need to move towards greater space in the area of security and defence policy so that our soft power is complemented by a force capable of responding to a new configuration of threats; we need to work towards a review of the united nations system, in which one of the veto powers has been imposing its will, and, mrs ashton, in an area in which you have been working: that the european union, to be credible, must speak with one voice on the international scene. otherwise, we're just going to be really the organization that signs the check on the great contemporary dramas. only on this basis can we have an integrated approach in which the notions of security, defence, diplomacy, development aid, trade, culture and even civilization are linked together, complement each other, in order to respond to the new challenges and threats that are emerging globally. and only in this way, mrs ashton, can we achieve what mr danjean proposes in his report, namely a multipolar order that is fair, that is credible, that is reasonable, that makes it possible to defend the principles we hold to, namely the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states and, of course, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. before i close, mr president, i should like to acknowledge the efforts made by the high representative/vice-president of the commission in this last appearance to make european union policy more credible, more coherent and more effective in what at first seemed an absolutely impossible task. i would like to express my appreciation to you, mr president, and also my gratitude to all your colleagues for your continued willingness to engage in dialogue, a willingness which i extend not only to this member but also to my political group. my best wishes, madam high representative, for your future!
mr president, mrs ashton, in this farewell speech i would first of all wish you well, but from the critical standpoint which my group has maintained over the years and which we will continue to maintain as long as there is no change in foreign and security policy. we are facing a complete failure of this project of regional integration, which does not take into account the general interest, the workers, employment and the quality of life of the people. it's a project, therefore, failed. we need another regional integration project, one that puts people, people, back at the centre of attention. and, within this failed project, undoubtedly, maintaining a security policy subordinated to american policy does not lead us anywhere, to any situation in which it is clearly stated that the world needs to be led by a different policy, one that is committed to disarmament, to peace and to overcoming conflicts, from the point of view of prevention. boss obama came to brussels and gave us orders: increase military spending and deploy nato around russia. a total mistake.
mr president, mrs ashton, i will not insist on describing the multipolar and complex international scenario, with asymmetrical threats, with conflicts over energy, security, resources or mass migration, but i do want to stress that it is very discouraging that five years after we have equipped ourselves with the necessary instruments for this - instruments of which you are the visible head - we are stating the obvious: that in this geopolitical environment the european union must project an integrated strategy of its role in the world. it is very discouraging that it was only in december 2013 that you agreed with yourself - in your multiple capacities as high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, vice-president of the commission and president of the foreign affairs council - to tell us that we need to move forward in the coherence of the european union's external action in the areas of development, trade, energy, the environment, migration or global economic governance and other issues of global scope. then go ahead, mrs ashton, and present parliament with results instead of requests for greater consistency. you are responsible for making all these policies coherent. because it is also very discouraging that, while you say in the communication - to yourself and to the european parliament - that without development there is no security, you are committing - to support ukraine - three billion euros which will affect the budget of the european union, specifically civil crisis management and capacity building in africa. and amending budgets are already being requested in the committee on budgets. the aid to ukraine is a shared political decision, but it should not be at the expense of other policies, particularly development policy, or of mortgaging future eu budgets, for the year 2016 in particular. and a fundamental aspect which the communication focuses on is energy: the european union's foreign policy will have the opportunity to be independent and unified if there is a strategy for the diversification of energy supplies and an infrastructure which allows for a wider use of renewable energy sources, but also of indigenous sources and resources...
mr president, i would first of all like to congratulate mr danjean on his report and thank mrs ashton for her efforts over the years. we are in a global, interconnected, interdependent world. we need to have, the union needs to have, more coherent and effective external action and this increasingly requires that we have one voice and one direction. consistency must be ensured by your double, or triple, hat, mrs ashton. the european union, for many reasons, interests and values, geographical location, characteristics of its economy and trade, its energy dependence, historical and social links, requires a stable and peaceful world, to which we must contribute by cooperating closely with the united nations and other partners, among whom i would highlight the united states. the first area of concern should of course be our complex neighbourhood, where the effectiveness of our action has been tested. given the variety and complexity of challenges and crises, our approach to external action must be comprehensive. crises require comprehensive responses, in which there must be ingredients not just political, economic, cooperative, humanitarian or food. we often need security elements, military elements too, as we have seen in libya or mali recently. ladies and gentlemen, history is not over, nor have conflicts involving military means disappeared. we have just seen this in the unfortunate case of crimea. we must therefore look more closely at the security and defence aspects.
vice-president of the commission and high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. - mr[nbsp ]president, i would like to thank everyone who has taken the trouble to participate in this debate. can i begin by again thanking mr danjean very much for his report. it is extremely important that this debate continues. i want to just pick up a few of the comments that have been made, beginning with this concept of a comprehensive approach, because i agree that if it becomes simply a catchword, it is waste of time. i recall that when i started four and a half years ago, that actually, in this city alone, it was practically impossible to bring together people working on the same geographical area or indeed, i would argue, on the same set of issues. people did not know each other. they had never met. the institutional framework provided opportunities for people to develop their individual approach or their institutional approach, but not a european union approach. if you add into that the work going on in the member states, you can imagine the fragmentation that existed. so this approach was specifically designed to try to make sure that, in using our resources, we used them properly and well to bring together the work that we did, and to have a greater and better impact on the range of challenges. the horn of africa is often cited as the best example of that, and it is. if you speak to the somali president or the foreign minister, and you speak to the people running the atalanta military missions, to the colleagues working on development, to the african union or to our international partners, they will all tell you that we have come a long way since the days when it was impossible to work out which bit of the union was operating at any one time. but i would be the first to tell you that it is the beginning and not the end. there is much, much more to be done to consolidate and develop this approach and bring the instruments together. i have to tell you that, without the support of parliament, it is not by any means a guaranteed approach. i also want to say that i agree with those who talked about security and development going together. if you had sat, as i did, with many of the members from the african union nations, who have been in brussels for the summit, they will all tell you from their own experiences that unless you have security, you cannot do development. they have to go hand in hand. that means thinking more creatively and, in a sense, more strategically, about what it is we are trying to do. you can pour money into a problem. that is easy. we can throw money at it, but if you do not get the results, it is a waste of time and resources. so you have to think about how elements of our strategy interact with each other. i think that is going to be even more important in the future. a number of colleagues talked about energy, and it also applies there. when we were holding the us-eu energy council, which secretary of state kerry and i chair, we were making exactly the same points that have been made in this debate: the need member states to work more closely together in an interconnected way and to think about energy supply, energy diversity, diversification in the context of climate change and environmental needs, and the impact that can be made by member states not being reliant on individual sources of energy. energy policy is also about foreign policy, because we get our energy from many countries, some of which are going through extremely difficult times. the supply of sweet oil from libya, which is used by some countries for certain parts of their work for which they need oil supplies, was badly disrupted. the only other source of that same supply is nigeria, which itself has challenges and difficulties. so there are many ways in which we need to think about energy policy in the context of our foreign policy. just think of the north of iraq as another example of that. when we think about our neighbourhood, we know that we have had dramatic change and that countries are still hugely at risk from what could happen. nowhere is that more true than in libya. libya is going through terrible difficulties and actually one of the problems, in terms of the structure of libya and how they are trying to develop their institutional framework, is that it is very difficult to support libya in the ways that we normally do – by which i mean trying to find the people who are in the right place, with the right authority to do things. that means we have to rethink, to some extent, in a creative way, both how we collaborate with the libyan people and the libyan authorities, and how we work together internationally. that is exactly what we are doing now and it is why i am appointing a personal envoy to do that, because it has proved incredibly challenging. in terms of the point that was made about the budgets, the future and the question about humanitarian aid and the instrument for stability, i come back to my point about comprehensiveness. the point about the instrument for stability is that it is designed to try to create stability. if you do not have stability and countries collapse, then you have a greater need for humanitarian aid. so these are not in competition with each other and should not be. i will be the first to support kristalina georgieva in the magnificent work she has done to try to get humanitarian aid and support for those in greatest need. nowhere is that more evident than in syria today. but we also need to have support from this parliament to ensure what we do have, that can help create stability, or maintain stability, is able to be put to good use. i hope that this will be taken into account in the committee on budgets. on defence, there are some members of this house who i will never convince on aspects of defence, so let me just say two or three things. we are not in competition with nato. i attend meetings of the foreign ministers and defence ministers of nato. we work closely with nato to do two or three things. one is that our membership is slightly different, so there are ways in which we can engage countries to enable us to think more strategically about defence and security matters. secondly, there are times when nato would not wish to be in the front line because of its very specific role, and here it can look to the european union to help fulfil obligations. the central african republic initiative will be launched this week. there are places where it is better to have an eu presence than a nato presence. that is not me saying that. that is what nato would say. thirdly, there is work to be done in support of what nato does and what we do. when i think about the lessons we have learned in these last three or four years about the way in which we need collaboration, this is not about loss of sovereignty, but about collaboration to ensure that we have the assets that are going to be needed in times of conflict – times that are changing and yet seem now to remain the same. so they are different, but they are complementary. one of the most important elements of this is complementarity. i may not convince everybody, but that is what the purpose of all this has been. we are not weakening nato. our purpose is to strengthen all that we do on defence. i think this going to be an important part of the defence ministers’ meeting which i will chair the week after next, but also in the build-up to the nato summit which will take place in wales in september. i also agree with what has been said about moldova, and i would mention georgia. it is very important that we get these agreements in place for them. i also agree about bosnia herzegovina, because i have spent a lot of time talking with political leaders in bosnia herzegovina to develop a broader approach and a growth and jobs compact for them, as they are looking at record levels of unemployment. it was 38% – and over 50% for young people – when i was last there a couple of weeks ago. that brings me to the point made about employment and workers. one of the biggest challenges we face in our neighbourhood is the number of young people. think about the communities that we are working with, where there are huge numbers of young people who want a future and are looking for good educational opportunities, employment prospects, and the future development of their lives. they are now more and more interconnected with each other and, unless we have good and strong policies to support those young people across our neighbourhood, i think our societies are going to find it much tougher to be able to develop in the way that we would wish, with peace and security at the heart of them. for those who are worried about how many people are in the service, i have checked. twenty-one per cent of posts as officials in the external action service are held by people from member states who joined after 2004 and, at higher levels, it is 23%, which is more than the population percentage of those countries. i am not saying that i am complacent about that, but actually the record is pretty good. let me finish by making a couple of points that i think are really important. at the heart of everything that we do, we have to keep the values that we hold dear. if we do not do that, we will have failed. the promotion of democracy, respect for all individuals and the right of people to have their voices heard is a fundamental and crucial element of what all the nations that have become part of the european union stand for and of the aspirations of so many people who see the eu as a valuable force for the future. the treaty gives this position certain powers. it does not give it powers to do things that i sometimes hear members of this parliament suggest that we should do. it is an intergovernmental foreign affairs council. it is an intergovernmental process at one level, linked to a community method and developing and strengthening what that means for the roles that can be played, not just by an individual, but by a service and an approach that has been part of a treaty. it is work in progress, with a long way to go. i hope that, as this develops, you will see the potential for what it can be, supported by all member states, because they are crucial – and i am very proud of the support i get from the foreign affairs council and from the member states – but also linked to the aspirations of what this could be. this is not about loss. this is about gain. every member state participating in the eu process gains from it. they are able to better project their power and their strength. it is true for the one that i know best; it is true for every single one represented here. i wish you good luck and all the best for the future. for myself, the first thing i will wish for will be a holiday. the next item is the debate on the recommendation for second reading by the committee on international trade on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 428/2009 establishing a community regime for the control of exports, transfer, brokering and transit of dual-use items (18086/1/2013 - c7-0093/2014 - 2011/0310(cod)) (rapporteur: christofer fjellner) (a7-0236/2014).
member of the commission. - mr president, first of all i wish to thank the rapporteur, mr fjellner, for his constructive approach to this proposal and all the efforts deployed to find an agreement on these substantive and complex issues. it is indeed important that this file is concluded before the end of this legislature. as you will know, adoption of this legislative proposal is all the more urgent for economic reasons, as companies across europe have called on the eu to ensure rapid updates to our control lists so as to ensure a level playing field with companies from other third countries. before the lisbon treaty, a different decision-making procedure was used, with the result that updates were available earlier. however, the result of this rather long exchange is a wealth of ideas about how we can adjust the wider eu policy on dual-use goods. updating the list is also important to ensure that export controls focus on the most sensitive items and continue to contribute effectively to international security as well as to the eu’s security. as technology improves, particularly in the military domain, we can afford to desensitise carefully identified goods to ease their trade across borders. i am conscious that during this legislative procedure the honourable members have tabled various amendments that touch on the important issues pertaining to the overall eu export control system, its effectiveness, its contribution to our competitiveness and our security, as well as the global protection of fundamental rights. i am therefore particularly satisfied that extensive discussions took place between the three institutions and that an agreement could be found. i am confident that the ongoing review of the eu system will provide an opportunity to address these important issues. in this respect i am happy to inform you that a commission communication will be adopted shortly, before the end of the month of april. the communication will set out options for addressing the various issues raised by this parliament and by other stakeholders in order to modernise the export control system and strike the right balance between security and competitiveness. we must be able to respond to new challenges, such as the export of cyber tools and internet surveillance systems that could be used in violation of human rights. the forthcoming legislature should expect to provide a political appreciation of the future of eu export controls policy very soon after july and this will probably be one of the few cases where, for understandable policy reasons, we control exports rather than keeping the markets open. goods with sometimes life-saving civilian applications, as in health research, must not threaten human lives if used instead and inappropriately for military purposes. i am therefore confident that this file will keep our respective institutions very politically engaged.

the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european telecommunications market is not affected by the introduction of new technologies, and that the commission is not obliged to take any action to ensure that the new technologies are not used in the same way as the old ones. this is what you're going to understand today.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to ensure that the resources from the european social fund are effectively used to improve the situation of older workers. this report points to the need for financial and economic control instruments in the implementation of projects financed by the european social fund. such control instruments are necessary to ensure that the definition of 'older workers' is adapted to the minimum retirement age in each of the member states of the union. i have decided to vote in favour of this report to improve access to european social fund resources for retired workers in the eu.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it strengthens the role of the mass media as instruments for the promotion of the 'values' of the eu's foreign policy. the report understands the foreign policy of the european union as a monolithic bloc and does not express that a large part of the population rejects the policies of eu imperialism. the report proposes to create a tool to attack free trade and to try to finance destabilisation by manipulating information in countries which are not allies or subjects of the european union. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - the aim of this proposal is to ensure a high level of protection of health and the environment and to safeguard the internal market in motor vehicles with regard to their noise level. to this end, member states should harmonise their legislation as regards the permissible sound level of motor vehicles, including the different technical requirements. this will not only ensure uniform application but also set clear conditions for manufacturers. this report provides for the application of a set of limit values according to the vehicle category over three phases and requires the manufacturer to provide information on the noise levels of vehicles at the point of sale and in technical promotional material. it requires the installation of appropriate warning systems to protect the blind and other vulnerable persons. finally, pay particular attention to the characteristics of the road surface, as these are directly related to the noise level of vehicles.
in writing. - half of the union population in urban areas is exposed to noise levels above 55 db(a) as a result of ambient road noise. constant exposure to traffic noise increases the risk of cardiovascular diseases and high blood pressure. the proposal represented much needed policy to tackle noise at source. both the rapporteur and members of the committee took a position to weaken the commission original proposal, going below even the current requirements, introducing countless loopholes and derogations. finally, even though approaching vehicle audible systems or avas for electric vehicles, a fundamental security tool for people with visual impairment, will be compulsory, the report does not fulfil the minimum objectives for such a proposal.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it grossly underestimates the seriousness of the problem of traffic noise in many areas of europe. thousands of people suffer from health problems in many areas of heavy traffic in the european union. the original proposal of the european commission was much more ambitious and included noise levels much lower than the limits contained in the current proposal. in addition, important articles introducing measures on the classification of eu roads according to the noise they produce, the labelling of the noise level produced by vehicles, etc. have been deleted. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it does not include a responsible and verifiable check that the meat sold does not come from genetically cloned animals or their descendants. this report proposes a database for the monitoring of bovine stocks in the different member states of the european union which does not explicitly exclude this type of animals, introducing the potential risks associated with the set of databases. the control of meat from cloned animals has been a priority issue that has not been taken into account by the other european institutions. the european commission and the council have refused to identify animals that may pose unknown health risks. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains a reference to the creation of tools to defend the european market from trade retaliation which may be useful, it recognises the role and legitimacy of the world trade organisation, recognising it as a motor of development. as we see every day, international trade is the cause of the underdevelopment of many regions of the world, and there is no type of trade that is not based exclusively on market principles. although it is changing, as this report claims, trade remains the main source of the planet's economic, social and environmental problems. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it introduces a series of democratic controls by the european parliament on the negotiations carried out by the commission by means of delegated acts under articles 290 and 291 of the tfeu. in addition, the report has succeeded in introducing into the tripartite negotiations with the commission and the council the reference to the rights of workers affected by this trade flow between the european union and bangladesh, including the international labour conventions, making it clear that the european union must ensure the implementation of these. although international trade is still not a driver of development, this report introduces ways of democratic control and respect for workers' rights. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - this draft regulation aims to increase the protection of public health and safety by measures such as the removal of barriers in the internal market or the improvement of transparency in relation to the information received by patients. this is to be achieved by clarifying the scope of the legislation and establishing clear obligations for manufacturers, by making the requirements more stringent and by adapting the risk classification and the advisory procedure, and by measures to improve transparency and access. all these actions are therefore aimed at tightening up the provisions to ensure the highest levels of public health and safety.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a considerable advance in the protection of the european consumer, by proposing a control regulation against market laws which only seek to increase the profits of the pharmaceutical companies. the report defines the term medical devices as all types of devices used in the diagnosis, prevention, monitoring or treatment of diseases. the regulation of such instruments is much better set out in this proposal, avoiding the bad practices of the pharmaceutical industry by improving labelling, monitoring by control agencies, etc. this report improves on the original proposal, and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. - in favour. implantable devices are not like medicines: when a serious incident occurs, it is not possible to just stop the treatment – the patient has to be operated on again. the recent scandals with faulty breast implants, hip replacements and other devices have underlined serious flaws with eu legislation on medical devices. the greens/efa supported the rapporteur, who pushed for a pre-market approval, but epp, alde and ecr were strictly against. faced with this political reality, we supported the stronger controls so as to have better evaluation of high-risk devices before they are put on the market. we succeeded in getting our proposal, that innovative high-risk devices should always be assessed against the existing reference treatment, adopted.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents an improvement in the legislation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices which will make it possible to put an end to the inconsistency between the different national regulations in the european union. the report develops a classification of these types of products according to the risks they pose to the user and to public health, allowing for appropriate treatment for each type of product. this report includes improved transparency on potential uses, protection of minors and people with disabilities, exemption from the rules for products for home use, etc. all these principles constitute a report which improves the protection of users of such products and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a breakthrough in environmental accounting of the economies of the member states of the european union. the report covers the development of new accounting in relation to the existing accounting system, which only covers air pollution, environmental taxes and material flows. the report proposes to include the environmental expenditure of states, the amount of all environmental goods and services produced by the economy and the energy flows of the state in question (energy input, consumption, etc.). this proposal will improve knowledge of the environmental impact of the member states' economies, which is absolutely necessary for the establishment of clear policy objectives in this area. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - the aim of this proposal is to establish 2015 as the european year of development, given that the eu is the largest donor of official development assistance worldwide. its strong commitment to supporting countries dates back to 1957, when the treaty of rome first established a european development policy. however, european citizens are often uninformed about these issues and are unaware of the added value these development policies bring to society. the european year of development therefore represents an opportunity to solve this problem by improving the level of information on european development policies in all member states.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although the impetus it can give to the european union's development policy is important, it has been decaffeinated and, once again, does not tackle the main problems of development policy. the report includes points on which there is no disagreement - in my view - such as the promotion of the fight against gender discrimination, the approach to decentralised aid, support for young people, etc. however, a development policy isolated from the political and economic problems produced by the eu's neo-colonial policy means continuing to throw sand into the sea. development means fighting the causes of underdevelopment that are in the present capitalist world system. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - development and the aspects of development cooperation have changed radically in recent decades. if we take 2015 as a reference point, the year in which the so-called millennium development goals were supposed to have been achieved, it is clear how important the european union considers the coming year to be. the main and largest donor of official development aid in the world can only strengthen through concrete policies the commitment that we can even find in the founding treaties of rome, and to which the last treaty of lisbon only gives full continuity by implementing actions such as the establishment of this very necessary year.
in writing. - the debris of spacecraft, satellites and similar objects in earth orbit poses a safety risk to new satellites and orbital devices such as communications satellites. this question is critical today because of the importance of satellites in social and economic life. having a monitoring system in place that can help minimise the risk of collision and damage or destruction of satellites is of great importance. the report is moving in that direction.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although the monitoring of 'space junk' is indeed a very important issue, there are more important political priorities for which no resources are allocated. the monitoring and tracking of such space objects is essential to enable the continued use of all technologies related to the services that satellites can provide. without a comprehensive space control, such technologies are subject to high risk and could suffer periodic incidents that further worsen the situation. however, this programme, although necessary, seeks to protect the investments of private technology groups, while european citizens are denied access to public resources through austerity policies. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this resolution because, although it contains measures which will benefit farmers and livestock farmers in the event of any health problems affecting their production, it is a guarantee that european agribusiness will take advantage of it to ensure their production with cap funds. the report also proposes the use of the flexibility mechanism for financing agricultural health crises, legitimising the instruments developed for the economic governance of the european union. that is why i could not vote in favour, even though the report proposes crisis aid measures for farmers and livestock farmers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it sets strict criteria for the importation of wood products into the european union. the report reinforces the forest law enforcement, governance and trade (flegt) licensing system established by council regulation (ec) no 2173/2005. this regulation did not apply to all wood products irrespective of their origin, but only to those for which a voluntary cooperation agreement exists, allowing circumvention of those requirements when such products are imported from third countries with which such voluntary agreements do not exist. the report proposes that all timber products imported into the eu should comply with this legislation, causing a real impact on imports from this sector. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - in favour. formal approval of the partner countryʼs licensing scheme is perhaps the most important act in implementing the euʼs flegt policy. it has to be ensured that only certified timber enters the eu market. the greens therefore suggested that this be done by a delegated act, which gives parliament also a right to veto. however, this idea was dismissed by parliamentʼs legal department as not admissible, given that approval of a licensing scheme does not alter the basic flegt act. the greens then welcomed the council proposal to have the ‘silent procedureʼ of the implementing act reversed for the approval of the licensing scheme. that means that if the council does not establish a position, the commission cannot approve the proposal for an implementing act. however, this option has been dismissed in trilogues since parliament insisted that the council should not have its powers increased where parliament has no say at all. reversal of the ‘silent procedureʼ is moreover not provided for in the implementing act procedure. since the council did not insist, the greens could not come out in favour of a procedure grossly altering the balance of powers between the two legislators.
in writing. - in this report i was unable to vote in favour of the parliament's decision to approve the management of the budget of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators for the financial year 2012, but i did vote in favour of the resolution that follows. by this report, the european parliament exercises its right to scrutinise the accounts of the european union agencies. in this case it approves the management of the said agency, and as i do not agree with it i have not voted in favour. however, the resolution fully reflects the main highlights of the aforementioned management during the 2012 financial year. that is why i did not vote for the discharge decision but for the resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents an improvement in the regulation of clinical trials in the european union, so that this type of testing of medicinal products for human use can be carried out more transparently. this report introduces the view that clinical trials of this type of medicinal product cannot be considered as a trade secret, since they concern human health. the report also calls for the creation of a european database containing all information on such clinical trials. this report promotes transparency, ending the obscurantism that prevails in the activities of pharmaceutical companies. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. - in favour. we concentrated our work on transparency and the role of the ethics committee. there was a huge campaign from civil society for transparency of clinical trial data. on the other hand, the pharmaceutical industry wanted to subject such data to their very far-ranging understanding of what would be commercially confidential. we not only called strongly for the clinical study report to be uploaded into the eu database, but were also the driving force behind ensuring also that the law explicitly specifies that clinical study reports should not be considered commercially confidential. this would not have happened without us, this is a clear victory for us. we were also keen to re-introduce an ethics committee, and requiring a positive opinion by them to allow a trial to go ahead.
in writing. - the ultimate objective of such trials is to concentrate resources and efforts in a highly efficient manner on the development of special treatments for the so-called rare diseases, which require so much attention. this standard will facilitate cross-border cooperation to carry out such larger, more viable and reliable clinical trials. in addition, transparency in this area will be increased by publishing such trials in a public database to be set up on an ad hoc basis. all this will simplify existing procedures by establishing a uniform framework in all member states with the corresponding sanctions for those responsible, both researchers and pharmaceutical companies, who do not comply with the regulation adopted here.
in writing. - i think it was a missed opportunity to establish a stricter and more transparent control of nuclear installations. moreover, parliament has not had the capacity to take part in the decision-making process on this text, as on all the texts dealing with the nuclear issue, and has only been consulted. the commission's text, which is not very forceful, is accompanied by the contemporary spirit of the author of the report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains many points seeking to tighten legislation to improve the safety of european nuclear installations, it continues to regard this type of energy as a necessary source for the eu's energy production. the report is aimed at improving safety conditions in european power stations by delegating to the european commission the task of reviewing these new safety standards. the report envisages the opening of new nuclear plants. we believe that nuclear power production has too costly externalities and too high risks to be profitable without incurring the costs to the public administration and the environmental threats to the nearby inhabitants. that is why, despite improving the safety of power stations, i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - against. the proposed legislation regrettably represents very little improvement on the current situation as regards safety of nuclear installations. yet pro-nuclear member states will use this legislation to pretend that safety of nuclear power plants is dealt with under this legislation. we will however push for improvements. although we did not succeed in changing the legal basis (parliament is therefore merely consulted under the euratom treaty), it is key to continue to push for more transparency and participation in the decision-making process by the public and by civil society (in particular through the aarhus and espoo conventions). as it stands now, the jordan report limits public participation to some information but no access to any real decision-making/peer review processes (weakening the commissionʼs original text). priority should be given to nuclear safety.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because i consider it to be one of the most important issues in fiscal policy in the european union and, despite introducing positive changes, it delays its implementation until the end of 2016. the report introduces important changes, such as a new mandatory element and the fight against undertaxation, which are fundamental, when most large european companies are taxed at outrageous rates thanks to the tax engineering allowed by the laws of the member states. however, the report does not point to the need to implement such measures urgently, at a time when multi-billion dollar profits are barely taxed while states go bankrupt due to lack of revenue. delaying action means continuing to allow this looting of public coffers. i have therefore been unable to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it supports the european union's internal security strategy, as well as frontex and eurosur. for me, as for my whole group in this parliament, these agencies are part of an institutional framework aimed at persecuting migration, in violation of human rights and fundamental freedoms of human beings. the report points to the effects of the economic crisis, but not to the austerity policies which are decimating public resources in the member states. the committee also calls for a report on the human rights situation in immigration detention centres, without calling for their closure, the closure of these prisons for people who have committed no crime, only migration. i have decided to vote against this report because it implicitly takes over the eu's migration policy.
in writing. - we have not achieved our objective of having the european emissions trading system take account of extra-community flights and limit it to intra-community flights only. it's being delayed until 2017. that is why i voted against.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it clearly limits the application of the emission allowances of european airlines, so that they can account for greenhouse gas emissions well below their actual levels of emissions. the air transport sector is one of the world's leading polluters, accounting for 3[nbsp]% of global emissions, and its emissions have doubled between 1990 and 2006. this report provides an exemption for european airlines from accounting for all these emissions, leaving out all flights from or to third countries outside the european economic area. this is a clear falsification of the emission levels. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i agree that the application of the european aviation emissions trading system should not be suspended until the conclusion of the icao negotiations, but i do not support that it should apply only to intra-community flights, while flights to or from countries outside the eu are excluded until 2017. the eu must believe in the policies it develops, and suspending the implementation of the system depending on the opinion of other international actors is not a sign of trust or respect for democratically approved decisions. i would also like the commission to ensure that the funds raised are used properly and to reduce the discretion enjoyed by the member states. i regret that the interinstitutional agreement suspends the application of the eu ets. the commitment will also require member states to report on how they invest the profits they make from auctioning allowances.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is essential that there should be convergence in the sector; the fees charged for the use of the different types of bank cards cause considerable uncertainty for european users because of the discretionary powers exercised by each member state of the european union. each year the sector receives 9[nbsp ] billion euros from the payment of such fees, which is a significant volume of business extracted through all kinds of practices, many of them abusive, in a context of international financial crisis. this proposal improves the rules by preventing abusive practices carried out by different companies in the sector against users. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - the defence of the european consumer has been supported again by the european parliament through this project, which guarantees that a truly recognised means of payment, like any type of transaction carried out by credit or debit cards, does not entail an additional cost, often unknown and more often different, depending on the place where it is carried out. margins and commissions will be set up so that the spirit of the internal market is also operational in these transactions. in this context, legislation on banking commissions proper is still pending. this legislation will give consumers greater freedom when making payments and will improve the security of all payments made electronically via the internet.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it introduces a number of technical developments which need to be regulated, since the directive regulating payment services in the internal market is from 2007 (directive 2007/64/ec), and there have been numerous technological changes since that date which have transformed the market. card payments, mobile payments, etc. are still regulated differently in each member state. the report proposes a relative harmonisation of the operation of this type of payment service in the european union in order to seek better protection and consumer confidence in this type of payment service in the internal market. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial vehicle' to cover vehicles with a maximum mass exceeding 10 tonnes. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - the new technologies require innovation, including legislative and regulatory innovation, to prevent new frontiers from arising in a contradictory manner between potential consumers in the different member states. this will provide a secure legal framework for the user of services within the community, with all the security guarantees, both with regard to own information and to any additional costs generated in a random way. the aim of this directive is to establish in an unambiguous way how such payments are to be made.
in writing. - the internal market in electronic communications is at the heart of the digital economy. the role of telecommunications as a vehicle for innovation and connectivity should therefore be promoted, so that europe can fully exploit the opportunities for growth, competitiveness and employment that the digital internal market will offer. the european commission has therefore proposed to revise the main laws applicable to the telecommunications sector. this report, led by my colleague pilar del castillo, calls for the final abolition of retail invoicing for voice, sms and data roaming charges. it advocates internet accessibility for all, hence service providers should not only meet the basic needs of users, but should also be able to tailor their offer to more specific needs. due to their high importance, it also addresses the issue of conditions and procedures for the allocation of radio spectrum for wireless broadband communications, as well as the use of the parts of the spectrum that are not reserved.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although i consider it essential that there should be clear rules in the european union governing the electronic communications sector, it is a firm commitment to deregulation. the report introduces key issues to close the technological gap between the different european regions in terms of infrastructure. it also introduces a wide range of measures aimed at improving the functioning of the sector. however, all these measures reflect a neoliberal approach according to which public administrations must bear the costs of infrastructure, but the private sector is the one that enjoys the social gains. that is why, despite the improvement of the existing rules, i could not vote in favour.
in writing. - in order to further strengthen and promote one of the founding pillars of the european union, the single market, this regulation aims to facilitate the practical exercise of the right of providers of electronic communications services and networks to provide services through a harmonised and simplified notification system based on a harmonised model. it also seeks to facilitate the practical exercise of the right of citizens and businesses to access competitive, secure and reliable electronic communications services, with common rules ensuring a high level of protection, privacy and security of their personal data, and to achieve a more coordinated framework for the use of harmonised radio spectrum at union level for wireless broadband communications services. finally, it provides for the gradual abolition of unjustified roaming surcharges for communications within the union.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of the regulation ending roaming charges in 2015 and including a definition that safeguards the principle of net neutrality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it is a necessary measure to combat consumer distrust caused by the high number of abusive practices linked to the use of personal data relating to electronic identification. the report includes a proposal for a regulation which aims to close all loopholes in european legislation in this area, thus providing users of this type of electronic transactions with a much safer and more trustworthy framework. in a context of increasing levels of electronic transactions, it is necessary to address their regulation in a way that eliminates or minimises bad practices. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it is a proposal which goes in this direction.
in writing. - new technologies require a regulatory framework based on trust so that users can carry out any type of transaction electronically, knowing that they are interacting efficiently but, above all, covered by a regulation applicable to all member states that completely eliminates the feeling of legal uncertainty that the citizen currently perceives. electronic authentication or identification systems have to be based on the procedure that provides the most guarantees to the user, so the cross-border use of data should be regulated, as we are currently faced with very different levels of data permeability. this regulation will apply to both natural and legal persons, such as smes, which will be particularly helped by it. electronic signatures, seals and other similar systems will be in stable use if the regulatory framework is truly established in a formal, serious and applicable manner.
in writing. - the 2008 financial crisis put the proper functioning of the european audit regime for public-interest entities to the test. the causes are certainly many and must be sought in some shortcomings, such as insufficient supervision and the lack of adequate regulatory safeguards. tools and procedures should therefore be identified to improve the quality of audit services and competition in the market, in order to achieve a balance between costs and benefits for firms facing a difficult economic situation and users of audit services.
in writing. - i think the reform is manifestly insufficient. that is why the socialists tabled amendments to ensure that there is a rotation within a reasonable period (10 years, extendable to 14 years) and not every 24 years, as the report proposes. we also believe that the list of prohibited services is too lax and will be monitored by the audited company through its audit committee. we still have a financial and stock exchange system with muddy feet if the information on the accounting status of companies is not of quality. finally, auditors should concentrate on their audit activity. allowing, as the report does, up to 70%[nbsp ] of consultancy services to be invoiced to the audited firm itself, makes the audit a subsidiary activity for the consultant auditor and jeopardises his independence. in spain we have too many examples of the disastrous results for the economy and the taxpayer of the lack of quality in the audits. do you know the bankia case? do you know that 90% of the audits of the spanish banking system are carried out by a single auditor, deloitte, with the consequent systemic risk and the vices and the arrogance that monopoly or oligopoly entails?
in writing. - i voted against this report because it does not represent a real improvement in the requirements for statutory audits in public interest entities. the onset of the financial crisis pointed to how many of the entities operating in the financial sector had evaded their responsibilities, thanks to weak regulations that allowed free will without sufficient, or independent, supervisory bodies. this report is presented as a report which seeks to improve the requirements of statutory audits for public interest entities, such as savings banks, credit cooperatives, etc., which, in spain, have played a central role in the collapse of the financial sector. however, the report does not even require a genuine independence of the audits which can continue to audit a single client, a fundamental requirement to ensure the independence of the auditors. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it does not represent a real improvement in the requirements for statutory audits, but an increase in the turnover of the large multinationals which dominate the sector. the private audit sector has gradually replaced public bodies that monitor the accounts of companies and its operation has become one of the clear culprits in the massive financial frauds that triggered the economic crisis we are facing today. the report includes numerous amendments to the audit rules which introduce easily avoidable limitations and do not fundamentally change the functioning of a sector which has allowed the massive fraud of entire banking sectors in the eu. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it is an obscene acknowledgement of a fascist coup d'état, which was largely promoted by the european union and the united states themselves. this report makes it clear that the eu's only interest in ukraine is economic, and as long as the new government, like this fascist puppet imposed from outside, favours the eu's commercial interests it will have its support. this is the project of european 'integration', which is committed to an imperialist policy of destabilisation in order to seize the markets and resources of the region. while the situation in ukraine was not the best, we now have the guarantee that european capitals will be the only ones to benefit from the latest political changes. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a boost to the so-called 'comprehensive approach' to the european union's external action, which proposes to promote synergies in civil-military cooperation in external action and the use of funds earmarked for cooperation and development for military purposes. this approach means reaffirming the imperialist character of the european union and making available the instruments of external action in its favour. my group has tabled an alternative report because it is impossible to work with a text of the characteristics of the present one, which means opening the door to the financing of military projects with eu cooperation funds. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. - the external action of the european union is a priority, but it is hampered by the interests of the member states' respective foreign policies. that is why the lisbon treaty itself established an ad hoc figure to counter this negative reality (examples of which we have seen on several occasions, the case of kosovo being a paradigm, and which cannot be repeated in such hot cases as ukraine and crimea) and to encourage the european institutions and the member states to coordinate foreign policy more effectively and thus to use their political strength better in the face of external events. a non-coordinated eu response will lead to weak and in no way operational action, and this is something europe cannot allow.
in writing. - in this report i voted against the decision of parliament to give discharge to the commission in respect of the implementation of the budget of the executive agencies, but in favour of the resolution which follows. this report approves the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2012, a decision which i voted against, considering that the commission has managed these funds in a way that has benefited private companies and eroded the interests of member states that have been hit by the austerity policies promoted by the commission. i voted in favour of the resolution because it contains many detailed criticisms and comments on the management of the funds which the commission will have to follow up.

in writing. - i voted against this report because it does not include a responsible and verifiable check that the meat sold does not come from genetically cloned animals or their descendants. the labelling rules proposed in this report are voluntary and farmers will not have to give up the current labelling system. the question of the control of meat from cloned animals was raised by the european parliament at earlier stages, but during the negotiations with the other european institutions which make up the tripartite dialogue this article has been removed from the report. the european commission and the council have refused to point out that these animals may pose unknown health risks. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. - against. at parliament level, we were successful with the introduction of labelling provisions for ‘clone foodʼ. regarding voluntary labelling, we do not believe that a simple reference to the general food labelling legislation is enough for a sensitive product such as beef and therefore rejected the deletion of the voluntary labelling provisions. keeping the approval system guarantees that consumers can have trust in what is indicated. on eid, views within the group differed slightly. in the committee on the environment, we agreed that a harmonised approach would be useful and decided to support an amendment calling for a mandatory eid system in 10 years time. the main argument for eid is that it provides for a faster and more accurate reading of individual animal codes directly into data processing systems (which means better and faster traceability of infected animals and/or infected food). a transition period of 10 years would allow those concerned to have time to familiarise themselves with the system. the main argument against mandatory eid is that it has the potential to disproportionally disadvantage small farmers (who cannot profit from economies of scale). however it seems that solutions can be found in that regard, e.g. compensation for small farmers.

in writing. - the european system of financial supervisors (esfs) authorities play a key role in ensuring the solvency and safety of financial institutions and the stability and orderly functioning of financial markets, in accordance with european rules. they thus contribute to economic recovery and job creation in europe. the european parliament has been one of the main drivers behind the creation and development of these authorities. the court of auditors has found that the accounts of eba, eiopa and esma for the financial year 2012 are complete and correct in all material respects, the opinion of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, for which i was rapporteur, stresses that the additional tasks assigned to the authorities in their respective fields of activity will require increases in budget and new human resources in order to enable them to carry out their supervisory role satisfactorily. we have also asked the commission, as part of the review of the authorities' regulations planned for the beginning of the next parliamentary term, to create an independent budget line in the eu budget and to examine the payment of fees by market participants.

in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it makes some very good references to the cost of tax fraud, tax evasion and tax avoidance, it does not call for a european union tax policy to solve economic problems. the report details the losses suffered by eu financial resources due to fraud, and points to the agricultural and cohesion policies as the most problematic. however, there is no mention of the huge amount of financial resources being absorbed by the banking sector of the member states because of their continued fraud. the report also stresses the need to implement the european and mediterranean plant protection organisation, a new instrument to boost agro-industrial enterprises. i have therefore been unable to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this resolution because, despite the unusual balance in its wording, it continues to claim that parliament can impose itself on national sovereignty in matters which go beyond the implementation of human rights and have more to do with the imperial objectives of the european union. the resolution introduces in a politically balanced way the need to address human rights problems in iran, etc., but it takes the opportunity to subject the european political will to the interests of us imperialist policy, denouncing iran as a destabilising agent in the region, when the main destabiliser is the united states. that is why i could not vote in favour of this resolution.
mr president, we had two challenges: firstly, the european union's reduced dependence on oil - which has become even more apparent in recent days - and secondly, the reduction of the impact of transport on climate change. for years we have also been warning that the lack of infrastructure and recharging points for vehicles or ships using new fuels was clearly putting us in a vicious circle, because if there were no recharging points, there would be no cleaner cars and trucks, and if there were no cleaner cars and trucks, there would be no recharging points. i therefore welcome this agreement, which mr grosch has achieved with difficulty - again because of national selfishness - but at least we have reached the point of acceptance. the deadlines have been delayed in my view - we would have preferred it earlier for parliament and the commission - and a decision has also been taken which is not technologically neutral as regards the plug. i will not say who benefited because we have in principle obtained a certain transitional period for the plug which did exist. in any case, i only hope that the choice made will not delay the implementation of this directive by a single day - and i am right in saying 'not a single day'. i mean, i hope that one-off plug we've been talking about is on the market when it's needed. but at last we will see a network of hydropower plants like the one that will soon exist in my region - in aragon - where there is only one station at the moment. and there will also be lng moorings in ports. there was no budget, there is no budget in this directive, but it was foreseen - and i thank mr kallas for getting a good agreement on that - in the connecting europe facility. so although the commission had a little difficulty accepting these kind of strange projects, where transport issues but also energy were involved, i think we have finally got a good bet. i hope that the projects will soon be available, both for ports and for roads and also for urban nodes. i hope that these projects will be presented soon, that the commission will give them priority and facilitate them. only in this way will european and other car, truck and shipbuilders be encouraged to build them with a diversified capacity to accept other types of fuel: this will be the way to make european transport greener.
mr president, i too will be speaking on the report on plant health. the biggest problem facing plant health is the importation of pests from third countries. and the amendments to article 40, 78 to 85, propose a new strategy for more effective import controls, by being more preventive and comprehensive. this position was approved by the committee on agriculture. it is a position to defend farmers and plantations within the european union. the european union is the area of the world with the least protection against imported pests. a method for avoiding plant health risk is laid down which is no more or less the same as that which exists in animal health. we have always maintained in this parliament that the european union must protect itself as the united states protects itself, as russia protects itself, as the rest of the world protects itself. we cannot be as unprotected as we are in all things plant health and pest. we must also be aware that europe is less and less able to use pesticides to combat all these kinds of diseases that come to us from third countries. who are supporting this position that i'm advocating? it is being supported by farmers, who are losing their crops and suffering the consequences of an imported disease. and who's against it? they are against companies that trade in plants and seeds, which do not care if a crop is lost because they do not lose anything and do not have to fight against it. that is why i am defending this position and these amendments which offer us a system more like that of russia or the united states. and a few words only on animal health. the report and the regulation deal with animal health, not animal welfare, antibiotic resistance, or transport of animals. it deals exclusively with diseases affecting animals and which can be spread within the european union.
mr president, commissioner, on many occasions and in many reports we have called for genuine reciprocity in agricultural trade with third countries. this reciprocity in plant health matters is precisely what the committee on agriculture has adopted in the fajmon report: it consists in applying to plant production the same health protection that we apply to livestock production. all that is not on the list is either prohibited or under study for authorisation. it is nothing more or less than what countries like the united states, canada or russia apply to our vegetable production. this system would require that the checks be carried out in the country of origin and paid for by the exporting third country, which is not the case today: the european union, in addition to being open to the entry of all kinds of pests, pays for the checks of products that should never have left their country of origin; but moreover, the burden of proof also falls on the union. the current system requires us to prove to the third country that its shipments are contaminated. this has to stop. the system is not working properly and the commission knows it. last year there were countless border interceptions and the commission acted late and badly. thus, there were 33 interceptions in 2013 of the black spot fungus in citrus fruit from south africa, a proven risk to european citrus plantations, and the commission only reacted when the south african season had ended.
vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i will be brief because i think there is general agreement on the importance of giving small and mediumsized enterprises the means to overcome the great challenge of combating the crisis and providing job prospects for our young people. i would just like to say a few words about financing, access to credit for businesses. in total, we have decided to allocate 150 billion to industrial policy, to business in general, from the regional funds, 40 from horizon 2020 and 2.3 from cosme. as regards horizon 2020, it was parliament which decided to allocate 20% to small and medium-sized enterprises. there is also the battle for cosme, internationalisation, venture capital and the tourism sector, which is just for small and mediumsized enterprises. there is also the large package which the european commission proposed together with the european investment bank, which is unfortunately blocked by the council. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. unfortunately, the package is blocked by the council and therefore we must continue to push for the european commission and the european investment bank to make the proposal a reality, which could have given rise to many measures to support small and mediumsized enterprises. mr president, i think this debate has once again demonstrated how much parliament and the commission agree on the protection of the small and mediumsized enterprises sector. we cannot get out of the crisis by simply reducing public debt, but only if we are able to help the real economy, develop the market and, again, follow the fundamental line laid down in the treaty, which is the social market economy where the market is only an instrument for social policy, and social policy can be pursued in europe if we continue to help the internal market, industrial policy and policy to support small and mediumsized enterprises, because only in this way can new jobs be created and the crisis be prevented from having any further negative effects.
mr president, on 25 may this parliament will be judged by the citizens. after seven years of crisis, the question is: is the european union closer or further away from its citizens? during this term we have passed over 700 laws. there are certainly a number of surplus and some fundamental ones missing. important things have been done in the financial field, but there are also unfinished business. one, and not the least important, is the implementation of the financial transaction tax. after the failure of a fee for all the member states, enhanced cooperation was initiated for 11 member states, including spain. my government - and i welcome it - is a supporter and promoter of an effective economic and fiscal union without which europe cannot move forward. if we want the union to remain competitive with other regions, if we want to overcome the demographic challenge and maintain our distinctive brand of welfare state, it is time to do our homework. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the application of the principle of subsidiarity. nothing new under the sun! gentlemen of the council, make up your minds.
mr president, in this last part-session i feel obliged to give an account. we have ratified a number of initiatives to strengthen the rights of europeans: more protection for citizens when they act as consumers, an end to unfair terms by strictly enforcing compliance with european law and, in the event of non-compliance, sanctions against infringers. it also means more security for the most vulnerable: helping the retail trade, on which many european families depend, and implementing the rapid resolution of collective disputes so that they do not burden the delicate economy of european households any more. the measures to stimulate growth because, at the dawn of the economic and financial crisis, erratic policies have been applied which are leading us to deflation, with harsh budgetary adjustments which weaken not only the welfare state but also the confidence of the citizens. poverty and inequality have reached shameful and intolerable levels, as in my country (the second country with the highest rate of child poverty). the priority of this parliament is to defend the general european interest and to safeguard the common good.
mr president, on 8 april representatives of the parliament of catalonia, representing the will of a majority of that parliament and of the catalan citizens, went to the spanish congress of deputies to ask for the transfer of the competence to consult the catalan people on their political future. the congress of deputies flatly rejected the proposal. unfortunately, the no is the usual response from the spanish authorities. in 2005 he was the no to the new political statute for euskadi approved by a majority of the basque parliament. in 2010 it was the constitutional court that declared important parts of the catalan statute that had been approved in a referendum by the catalan people unconstitutional. yesterday, the navarrese people of etxarri-aranatz held a democratic, consensual and transparent referendum, in which more than 90% of the voters declared themselves in favour of the creation of an independent basque state. it was a real democratic exercise. catalonia will vote on its future on 9 november. the dialectic of votes and democracy will be imposed on the dialectic of imposition and denial by the spanish authorities. finally, today marks the 83rd anniversary of the proclamation of the second spanish republic, a time of democracy and hope for the peoples of the spanish state, which was cut short by the fascist uprising of general franco, which led to a forty-year dictatorship whose consequences we are still suffering.
madam president, during this parliamentary term we have adopted legislative initiatives on capital requirements and created a european system of financial supervision. to overcome the crisis, to restore credit and to reap the full benefits of european integration, we must go further. the adoption in this house of the directives for the harmonisation of deposit guarantee schemes and the adoption of a union framework for the resolution of financial institutions is a significant step forward in the process of providing security for depositors and protecting taxpayers against the problems of financial institutions within the union. it is also an essential requirement for the functioning of the banking union, which should break the vicious circle between sovereign and private debt, end the fragmentation of credit and improve the transmission of monetary policy in the euro area. i would like to express my satisfaction that, after the adoption of the single supervisory mechanism, an agreement has been reached in extremis to establish a single resolution mechanism and fund which will enable effective european action, speed up the transition to a single resolution fund and respect parliament's responsibility as a co-legislator. however, i would also like to say that the process of reforming and strengthening the financial system must continue with structural reform, the improvement of the banking union as a single deposit guarantee mechanism and the establishment of a common fiscal safety net. we must continue our efforts because, in the end, banking union will require financial union and fiscal union.
