member of the commission. - mr president, you have listened to me with great patience and i shall not, of course, repeat my arguments. i would simply like to answer some of the questions raised by the previous speakers. first of all, i believe that the proof that the commission which i had the honour of chairing was on the right track is that the criticisms come from both ends of the house and very often in the same tone which reveals a refusal to see, categorically, the difficulties and the extraordinary challenges we have had to face, and the same tendency to give, of course, no coherent answer. the truth is that we have probably experienced the greatest economic and financial crisis since the beginning of our european integration, and that it was not the european union that caused it. it is this truth that some "sovereignists" - to use their expression - do not understand or do not want to understand. europe has not been the cause of excessive private debt and financial irresponsibility. on the contrary, all this has happened under national supervision or lack of it. europe is the answer. we now have one of the most ambitious regulatory and supervisory systems in the world, if not the most ambitious. to say that europe is worse because of the european union is a lie. it shows a complete lack of respect and intellectual rigor. it was not europe that caused the financial crisis, it was the united states that started it. europe was vulnerable, but the european union was only reacting, it was not the cause. and all of us who share the european ideal, whether we are on the right, the left or the centre, must have the courage to say so, otherwise we will reinforce - and this is an advice i give you when i leave office - the populisms of the extreme left or the extreme right. i listened carefully to some of you saying that 'populism is now stronger' and blaming the european union for this. my dear friends, that is not true. populism and xenophobia exist very clearly outside the european union. look what happened in switzerland, against immigrants; look what happened in norway, with this terrorist - a maniac - who killed i don't know how many young people because he is against a multicultural europe; look at the tea party in the united states. is it europe's fault that the tea party exists in the united states? in today's world, there is an aggressive populism, with arguments sometimes from the left, sometimes from the right, and it's hard, i have to admit, to tell the difference. so to say that this is the result of the european union is a lack of intellectual rigor and a lack of political honesty. what we have to do as europeans is to show that europe did not create the crisis, nor did the public debts of the member states. europe can do little when a member state, for example, falsifies its accounts. europe has had to deal with this. the first initiative of my second commission was to ask the member states to give us more powers to supervise national statistics, because in the first commission i chaired this was refused. this was not rejected by greece, it was rejected by the large member states who did not want to give more responsibility to the european union. so if we really want to debate, let us be precise and rigorous in terms of intellectual honesty and political rigor. that's why, dear friends, i won't waste your time. i would like to say something to you with great conviction. the team i have had the honour of chairing has worked - and i see some of you in this parliament now, and they know it - with great dedication and great rigour, always putting the european interest first, and i want to say to you, since we are an assembly of different political forces, always putting the idea of the european common good first. it was not my colleagues from the epp group, the socialists or the liberals who made up my commission, it was men and women who worked for europe. you know what my party is: it is the epp party and i am proud of it. but as president of the commission, my party has been europe. this is a message i would like to share with you, and in particular with the major pro-european forces of the centre-left and centre-right. of course, differences must be expressed, but they must not weaken the european camp. we must not give gifts to the extreme right and the extreme left. we must unite the pro-european forces. they must have the courage to defend europe. they must also do so in the capitals and not just here in strasbourg. we must be able to have this grand coalition for europe because i believe we have enough energy to win the battles of the present and the battle of the future.
por escrito. – el balance de la pasada legislatura no puede ser más negativo. para una mayoría de ciudadanos, europa ha pasado, de identificarse con la idea de solidaridad, a hacerlo con la de sacrificio. la mayoría conservadora ha impuesto un enfoque ideológico frente a la crisis priorizando la reducción de la deuda y el déficit fiscal frente al crecimiento y el empleo. la unión europea es la zona económica mundial con mayor impacto de la crisis sobre el empleo. nos ha costado la pérdida de más de 2,5 millones de empleos. se han disparado desigualdad, pobreza y exclusión social. la austeridad ha fracasado en europa. mientras obama apostó por políticas de estímulo. estados unidos crece y crea más de 8 millones de empleos. ahora, enfrentamos la amenaza de una tercera recesión. pero los promotores de la austeridad siguen apostando por el sufrimiento frente al crecimiento. como resultado, los ciudadanos se alejan de europa porque europa se ha alejado de ellos. y el populismo crece amenazando la idea misma de europa. la nueva comisión tiene la oportunidad y la obligación de corregir el rumbo. probablemente, no habrá otra.
, in writing. the outgoing president of the european commission, josé manuel durão barroso, delivered his farewell speech in the european parliament without even mentioning the unemployment that is affecting europe today, especially countries such as greece and spain. this is the main reflection of a decade in which the european commission, which should have devoted its main efforts to creating jobs and combating the crisis through growth policies and public investment, has been lacking in many areas. however, in recent years the european commission has concentrated its efforts on implementing the prescriptions that the heads of state or government were imposing from the european council, blurring the european commission's capacity for action and reaction. we are now facing an eu which must urgently change course to restore hope to a european dream that has been hijacked by the rise of populism and the far right and by the devastating effects of the crisis and the austerity policies that have led to high unemployment and the impoverishment of european families.
president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european council meeting scheduled for the end of this week will be exceptional in several respects: the european council will be the last meeting of the european council under the first permanent president of the european council, mr van rompuy. and assuming that parliament approves the new commission tomorrow, it will also be the last of the current commission president barroso. but it will also be exceptional in substance: first, the european council is called upon to reach agreement on the 2030 framework for the european union's climate and energy policies. i do not need to remind this house of the importance of this matter. it is in the interest of all of us to develop a coherent european climate and energy policy, which ensures affordable energy prices, industrial competitiveness, security of supply and the achievement of climate and environmental objectives. it is certainly not an easy task, if our overall objective is clear, each member state has its own vision, reflecting a number of factors such as the accessibility of energy sources, their industrial capacity and energy demand and also the different environmental cultures. this means that the negotiations currently under way to prepare for this week's meeting are complex and represent a major challenge, but we all know how essential it is to ensure an ambitious outcome, not least in the light of the role that the european union wants and must play on the international stage as a world leader. the agreement should be global and the key point is the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. the proposal under discussion is an internal emission reduction target of 40% by 2030 compared to 1990 levels. to achieve this, six main chapters have been defined covering the eu-ets emission trade system and non-ets areas, renewable energy sources and energy efficiency, the achievement of a fully functioning internal energy market, energy security and governance. i shall not go into too much detail, as the negotiations are still in progress, and as i speak the general affairs council is discussing these issues in the context of the process of preparing for the european council meeting. the presidency has worked hard to ensure that an agreement is reached. a successful outcome of this european council would allow the european union to present a contribution in line with the agreed timetable of the unefccc in warsaw for the conclusion of a comprehensive climate agreement by the first quarter of 2015. the step our leaders must take is therefore extremely important. in addition to energy and climate issues, the european council is called upon to discuss the economic situation. we know it is fragile and the latest forecasts remind us that we cannot afford any delay. we have managed to overcome the difficulties immediately following the crisis, but now we must boost growth, create jobs and develop competitiveness. only then can we rebuild an appropriate level of confidence in our economies. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, let me conclude by mentioning another extremely important point: the deadly spread of the ebola virus. you discussed this yesterday in the presence of the commission. i don't need to tell you that we are in the middle of a serious crisis. we need a global response both internally and externally, and it was agreed that the european council should take stock of the situation and, above all, highlight the strategic actions needed to bring this deadly virus under control.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i am honoured to be here today to present to you the views of the commission on the european council meeting this week. the summit will seek to agree on the 2030 climate and energy framework and discuss the economy and external developments, including ukraine, and we will also address the ebola epidemic. let me start with a few remarks on the economy. this week’s meeting is not one for decisions in this regard. it will be for the new commission to initiate the new european semester in a few weeks from now. throughout the crisis, yes, our comprehensive response has always been built upon the three pillars of fiscal consolidation, structural reforms and targeted investments. this is still valid today. while economic recovery in the eu is still fragile and uneven, we are seeing that the efforts are paying off. those countries which downturned the most are now better off than those which are lagging behind in addressing the root causes of the crisis. the reforms to european economic governance have been instrumental in making this progress possible. together, we have changed the way that europe’s economies and financial sector are legislated, supervised and regulated. the framework for that has been created. now we need to stick to it and to fully implement it. this is very important for restoring confidence. agreeing a new framework on energy and climate policies for the period up to 2030 at this european council will show how credible we are in transforming our economies and societies towards a low-carbon future. the proposals in our current 2020 framework have been of strategic importance. they have put our union firmly into a position of global leadership and were widely recognised as a key contributor in the global fight against climate change. importantly, we came to these agreements by finding the right mix of ambition and realism. by combining two strands – environment and energy – consensus was possible. there are economic advantages to climate-friendly innovation and investment and an economic case for cost-effective decarbonisation is clearer than ever. we also broadened the scope to include energy security. recent challenges to our security and the strategic dimension have given energy security concerns even more impetus. energy security must therefore be part of the climate agenda. yet sadly our european climate ambition is far from being matched by the two most important polluters globally – the united states and china. public opinion in europe accepted the targets of 20-20-20 by 2020, even if they were aware of the difficulties in implementing them. the eu felt let down when a comprehensive global deal did not happen, despite pressing others to follow suit. but developments afterwards have shown that the union was and remains on the right side of the argument. there is now a renewed momentum towards a global, binding climate treaty to be agreed in paris next year. agreeing on our own 2030 framework now will set the tone; it would provide our union with key leverage in a crucial phase of the international negotiations. the commission’s 2030 proposal from january is the frame of reference for this eu debate. our proposals are clear, ambitious and balanced, with a 40% emission reduction target at their heart. the ball is now in the court of the european council. leaders must assume their responsibility; we expect difficult discussions but we are confident that a decisive deal is within reach now. the third issue to be discussed at the european council is the external situation, in particular the conflict between ukraine and russia. with the unsettled conflict in ukraine we realise more than ever that to defend our values and protect our interests, europe needs to take the lead and be active. we need to continue contributing to a political solution. at the same time, we need to demonstrate that unlawful and uncooperative behaviour brings with it heavy consequences. the situation in ukraine is a clash of world views that touches the very heart of the european union, its principles, its values and what it symbolises: freedom, democracy and rule of law. this is why the eu from the start took a principled position against russia’s illegal annexation of crimea and the destabilisation in ukraine’s eastern region. since then we have done all we could to make the most of a bad situation. the political and peaceful solution of the conflict has always remained our first priority. not any solution, but one that guaranteed the sovereignty, independence and unity of ukraine. our relations with our eastern neighbours are not detrimental to relations with the other neighbours. we never sought exclusivity in our relations. in fact, the european union has invested a lot in the strategic partnership with the russian federation, convinced that it is in our common interest to cooperate. developments are still unfolding. the european union continues to work for a politically negotiated solution. the commission has made every effort in this regard by taking the lead in promoting trilateral talks on sensitive issues such as trade and energy. just today, the commission is mediating another round of talks on the gas issue. on the security front, priority needs to be given to full implementation of the minsk agreements. this is the basis for restoring and consolidating trust. the ceasefire needs to be respected and verified. elections in the donbas need to be held in accordance with ukrainian law and the border needs to be controlled and monitored. we cannot give up on ukraine. we cannot give up on reaching a solution. if we do not reach a solution, what would be at risk would be both ukraine’s independence and also the security, stability and unity of the european continent. we must defend the credibility of a multilateral order based on values, equality and the rule of law. at the same time, we are greatly concerned by the humanitarian and security situation in syria and iraq. it is deteriorating dramatically day by day. the rapid progression of isil is alarming. military action in line with international law is necessary, but it is not enough. it needs to be part of the wider effort, comprising measures in the political and diplomatic, counter-terrorism and terrorism funding, humanitarian and communication fields. the commission has been active on the humanitarian part. to date, around eur 2.9 billion has been mobilised to those in need in syria and iraq, but the security situation impacts negatively the delivery of aid. while military intervention will be the key to defeating isil, it is imperative not to link the delivery of humanitarian aid to military objectives. humanitarian access should not be put at risk. unfortunately, there is yet another crisis which the european council will have to address, and this is ebola. the ebola outbreak is not just a problem for west africa; it is a challenge for the international community as a whole and europe has a responsibility to do its part. the commission and the member states have provided assistance to the countries affected and to the humanitarian effort on the ground – more than eur 600 million already, and it is not just money. twelve member states are providing medical and other equipment through the eu civil protection mechanism. but we need to do more to help the affected african countries and also protect our own citizens. the commission discussed this issue at todayʼs college, and will feed into a discussion at the european council. this week’s european council will cover very telling issues as far as the need for european union unity is concerned: what the european union is for; what it should do and what challenges it faces. i look forward to hearing your views here today on how we can work together to tackle these challenges. it is with this spirit of cooperation and with the crucial support of this house that europe must be successful in coping with today’s and tomorrow’s challenges.
i would like to thank the president-in-office of the council for his excellent report, which has been very well received by the house. but if we want to turn that around, we have to look at the data of reality and not remain blind to all the alarms that are being set off. we should listen to the flood of analyses and recommendations from experts and think tanks and not remain deaf to this analytical coincidence, and we should abandon insensibility to the social consequences of the policies that have been put in place. if we look at the data, we see that the latest oecd and international monetary fund reports agree that the growth prospects in the european union in 2014 and 2015 are not optimistic at all; any prospects are worse than what has happened before. we also see that, at best, we are in an economic slump and, at worst, we are entering a third recession. but the middle scenario is stagnation, what the imf has called "secular stagnation". if we talk about inflation, we see that the best hypothesis is low deflation, and the worst hypothesis is clear deflation, and that either of these limits our chances of reducing the deficit and increasing growth. at the same time, we have not been able to reduce the level of unemployment either. in view of this situation, analyses by the imf, the oecd, think tanks and the german institute for economic studies itself point out that what is happening to us is a consequence of the policies we have been implementing. what can be done about this? the new commission must take advantage of this situation to launch the €300 billion programme of public and private funds to stimulate growth and employment. where to do it? the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar energy, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of renewable energy sources. parliament has always been more ambitious than the commission in this respect, and the socialist group more than parliament as a whole. so, cheers to the new commission! try to put in place a new economic, environmental, sustainable policy in the european union.
in writing. the ec will decide on the 2030 climate and energy targets. juncker called for a 'green europe, a leader in renewable energy' and now we have to make it happen. the ep set out its position in february 2014 and, although the s$d group was more ambitious, we must not lower the ep's approved demands (30% on renewables, binding on member states; savings and efficiency -40% binding and -40% emissions) to improve the competitiveness of the european economy, to preserve the environment and to secure energy supply. this requires progress in the unification of the energy market in europe, with the development of interconnections being crucial, an objective which has been 'lagging' because of the lack of political will to allow the existence of energy islands, such as the iberian peninsula, which can play a relevant role in the supply of gas to the rest of europe, as well as in the development of renewable energies.
president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, it is a pleasure and an honour for me to be taking part once again in a sitting of the european parliament, which has on its agenda items relating to the community budget. specifically, the subject we are now dealing with concerns first of all the draft amending budget no 2 for 2014, already approved by the council at its meeting of 14 july 2014. as you know, this budget is part of a procedure which is precisely codified in the financial regulation, which, once the result of the previous financial year has been defined, requires the adoption of the necessary budgetary changes for the current year. in line with the forecasts in the financial regulation, the commission therefore proposed to book in 2014 the surplus of around eur 1 billion recorded in the 2013 budget. we note that the european parliament is about to approve amendments to this purely technical budget, providing for a new budget line on which to set aside this amount pending its use for unforeseen payments. this approach - as we have been told very clearly - is reflected in the more general discussions we are having on the 2014 amending budgets and the draft budget for 2015. it goes without saying that the amendment proposal itself cannot be accepted by the council, but it will obviously be taken into account in the more comprehensive debate we will have in the conciliation procedure, and i am sure that in this context we will be able to strike the right balance for a decision which meets the needs of the various parties in accordance with the rules laid down by the legislation in force.
member of the commission. - madam president, the commission proposal for this draft amending budget was tabled in april 2014, in accordance with the article 18 of the financial regulation. it concerns the budgeting of the 2013 surplus. as pointed out by the rapporteur, mr deprez, the amount of the surplus is one billion, five million euros, and it mostly comes from the additional revenue from competition fines received towards the end of 2013. only a very small part of the 2013 surplus – somewhere in the region of eur 275 million out of an executed budget of almost eur 144 billion – comes from the expenditure side of the budget. at the same time, the commission has also presented amending budgets requesting additional expenditure of eur 4.7 billion since the end of last may. last year, the reinforcement of payments in amending budgets 2 and 8 of 2013, totalling eur 11.2 billion, had been fully used by the end of 2013. this year again, the situation of payment is tight; it started with a backlog of eur 23.4 billion. we simply have no possibilities for redeployment, and several budget lines have been fully exhausted. overall implementation stands at the level of 82%. it is in light of this scarcity of payments across the budget that the commission understands the amendments proposed by the parliament to create a reserve for payments in the 2014 budget with the same amount as the surplus. out of the seven amending budgets, six are still outstanding. two of them concern the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund. together with the council, we will need to find a compromise on all draft amending budgets on the table – including the three for this year – which reinforces payments amounting to eur 4.7 billion. the commission considers that all of the elements needed to do so quickly are available. this year, we have a unique opportunity to cover the additional expenditure with the revenue mainly coming from funds. this means that we can cover it at no cost to member states’ budgets. taking this decision will only increase the eu’s credibility and allow us to gain control over the eu budget. i invite members to act responsibly and to take the appropriate decisions in the forthcoming conciliation.
i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations. it is true that the agenda includes the second amending budget, but it is clear that what is on the table and at the heart of the debate we are having at the moment in the committee on budgets and in the european parliament is how we solve the payment crisis that we have been dragging on since 2010. i have the impression that when we talk about payments we often repeat the obvious, but it seems that the council's position is not so clear on this point; so we must continue to repeat the obvious and be patient to see if we can get the council to change its position once and for all. and the first obvious thing, which we keep repeating in this parliament, is that we have to pay what we owe. i think it is quite simple to explain to our citizens that in the european union, the council, the commission and parliament we have taken decisions and reached agreements; that many companies, ngos, public institutions, private institutions and universities have trusted in the proposals we have made, have participated in european programmes and now all we have to do is simply pay the invoices they have sent us in relation to those agreements we have reached with them. and so this is an obvious fact which we shall be tired of repeating, but which it seems that some countries, at least in the council, are not so clear. that is an unacceptable situation. we cannot continue to delay the settlement of the arrears. we have been discussing this problem since 2010 and the situation is becoming more and more worrying, until we reach some 26 or 30 billion euros, because we do not even know what figure we are talking about anymore. and i will say two more obvious things: firstly, not paying is not respecting those agreements we have reached. and secondly, by not paying, we are also not respecting the agreement on the financial framework, and what we are really doing is cutting the budget through the back door. as the commission has told you, you have a golden opportunity, it will not cost you a single euro to reduce these defaults by at least five billion euros. take advantage of the opportunity!
member of the commission. - madam president, to sum up this whole discussion, it is clearly this: eu credibility is at stake and there is no question to answer; we have to fulfil our obligations. we have a unique situation: to solve the problem at no expense to the member states. that is a really unique situation as far as i know; it has never happened in the past. the commission has this money, it is on the account – eur 5 billion. legally, we are not able to use it; we have to give it back to the member states. so now, the reply awaited from the council is whether the council and the member states prefer to put this money in their own pockets and ignore the commitments they have made in the past, and ignore the payments they have to make, or do they want to really address the problem, show their european will and pay the bills? member of the commission. - madam president, i was thinking about what to say now, but i think there is one issue that we have to clarify from the very beginning about this amending letter no 1 to the budget 2015. it is not true that this letter consists of cuts of any kind to direct payments. the crisis reserve is established by law on an annual basis by simple application of financial discipline. this crisis reserve was created to solve crisis problems in agriculture and that is what is being proposed by the commission: to apply the crisis reserve to the crisis situation. however, it does not have a direct impact on the level of direct payments for farmers. as you know, heading 2 for agriculture is one of the biggest in the eu budget. it consists of almost eur 45 billion. at the end of every budgetary year, calculations are done to see how much is left in additional revenues after fulfilling all the obligations to the farmers. when you look at the history of this heading in the past there were savings in every annual budget – savings amounting to at least half a billion euro, sometimes even a billion. this money was usually used to top up any direct payments that were legally eligible. so this will also be the case in 2015. what the commission has proposed in the amending letter is simply to improve the liquidity of the eu budget due to the scarce resources for payments. the only impact it will have is that some headings will have additional payment appropriations available at the beginning of the year when they are most needed, but it does not create any additional restrictions to heading 2. this amending letter does not change either the level of commitments under heading 2 or the level of payments available under heading 2. so what many of you have indicated – that the commissionʼs decision immediately reduces direct payments to farmers – is not true. you will see the result by the end of the year. we have produced the same type of amending letters every year in the past and it has never created such tensions. the same instruments were applied in every eu budget. the additional revenues that were indicated in heading 2 were transferred to all other headings on an annual basis because farmers are not able to use more money and resources than they are eligible for. heading 2 has the biggest margins of all headings. so we should not really concentrate too much on this situation. i can assure you that the amending letter does not create any reductions in direct payments for farmers and it does not have any direct influence on the level of direct payments that the farmers will have received by the end of the year. if i may make a few comments concerning the budget for 2015 as such. we have to remember that the eu annual budget is just an implementation of commitments taken previously in the mff; so if someone is arguing about why we spend money, we spend money because that was what was promised by member states. the commission is simply asking, or first indicating in its draft budget, how much money we need for a particular year – taking into account the commitments that were made by member states and taking into account the fact that 90% of the eu budget is spent in the member states by the member states – and not the commission, as we have to remember. it is not the commission that is trying to find new ways of spending money. ninety per cent of the budget is decided by member states. they have the projects to be financed and decided domestically. they launch the projects, they spend the money and they send the bills to the commission to be refunded. so the commission’s role is only to collect this information and then present to both arms of the budgetary authority how much money we need to fulfil their obligations or to refund money they have spent. so this whole process of discussion now as to whether we should cut more or less is actually about whether we should fulfil our obligations or not, whether we want to pay our bills back or not. that is the whole debate we are having here now.

president of the council. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this debate, in which the council has been invited to speak, concerns democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in hungary. the council is aware of the concerns expressed by certain groups in parliament on this subject. although it did not discuss the matter in detail, no proposal to invoke a procedure involving the council on this subject having been received. i want to be clear on the general themes of the issue: the european parliament has always been a party to the treaty of rome, and it has always been a party to the treaty of rome. if these values are part of the very raison d'être of the european union and the basis of our being together, all european institutions and member states are called upon to work to ensure that full respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law are always guaranteed. i know that this house fully shares that position. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the fundamental rights of the member states are enshrined in the constitutional traditions of the member states, in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and in the european convention on human rights, to which all the member states of the european union are parties and to which the european union itself will accede in due course. all member states must therefore ensure that their national law, whether primary or secondary, respects eu law. if there are any doubts or misgivings in this respect, it is the commission's responsibility to deal with them first and foremost, not the council's. i can assure you, however, that i shall pay close attention to what you have to say on this subject in the course of this debate. these are certainly useful considerations for the italian presidency, which is considering in these very days, on the basis of the commission's communication of 11 march, the possibility of holding a debate in the council on strengthening the rule of law in the union.
member of the commission. - madam president, as guardian of the treaties, the commission enforces the law of the european union, including the charter of fundamental rights, through infringement procedures, under the supervision of the court of justice of the union and, of course, in complementarity with the role of the national courts which work with the court of justice of the union to enforce the rights guaranteed by the charter in the member states. the commission's role is not limited to ensuring the protection of fundamental rights in the application of union law. the commission has also made a political commitment to protect the union's values. to this end, in march 2014 it adopted its communication on a new eu framework to strengthen the rule of law. the communication has the dual purpose of ensuring equal treatment between member states and promoting political dialogue in the event of a threat to our common values. in the event of a systemic threat to the rule of law in a member state, the commission plans to enter into a political dialogue with it. this dialogue must be based on loyal cooperation and must allow solutions to be found before the situation worsens. this process is in place to fill the gap that has existed until now between infringement procedures and the use of article 7 mechanisms. the framework for strengthening the rule of law will seek to ensure the proper functioning of all judicial and constitutional mechanisms and guarantees aimed at protecting democracy and fundamental rights in the member states. if these guarantees are jeopardised, the commission will not hesitate to take the necessary measures to ensure that union law and values are respected. the commission shall act within the limits of its powers as conferred by the treaties. on the other hand, it will not hesitate, if necessary, to launch infringement procedures for breaches of eu law and to initiate a political dialogue with the member state whose national mechanisms to ensure the rule of law are seriously compromised, whatever that member state may be. the european union framework for strengthening the rule of law applies to all member states in the same way. our debate today, madam president, is about the rule of law in hungary. in recent weeks, there has been a disagreement between the hungarian and norwegian authorities on the issue of granting subsidies to certain ngos. in the light of the information available at this stage, the subject matter of this dispute does not appear to fall within the scope of european union law. the management of union funds is not directly involved in this dispute. in addition, we have no evidence at this stage of a malfunctioning of the national mechanisms for the protection of the rule of law, nor of a malfunctioning of the hungarian judicial system. the ngos concerned have the possibility of appealing against the decisions taken. the commission has, however, used all its political weight to encourage the parties to settle this dispute and we are following this process closely. let me now return to the hungarian media legislation. in 2011, the commission services indicated that several provisions of this law were not in line with the provisions of the audiovisual media services directive, the treatment on the functioning of the european union and the charter of fundamental rights. following exchanges initiated by the commission, hungary adopted amendments in 2011 and 2012 to correct the highlighted points. the amendments now ensure that hungarian law is in conformity with union law. the compatibility of the new hungarian legislation on the tax on advertising revenue generated in the media with union law is under examination. the impact of this tax on freedom of expression and its compatibility with the freedom of establishment guaranteed by the treaties remains to be assessed. we are looking into this situation and are continuing to dialogue with the hungarian authorities. the commission has also proposed that the hungarian authorities should be given the opportunity to present their observations on the application of the new legislation. if this were not the case, the commission would of course not hesitate to use its powers in infringement proceedings. i would also like to inform you of the outcome of the case concerning the independence of the hungarian national data protection authority. following the judgment of the court of 8 april 2014, the hungarian authorities acknowledged the breach of union law and fully compensated the national commissioner responsible for the authority, who did not indicate his intention to resume his duties. in these circumstances, the commission closed the infringement procedure. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, tonight's debate is an opportunity to remind ourselves that what makes us feel european is our attachment to this community of values, principles and law enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights. the commission, as guardian of the treaties, has the duty to ensure that they are respected, whether the member states are large or small, whether they are founding member states or not. this is the guarantee provided by the new framework of the european union to strengthen the rule of law.

mr president, on behalf of the ppe it is with great respect that i salute the new commission and i hope that all of us here in the plenary will afterwards vote for this commission. it has been a long road map since we started this. this is an elected commission; this is different and many of us believe that we will now have a political future and that we are going to respond to the citizens. this is the commission we want. we will support you in your initiatives, in all the priorities that we all share here. i know that some of you do not, but you will feel how this is going to change the future and the unity of this european union. this is starting today and i feel proud from the ppe family, from all my colleagues and also for those who are going to vote in favour of this new commission and this new era under jean-claude juncker.
in writing. i voted for the juncker commission in the context of a broad agreement between the epp, s&d and the liberals. this is a much more political commission with much more potential than the previous ones, and it would have been irresponsible for parliament to weaken it before it began its mandate, because to weaken the commission is to strengthen the role of the states. the college of commissioners has emerged strengthened from the hearings, where they have demonstrated their independence and worthiness for office in an exercise of democratic and transparent scrutiny. the great political pact between the epp, s&d and the liberals is very positive and hopeful, given that the european parliament has been set up in such a way that neither the epp nor the s&d can articulate alternative majorities in the house. this shows that the two major parties must be able to reach agreements on those matters of general interest to the eu. i am convinced that the path of dialogue and agreement will be very positive for the legislature that has just begun and which can lay the transversal foundations on which to build the european union of the future.

in writing. - it is not the first time that i have taken a stand against free trade agreements, since trade deregulation is just another way for strong economies to penetrate new markets at the cost of the progressive dismantling of weaker production systems, thus increasing inequalities and asymmetries between countries and putting workers from different geographical areas in competition and subjecting the peasantry on both sides to unfair competition from industrial agriculture and agro-export businesses. the circulation of a huge amount of goods, including food that we eat every day and that we might find nearby, leads to a very large increase in greenhouse gas emissions, which further aggravates the climate crisis. although this report is purely technical, as it is a component of the process of ratification of the additional protocol of accession of croatia to the eu, i have not voted in favour of it for the reasons set out above.
in writing. - any agreement to facilitate business exchange is positive for european companies, and in a context of economic crisis still more, since exports are very important to maintain the growth of the european economy. moreover, the internal market is one of the best treasures of the european union. it has brought economic growth, prosperity and better life quality to the countries that are in it, so it is a great pleasure to welcome croatia in it. that is why i have supported this protocol, because it contributes to safeguarding the integrity of the union’s internal market and facilitates exports in asia.

in writing. - this report analyses the implementation of the european semester in the last semester and makes recommendations for the next, which will start once the european commission publishes its annual growth survey in november. the report is full of rhetoric about socially balanced and sustainable growth, calls for job creation and the fight against youth unemployment to make people believe that we are on the path to the new cycle. but the reality is that the european semester confirms the austerity policies which have destroyed millions of jobs and gives a free hand to continue down the same path. that is why i have obviously voted against.
in writing. - the current european economic context calls for greater coordination of macroeconomic and budgetary policies. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the internal market must also be strengthened, in particular the free movement of services; making this a reality and fully operational would be a stimulus for the economy. while signs of recovery have been shown, further stimulus is needed to achieve stabilisation in the medium term. in this context, the important role of the eu budget in stimulating sustainable growth, boosting job creation and reducing macroeconomic imbalances in the eu should be underlined. the youth guarantee and the eu youth employment initiative should be promoted as useful means to combat the high rate of youth unemployment. a sound budgetary policy, a real free movement of services that protects the consumer and benefits smes, and the implementation of programmes to combat unemployment are key stimuli for moving towards a stronger economic and monetary policy.

member of the commission. - this is indeed a very serious phenomenon that we are debating here today. it is a serious threat to the european union, and we saw what happened in brussels only half a year ago when a returning foreign fighter opened fire in the jewish museum in brussels and killed four people. we need to step up our efforts to stem the flow of foreign fighters and we need to work together in the european union. first of all, we need to ensure better information exchanges between the member states, notably by establishing appropriate mechanisms. one such mechanism is the passenger name record data that the council mentioned. pnr data could be an essential tool to carry out trend pattern analyses, identifying potentially high-risk travellers. this enables the authorities to better detect those foreign fighters travelling to and from the eu by air that were previously unknown to law enforcement agencies. pnr is also a very important tool to detect traffickers and drug smugglers. of course, an eu pnr needs a clear legal framework and coherent data protection safeguards across the eu in line with article 8 of the charter, as interpreted by the european court of justice. eu legislation must lay down clear and precise rules governing the scope and the application of the measures, and imposing appropriate safeguards so that the persons whose pnr data has been retained have sufficient guarantees to protect their personal data against the risk of abuse and any unlawful access or use of that data. i really hope that the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs can look at this again. as you know, member state after member state is developing its own pnr system, and it would be much better to have a joint system with common rules, not least when it comes to data protection. another strand of action is the detection of returnees from conflict zones to europe, and therefore issues of border security and border management play a role here. the schengen information system (sis) is an effective tool for the detection and disruption of suspicious travel by sharing information about foreign fighters. it allows today for specific action to be taken on the basis of alerts. the commission is making efforts to accelerate and improve the information exchange on sis alerts among member states, and it is crucial that member states use all the possibilities offered by the system today. it is also important that member states carry out minimum checks on persons as required by the schengen border code and systematically check the travel documents of all persons at external borders against the relevant databases. there are voices calling for a revision of the existing framework on this, but it is important to first look at how we can use in an optimal way the existing tools and measures and make the best of them. the situation is urgent and the commission is, of course, looking at technical discussions, but for the moment we do not plan any initiatives in this area. you must also understand that the commission reserves its position until the next commission is in place. looking forward, aviation security capacity-building in third countries is a priority. the commission stands ready to support work in this field highlighted by the european council in august. we will continue our work on detection technologies to make sure that our own aviation security is as strong as it has to be. a very important strand here not to be forgotten, because it is key, is preventive work. we need to address, as the council mentioned, terrorists’ use of the internet. we know that many of these organisations recruit via the internet. that is why we have started a dialogue with internet providers to see if we can cooperate in developing counter-narratives online and in cooperation, for instance, with returned people who can tell their stories. as you know, we also created three years ago the radicalisation awareness network. it plays a very important role in helping local actors and member states to improve the tools and understand the root causes of radicalisation. we have networks working in all member states with families and victims to draft counter-narratives, to pool the research, and we are working on exit strategies and will very soon be setting up a sort of centre of excellence that will be at the disposal of member states for all this. at this point i would like to reiterate that security and fundamental rights are intrinsically related here. combatting racist and xenophobic crime, intolerance, discrimination, including promoting integration and social cohesion, is a key element of eu policies. it is very important not to stigmatise any group here. we will also do everything to give priority to the enforcement of the framework decision on combatting racism and xenophobia by means of criminal laws. honourable members, member states are meeting a lot to discuss these issues. the commission is trying to be helpful, creating forums for the exchange of information. we need to step up our action here to combat this dangerous phenomenon of foreign fighters. we should use the existing tools at our disposal to the maximum extent made possible by border measures and national databases. we must also facilitate and promote european action, for instance a european pnr would be important here. we need to reinforce and spread the very important preventive work that has already been going on for a couple of years. this is the only way that we can jointly address this threat.

such operation organised by successive presidencies since the launch of operation hermes under the belgian presidency in october 2010. mos maiorum was prepared on the basis of the guidelines contained in the 2010 police joint operations guide. the purpose of the guide was to implement the stockholm programme, which, as we know, was partly intended to improve security within the european union and to combat organised crime. the main objective of 'mos maiorum' is to collect information from the participating member states and schengen associated countries in order to undermine the ability of organised crime to facilitate illegal immigration to the european union. the aim of 'mos maiorum' is to identify the modus operandi used by criminal networks to smuggle their victims into the territory of the european union and to identify the link between the illegal crossing of the external borders of the european union and illegal migration within the schengen area. these objectives can be better achieved by exchanging relevant data at eu level and introducing a more efficient and comprehensive information sharing model. the implementation of this joint operation shall not imply any departure for the participating states from any aspect of the eu acquis relating to migration flows and the guarantees it provides to the persons concerned. likewise, the operation has no negative effect on the reception capacity of italy or any other participating state. furthermore, the rules of conduct of the operation clearly provide that all relevant activities are to be carried out with full respect for human dignity and human rights, with due regard to vulnerable groups. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that this brief presentation has helped to clarify the context of the operation, which is designed to dismantle illegal criminal networks seeking economic profit by putting the lives of innocent people at risk. thank you for your attention.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, as enshrined in roman law, the mos maiorum is the custom of the ancestors, a symbol of moral integrity and a set of rules and precepts which the roman citizen had to respect. europe has been a defender of the rule of law since its origins and must remain so. immigration should be a matter of state, regardless of ideology or government. the 'mos maiorum' operation, coordinated by the italian ministry of the interior and open to the voluntary participation of all member states and schengen partners, should pursue a number of objectives already referred to by the presidency of the council, but mainly identify, pursue and disrupt organised crime groups; detect irregular migrants and gather relevant information for investigative and intelligence purposes; provide a clear and up-to-date picture of the situation in relation to human trafficking operations, their modus operandi, the main trends and possible changes they may undergo, and develop joint actions to have an impact on irregular immigration, especially in relation to border controls and border surveillance activities. in my view, 'mos maiorum' should be understood neither as a persecution nor as a mass roundup of irregular immigrants, but as a real persecution against the mafias that traffic in human beings. protocols and actions must be produced which can be applied regardless of the political moment and with a continuity which ensures their success. this continuity in border control policy can be seen in the fact that the template that the italians will use to report on the operational results achieved is similar, if not the same, as that already used in previous operations: the belgian one, in october 2010; the hungarian mitras, in april 2011; the balder of denmark, in april 2012; aphrodite and perkunas, of cyprus, in october 2013. all these operations have naturally been based on respect for human rights. europe is a territory in which the rule of law must prevail. we must be concerned about preventing deaths and abuses at our borders and, in turn, facilitating the entry and legal defense of those who need our protection. this is why it is important to develop joint and transversal actions at european level and in the member states, as well as with countries of origin and transit. we must develop the ambitious proposals contained in the smart borders package and even consider, mr president, definitively, the reform and strengthening of frontex's capacities.

mr president, on 3 november a police officer was testifying in valencia, in the spanish state, accused of a lack of aggression against algerian minors. the juveniles couldn't testify because they'd already been expelled, so it'll be difficult for the trial to be held with guarantees. it is one more case of the many reported in the so-called centers of internment of foreigners, places of shame, where those who commit the administrative fault of not having their papers in order can be detained for up to 60 days. these are illegal prisons where people are crowded into, deprived of their most basic rights. in the spanish state there are seven, with 9,000 prisoners, more than six per cell, much worse than in any prison. in europe there are a total of 280. the report is a good one, but it is not enough. is this the europe of human rights we boast about? do we want to convince the world of the goodness of our democracy? with a lake like this in our territory, colleagues, that is impossible. the detention centers for foreigners must be closed now. they are our shame, the great shame of europe, and we cannot tolerate them any longer.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this association agreement - on which i express my support and solidarity with the president of the moldovan parliament here - will obviously not lead to a collapse in production, in agri-food markets or in the agricultural sector of the european union. moldova is a country with small production. but i do want to take this opportunity to send a message to the commission and the commissioner who is here and who is working on this agreement. i would like to say that there is a need for greater coherence and coordination between this association agreement and the agricultural policy and the european agri-food system. once again, imports of products are used, in this case fruit and vegetables. as i have said, there will be no breakdown, but there is a need, commissioner, for greater coherence and coordination in the policies pursued by the college of commissioners.
mr president, i think the first thing we have to take into account here is that we are holding a debate for the elites. there is a lot of talk here about the moldovan people, but i have not seen any reports on the impact of this agreement on the people: on the moldovan people and on the various peoples of the european union. and this seems very irresponsible to me. because i also want to say to the moldovan people and to the people of europe that this neoliberal model that we know in europe has meant the destruction of the peasantry to unimaginable levels, with the occupation of our local markets by european agribusinesses; the destruction of small and mediumsized enterprises; the relocation of production and of the enterprises themselves. and now the people of the south are experiencing hunger, which was eradicated; we are experiencing poverty and social exclusion; we are experiencing destruction, the expulsion of thousands of families from their homes; and now it is also going to our public health, education systems. that's the reality we know... member of the commission. - mr president, i would like to thank the members of this parliament for their interest and overwhelming support, and for their determination. our discussion has confirmed that we agree on the need to continue strongly supporting the republic of moldova moving closer to the european union. at the same time, we need to send clear messages on the need to enhance reform efforts after the elections. we will now focus on the thorough implementation of the agreement, which contains a very ambitious reform agenda. the full benefits of the agreement will only be available to the moldovan people if we pursue these paths. it is moreover clear that the european union will stand by moldova in the present difficult regional situation. successfully implemented reforms will make moldova less vulnerable to external pressure. i also want to reiterate the union’s support for a solution to the transnistrian conflict within the framework of the 5+2 talks, respecting moldova’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally-recognised borders, and the special status of transnistria. in response to several speakers: the eu through its projects supports all minorities and regions mentioned today. i was asked by mr marinho e pinto about how we control and audit the projects. i think it is important to recall that it is about bilateral funding, which is transferred to moldova through budget support. payments are made by the commission only against delivery of concrete results agreed bilaterally between the government of moldova and the european union. as it plays an important role in the moldovan economy and today’s debate, some clarifications concerning wine. it is indeed highly regrettable, i have to say, that russia has stopped importing a whole range of agricultural products, not only wine, for purely political reasons, because if it comes to the quality of the wine it is an outstanding one. but your information that the union is not allowing imports of wine is wrong. in fact it does so, both under the current autonomous trade preference, and now also under the new dcfta. in fact the dcfta tariff-free quota has been doubled for exports. finally, moldova is a key country of the european union’s eastern partnership. moldova has shown significant political will in the past to achieve remarkable results in our cooperation. a positive track record of implementing the association agreement with our support will also be the best way for moldova to prepare for any future endeavours it might envisage in its cooperation with the european union.

in writing. - on the recommendation of the juri committee of this parliament, i voted against the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of ms ana gomes requested by the deputy prosecutor-general of the portuguese republic in relation to allegedly defamatory statements made by the member in a televised debate. article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the eu guarantees that opinions expressed by a member of the european parliament enjoy immunity when they have been expressed in the exercise of parliamentary functions. there is no doubt that there is a direct and obvious link between the opinion delivered by ana gomes and her duties as a member of the european parliament. suspending the immunity of ms gomes for the statements in question would restrict her freedom in the exercise of her parliamentary functions and would be manifestly contrary to the purpose of article 8 of the protocol.

in writing. - it is not the first time that i have taken a stand against free trade agreements, since trade deregulation is one more way for strong economies to enter new markets at the cost of the progressive dismantling of weaker production systems, thus increasing inequalities and asymmetries between countries and putting workers and peasants from different geographical areas in competition. it is an agreement for the economic elites; the debate conceals how the european model destroys the peasantry, how peasant products are displaced from local markets by those of agro-exporting businesses. the destruction of smes, the relocation of production and businesses, and the dismantling and privatisation of health and education in the southern european union are also being covered up. it is not an agreement to benefit the populations, it is an agreement to favour the interests of capital.
in writing. – i agree that this agreement is not an end in itself but only the beginning of a closer relationship with the eu. as we have witnessed recently in ukraine, we need stronger political and economic ties with our ring and now with the eastern one. by doing this, we will bring greater stability and prosperity to the whole european continent, not only the eu. as well, this kind of agreement is based on common values in terms of human rights, fundamental freedoms and the rule of law.
in writing. - it is not the first time that i have taken a stand against free trade agreements, since trade deregulation is one more way for strong economies to enter new markets at the cost of the progressive dismantling of weaker production systems, thus increasing inequalities and asymmetries between countries and putting workers from different geographical areas in competition. in return, moldova is required to reform key sectors such as justice, energy and other public sectors to bring them closer to the eu acquis in return for free markets. i think it is an act of interference by the eu in moldova, especially since two thirds of the population have spoken out against this association agreement. i have therefore voted against.
mr president, i would like to use this explanation of vote to point out that the spanish delegation of the ppe has voted against the northern ireland peace process report for a number of reasons. we consider that the absence in this report of any mention of the victims of terrorism and the rejection of the oral amendment tabled, which rightly sought to avoid cases of impunity, are sufficient reasons to vote against this report. but i would also remind you, mr president, that in the debate last night there were comments which drew a parallel between northern ireland and the basque country. i would remind you that there was an armed conflict in northern ireland between two parties. in the basque country there has only been and there is an armed conflict on one side, that of the murderous eta terrorists who have killed hundreds of innocent victims; and that, unfortunately, that terrorist gang, as we all know, is still active, refusing to abandon and hand over weapons, refusing to collaborate in solving more than 300 murders that have not been solved and refusing to disappear immediately from the face of the earth.
mr president, i am basque and my father lived in the basque country. my father was threatened with death for not paying the blackmail of the terrorist gang. my father was not part of the conflict, so i cannot accept that it is proposed that this can be the case in northern ireland, the example for the resolution of other conflicts. firstly, this resolution has been cooked up in an undemocratic way, without giving us any option to make any amendments. if only the oral amendment by mrs pagazaurtundúa, whose brother was killed for dissent - and he was not part of any conflict - had been adopted, we would have approved the amendment. there are three points which we do not accept: there is no mention of the victims, there is no equal treatment of murderers and murdered, and there is no justice for crimes. consequently, recital d, which states that there must be equal treatment, considers in parity and mutual respect - look at you, between murderers and murdered, none. because in the basque country there has been no inter-communal conflict, but people who did not think like the terrorists and were killed.
in writing. - it is undeniable that the progress achieved to date in the northern ireland peace process is a remarkable and positive example of conflict resolution, based on collaboration, consent and the principles of equal treatment and mutual consideration and respect, which has had a beneficial impact not only on political relations in northern ireland but also beyond it. we are, however, concerned that the peace process has come to a standstill. i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls on all parties to the process to work constructively towards a lasting solution to the conflict and the full implementation of the good friday agreement and subsequent agreements, in the interests of a lasting peace.
in writing. - since the good friday agreement was signed in 1998, the peace process has made successful progress in northern ireland, to the point where it has achieved remarkable economic results and has become an example of conflict resolution at international level. the involvement of various international actors, including the european union through the international fund for ireland, has undoubtedly contributed to this. however, the current state of stagnation in the peace process is a matter of grave concern and it is necessary that all parties return to the table to give a new impetus to the dialogue in order to consolidate the progress achieved, promote reconciliation and build a peaceful society that will eradicate violence once and for all. to that end, i welcome the european parliament's offer to help the parties in the objective of advancing the peace process and ensuring coexistence in peace and freedom. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - it is a joint resolution on the peace process in northern ireland, promoted by the british delegations to the european parliament. the resolution assessed very positively the progress achieved to date, but also:1. expresses concern that the peace process has reached a stalemate and urges all parties to the process to work constructively towards a lasting solution to the conflict, as well as the full implementation of the good friday agreement and subsequent agreements, in the interests of a lasting peace;2. the initiative to open talks between all parties to overcome the current stalemate is welcomed;3. welcomes the appointment of senator gary hart by john kerry, secretary of state of the united states of america, as his personal envoy; expresses concern at the continuing violent criminal acts undermining the peace process; and5. the eu's support for promoting reconciliation, in particular the work of the task force on northern ireland set up by the ec, the development of the peace programme and the unconditional support of the ep, is highlighted.

in the light of the recent events in cyprus, the commission has decided to withdraw its proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of cyprus, of the other part. the republic of cyprus has the full and sovereign right to exploit the natural resources within its eez. the actions of turkey within the eez of the republic of cyprus are in breach of international law and further undermine the continuation of negotiations for a comprehensive solution to the cyprus problem. as a candidate country for eu accession, turkey should respect the declaration of the european community and its member states of 21 september 2005, including the provision that recognition by all member states is a necessary element of the accession process. it must therefore avoid hostile action against any member state in particular and respect the sovereignty of the latter over its territorial waters. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - the european parliament's socialist motion for a resolution deplores the escalation of threats and unilateral actions by turkey against the republic of cyprus in relation to the eez but considers that the exploration of the natural resources by the republic of cyprus in its eez should not contradict or impede the negotiations on the reunification of the island. in this respect, it is noted that any oil and gas development should be carried out for the benefit of all cypriots. the document calls on all parties to act responsibly and constructively to resolve the crisis and in this regard urges turkey to withdraw its warships immediately from cypriot waters in order to reduce tension and facilitate the resumption of negotiations. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. on 3 october 2014, turkey issued a maritime directive (navtex, navigational telex) by which it unlawfully 'designated' a large area located in the southern part of the exclusive economic zone (eez) of the republic of cyprus, almost adjacent to the territorial waters of the republic of cyprus, as a reserved area for seismic surveys from 20 october to 30 december 2014, in contravention of the united nations convention on the law of the sea. the threats of turkey, a candidate country for eu membership, against cyprus, an eu member state, which have been materialized in the movement of turkish ships and which involve an unnecessary increase in tension in the region, are threats to the eu as a whole. the high representative should demand an end to the turkish occupation of cyprus and condemn ankara's continued violations of international law under the threat of freezing bilateral relations, including accession negotiations.

in writing. - the self-proclaimed independence of south sudan does not seem to have had the intended effects on the sudanese population. fundamental issues such as the demarcation of borders, the sharing of oil revenues and the use of the northern pipeline remain unresolved. significantly rising food and water prices, lack of healthcare and infrastructure, a malfunctioning economy, chronic food insecurity and high levels of acute malnutrition have generated tensions and led to violence. a negotiated solution is needed to resolve differences peacefully and democratically, as well as a process of national reconciliation in the service of the entire population. and to do that, it is absolutely necessary to put an immediate end to the supply of arms and ammunition to south sudan and the whole region. similarly, the country's natural resources, in particular oil, must be placed under the control of the state and used by the state for the benefit of its population in general. i could not vote for the resolution because it does not cover many of these aspects, so i abstained.
in writing. - the humanitarian situation in south sudan is dramatic and the humanitarian crisis in which the country is immersed has intensified in recent months. nearly 4 million sudanese are food insecure, 1.4 million people are displaced from their homes and more than 470,000 are seeking refuge in neighbouring countries. violence has escalated in recent months and atrocious acts of sexual violence are reaching alarming levels. the ceasefire agreement signed in january 2014 and reaffirmed in may 2014 continues to be broken and peace talks have barely advanced towards a lasting solution. it is essential to establish a genuine dialogue leading to a democratic political solution and laying the foundations for building a new democratic state of law that will ensure stability and peace in the country in a sustainable way. the eu and the international community must continue to meet their commitments to the population and the democratic transition in terms of funding and humanitarian assistance. the humanitarian catastrophe that millions of people in south sudan are living through must come to an end.
in writing. - nearly 4 million people continue to need urgent aid in south sudan following the conflict that erupted in december 2013. there is an open crisis between supporters of former south sudanese vice president riek machar (deposed in july 2013) and the african country's president salva kiir. in late august, the united nations warned that four million people - including 740,000 children under the age of five - are in a situation of food insecurity with indicators that border on famine. the ratio of rape as a weapon of war has also skyrocketed. there have been several commitments signed and broken by the parties involved, to form a transitional government. the s&d resolution and the joint resolution both insist on:- a genuine dialogue leading to the holding of elections;- greater funding and ensuring access for humanitarian aid;- promoting more effective sanctions;- the eu ensuring a long-term strategy to strengthen the rule of law and good governance.

in writing. - the hague convention of 30 june 2005 on choice of court agreements is a convention on a matter of private international law and was drawn up by the hague conference on private international law. the convention concerns exclusive choice of court agreements in civil and commercial matters. by these agreements, the two parties agree that any dispute over a particular matter will be resolved by the courts of the state they determine. in this respect, the purpose of the convention is similar, at international level, to that of article 25 of the brussels i regulation as re-enacted at european level. the provisions of the convention establish its scope, define the agreements on choice of court and regulate jurisdiction, recognition and enforcement and procedural matters. i believe that the european union should be involved in this convention, and i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the convention voted by parliament governs the recognition and enforcement of decisions in disputes concerning commercial transactions covered by exclusive choice of court agreements. the convention will apply to agreements in civil and commercial matters and will provide legal certainty by allowing parties to international contracts not only to have recourse to the dispute settlement forum of their choice but also to ensure that relevant judicial decisions have validity in other states parties. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. i voted today in favour of the hague convention on choice of court agreements, which i had the honour to sign on behalf of the european community on 1 april 2009 during the czech presidency, when i was minister of justice of the czech republic. this international convention is, in my view, of particular importance, since it will make it possible to conclude exclusive choice of court agreements, which are concluded in civil and commercial matters. these are agreements in which two parties agree that any dispute between them with an international element will be settled by the courts in the designated state. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure is imputable to the state. this new convention also allows parties not belonging to the european union to conclude such contracts. the treaty will lead to an increase in the enforceability of rights and to greater legal certainty for the parties to the legal relationship, since they will know who will decide their dispute and, in addition, who will recognise and enforce such decisions. the fundamental principle of this convention is the mutual trust of the contracting states in the activities of their judicial authorities.
