in writing. i could not vote in favour of this resolution because i have serious doubts about the credibility of the commission's impact assessments on smes. in my view, these evaluations are a mere formality, a procedure which in no way calls into question the interests of the big lobbyists, who are the ones who set the eu's legislative proposals. to help smes, we should put an end to the neoliberal policies of the eu, to the privatisations, liberalisations, cuts and austerity which are killing the internal market in the different eu countries.
in writing. impact assessments are a key tool for decision-making in all eu institutions and for providing transparent, comprehensive and balanced evidence of the economic, social and environmental impacts, the added value of eu action, the regulatory and administrative burden to be expected, and the costs and benefits of alternative pathways for all parties involved in the legislative process. however, impact assessments cannot replace policy evaluations and decisions and therefore the parliamentary committees of this house should systematically examine the commission's impact assessments. in addition, impact assessments need to pay particular attention to the impact of future legislation on smes. given that the cost of complying with a regulation for an sme can be up to ten times higher than for large companies, it is vital to carry out an independent, rigorous and high-quality impact assessment. i have voted in favour of this resolution to urge the commission to include all these issues in the draft revised impact assessment guidelines.

in writing. the european commission has started a process to amend the guidelines on impact assessments. impact assessments are an objective study that the commission carries out for each legislative proposal. in our experience in parliament we have seen how the committee's impact assessments argue against the very legislative proposals that the commission presents, for example, by showing greater environmental sensitivity. in any case, they require an objective and general view of the effects of legislative initiatives. the commission proposal is less specific in terms of the scope of the studies, leaving it more to the discretion of the relevant directorate-general to decide whether impact assessments are necessary and on which issues, opening the door to the possibility of doing without them in many cases. we have therefore voted in favour of the joint resolution of the european parliament, which calls for the mandatory and comprehensive nature of impact assessments to be maintained as far as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the review of the impact assessment of european legislation as a first step by the union towards simplifying the rules for smes to encourage job creation. it should be remembered - as i said in my speech last monday - that in the eu countries, smes account for nearly 70% of the working population, a percentage which in spain rises to 98%. that's why we have to be much more ambitious. we must get better guidelines in place that really help businesses across the eu to be more productive, and to help to create growth and jobs in all 28 member states, but especially in those that suffer from worryingly high unemployment rates that persist over time.

in writing. - in these 25 years there has been progress, but we are still far from meeting the objectives set out in the convention on the rights of the child. old unresolved challenges are joined by new problems that deprive millions of children of their rights. the current economic crisis is most clearly reflected in the increase in child poverty, a phenomenon which, far from being confined to developing regions of the world, also seriously affects many european countries, and in particular spain. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which, although it could go further in its demands, makes a clear call for member states with high rates of child poverty to redouble their efforts and investments to reduce it and to combat the social exclusion of children. the socialists will continue to demand that a minimum income be guaranteed, co-financed by the european social fund and national budgets, for low-income families with dependent children. specific measures are also needed to protect the rights of girls, who are the most severely affected by violence and gender discrimination worldwide.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution as it represents an opportunity to put the rights of children on the political agenda. a lot has changed since the un convention was created and passed, for better and for worse. and this has been taken into account in the resolution we have adopted. we must put children and young people at the heart of our policies and involve them in decision-making processes. we must empower them to maintain their integrity and their fundamental rights, such as education and food. unfortunately, no country, not even the signatories, has created the full conditions for the convention to be fully implemented. more than 20% of children are affected by austerity, which prevents them from having access to basic services and from being able to fully exercise their fundamental rights. the violations of children's rights are especially painful when we talk about migrant children, especially in terms of health. the example of child soldiers is bloody. the interests of the belligerents are put before the interests of the minors.

in writing. - on 20 november, the united nations general assembly marked 25 years since the adoption of the convention on the rights of the child. since then, remarkable progress has been made, from reducing infant mortality to improving the schooling rate - especially for girls - but more remains to be done. old challenges, still unresolved, are joined by new ones. the situation of children in relation to armed conflict is one of the five strategic priorities of the subcommittee on human rights. the debate on this item in the plenary, with the high representative/vice-president of the commission present, addresses the issue of the increase in child poverty. the text calls on member states with above-average child poverty rates to set national targets and prioritise investments to reduce child poverty and combat social exclusion of children and young people. it also asks them, together with the european commission, to integrate a specific focus on children and youth into the european semester, the annual growth survey and a renewed europe 2020 strategy.

in writing. we voted in favour of this resolution as we consider the united nations convention on the rights of the child (uncrc) and its optional protocols to be a fundamental standard for the promotion and protection of children's rights, containing a comprehensive set of international legal standards for the protection and well-being of children and setting clear legal obligations for all eu member states to promote, protect and fulfil the rights of all children within their jurisdiction. i also believe that the unced, as well as the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, respect the rights of the child to be heard and to express his or her opinion and to have it taken into account in all matters affecting him or her according to his or her age and maturity, which is fundamental when addressing the issue of child labour and its regulation; an example of this is the recently approved code of the girl, child and adolescent of bolivia.
in writing. - in the years since the adoption of the convention on the rights of the child, more progress has been made in the realization and protection of children's rights than in any comparable period in human history, and children's rights are now more important than ever in policy-making. the almost universal ratification of the convention reflects the world's, and also the eu's, commitment to the principles underpinning children's rights. in all parts of the world, institutions, structures, programmes and special measures have emerged to promote children's rights. together with its three optional protocols, it contains a fairly comprehensive set of legally binding international standards for the promotion and protection of the rights of the child. together with other international and regional standards, including those adopted by the council of europe, those instruments provide a solid basis for the enjoyment of human rights by all children without discrimination of any kind, while providing a reference point for the promotion and monitoring of progress in the enjoyment of children's rights.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the 25th anniversary of the convention on the rights of the child because i am convinced that in this quarter of a century we have made great progress in the protection of children, but we still have a long way to go. in the less developed countries, including some in latin america, hundreds of thousands of children live in extreme poverty, are forced to work, have no access to education or are victims of abuse of all kinds. the eu must be aware of this reality and help to combat it, just as we must also combat the reality of child poverty when it occurs here in europe. the countries that have suffered the most from the crisis - for example, spain - have once again seen the terrible face of child poverty, which we thought we had forgotten, and in which the spanish government chooses to remain inactive, refusing even to collect data on the phenomenon. however, denying reality does not help to change it, quite the opposite.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a proposal for a directive on the protection of children against the dangers of ionizing radiation. the convention acquired binding status in september 1990 after being ratified by 20 states and almost all states have now acceded to it. in this quarter of a century, remarkable progress has been made, from reducing child mortality to improving the rate of schooling - especially for girls - but this symbolic date also serves as a reminder of how much remains to be done. old unresolved challenges have been joined by new ones that deprive many children of both their rights and the benefits of development. in this context, unicef decided to declare 2014 the year of innovation for equity with the purpose of focusing global attention on the presentation and development of innovative solutions that promote the well-being of children.

in writing. the united nations convention on the rights of the child was adopted in 1989 with the aim of promoting and protecting children's rights. twenty-five years later, and although we can see progress in this area, violations of the rights of this vulnerable group continue to be committed. many millions of children are still victims of violence and poverty. it is therefore essential that the eu makes the protection of children's rights a priority in all areas of its foreign policy. moreover, the infringement of these rights is not only occurring outside the eu but also within its member states. children are particularly vulnerable to the cuts in social spending that have fuelled the aggressive austerity policies led by the troika. the eu and its member states need to promote additional measures to address this situation, for example by increasing and prioritising investments to reduce poverty and social exclusion among children and young people. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution on the 25th anniversary of the united nations convention on the rights of the child.

in writing. according to the estimates of the eu authorities, the achievement of a genuine digital single market would bring the eu €260 billion of additional growth over the course of the legislature, which would translate into a major boost to employment; it is not without reason that the demand for ict workers by 2020 is estimated to amount to 900 000 highly skilled, quality and remunerated jobs. the commission has shown its commitment to making this a reality in this parliament. we must move from words to deeds. europe cannot afford 28 fractured national markets in crucial areas such as telecommunications, data protection, copyright, cloud computing. only 25% of european citizens have 4g coverage (in rural areas, 4%), while in the united states, 90% of the population has it. progress is needed, and fast, to correct this situation by investing in quality network infrastructures that enable citizens and businesses to thrive in the new environment. it is urgent to end the fragmentation of the current 28 digital markets, ensure universal access to the network and make network security, net neutrality and consumer confidence the keys to the sdm.

in writing. we voted against this resolution on the digital single market because, despite the immense economic, political and social potential that the digital space opens up for european societies, the logic of the community legislator repeatedly attacks the principles of liberalisation, deregulation, privatisation and the principle of free competition as the only regulatory criteria. we have supported amendments which seek to democratize and facilitate access to the digital space for citizens and which seek to dismantle monopoly positions within the single market. but we believe that the regulation of the digital space should be based on democratic criteria and social utility rather than the logic of private profit. the digital space must be open to citizens, not just consumers.

in writing. - i have been studying closely the google antitrust case for the past two years with andreas schwab in a constructive way. we proposed last week the ‘rotation mechanism’ as a possible solution. i have listened to the arguments of the 22 official complainants, including the european consumer organisation! so it is not only a microsoft or german publisher problem: google gives a preferential treatment to its own services: this is the central issue, diverting traffic from rival links. now google has 90% of the market share in many eu member states. european enterprises are losing revenues and people are getting fired. european consumers are not having the most pertinent choice, because of google’s preferential treatment to its own services. i am not against google or any other us company! i am against monopolies and i want a level playing field in the european digital market. we want fair and neutral search in the interest of consumers. a final question: will google really move to find an agreement with the european commission only with the threat of a fine or the threat of unbundling?

the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as you all know, cites, the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, which came into force in 1975, aims to protect species by controlling international trade. it covers some 35 000 species, which are regulated in three appendices according to the degree of protection they require. since the commission's proposal, there have been two new accessions to cites, which now has 180 parties, including all eu member states. the european union has until now had observer status in cites, since only member states could be parties. however, this situation changed in november 2013 with the entry into force of the gaborone amendment, which allows regional economic integration organizations constituted by states to become parties to the convention. the request for approval sent to parliament by the council bases its draft decision on a single article of the treaty, article 192 on the environment, whereas the commission had based its initial proposal on articles 192 and 207, the latter relating to the common commercial policy. the opinion of the committee on legal affairs of this house considered that the double legal basis proposed by the european commission is appropriate in this case. however, since parliament has to adopt a recommendation concerning only the accession of the european union to cites and has not been called upon to adopt a position on the legal basis, we have confined ourselves, in this context and for the sake of legal clarity, to mentioning the issue of the double legal basis in visas. in our view, the accession of the european union to cites is a logical and necessary step to ensure the full capacity of the european union to pursue its environmental policy objectives. mrs ayuso says it is important to note that the rights and obligations of the member states under the convention will not be affected by this accession. in practice, the internal decision-making process will not be influenced, but will streamline the practices currently in place. in view of all this, mrs ayuso asks me to tell you that she thinks we should vote in favour of the european union's accession to cites.
five thousand animal species and twenty-eight thousand plant species are protected by the convention. nine hundred in imminent danger of extinction. we need mechanisms to prevent their extinction, whether through overexploitation or illegal trade, which is increasingly affecting a growing number of species. every year, 50,000 primates, four million birds, and 350 million tropical fish are trafficked. between 60 and 80% die on the journey. the market is clearly defined: supply comes from tropical countries, demand is concentrated in rich countries, consumers are looking for rare specimens and it is the pharmaceutical industry that buys poisonous spiders and snakes for experiments and new medicines. the european union is the main consumer of these exotic animals. it is the world's leading importer of reptile, parrot, boa constrictor and python skins. it's the second largest importer of primates and cats. we also need, i conclude, effective tools to prevent these exotic species from becoming brooms in the countries of destination.

debt levels instead of reducing them. we see therefore the current framework as a self-defeating framework. not only are the rules not serving its purpose but they are also bringing europe towards its madam president, i think that it is too early to judge whether the two-pack and the six-pack need revision. i would remind you that it is only two years since we were negotiating the final details of the two-pack. in my view a clear target for revision is how we count public debt. should we also include debt from public enterprises? i think we should, and this will be one of the main ideas in our future debates. talking about the revision of economic governance in europe, we have also to consider regional and local governments with fiscal and legislative powers. the deficit targets for those administrations have to be proportional to their share of government spending. only in this way will we ensure that there is no discrimination between different levels of government. this is especially important in countries where most social spending is done at regional level but tax-collection powers are still monopolised by the central government. i also have the feeling that maybe europe should look more at the united states of america – at how the federal usa was built and how they created a monetary and fiscal union. i ask myself whether the no-bailout clause should be analysed in our future framework for economic governance.
madam president, when the crisis began, the commission was quick to blame it on the member states' lack of rigorous compliance with the stability rules. he forgot that germany was among those states which failed to comply with the rules on budgetary stability and that spain was among those states which complied, with low deficits and low public debt - yes, with an already precarious labour market - and which today, because of the implementation of its policies, has an unemployment rate of 25% and the second highest external debt in the world. these are the consequences of his rule. the assessment can therefore only be negative. the european workers do not want more reforms, less social protection, more evictions, more poverty. we do not want this governance, which is also causing fascism to resurge in europe. the commission's role must be to achieve the productive and social convergence of the peoples of europe and not to be an accomplice of the markets and the emptying of democracy.
madam president, dear vice-president, ladies and gentlemen, today we are here to evaluate the two-pack and the six-pack. i think the positive results are obvious. if we look at the situation in the euro area countries, there has been significant progress in the fiscal consolidation processes and there has been progress in the reform processes. most countries have undertaken or are beginning to undertake major reform processes. moreover, it has been shown that those countries which are most ambitious in their fiscal consolidation processes and those countries which are most ambitious in their reform programmes are today the countries which are growing the most and are today the countries which are creating the most jobs. but that's not enough, your honours. we have to keep moving. we must be more forceful with those countries that do not comply, because the non-compliance of those countries affects the rest of the countries in the eurozone. but, as the vice-president has said, we must also make the whole process more transparent, we must give it greater democratic legitimacy. because at a time when it is necessary to move forward with the much-awaited and necessary economic union - ultimately, political union - it is at a time when european citizens, and in particular the citizens of the euro area, feel further away from europe. and i have no doubt that the lack of democratic legitimacy of this process has something to do with it. it is therefore time to move towards greater democratic legitimacy for both the two-pack and the six-pack.
madam president, there's a black rapper named tupac - i don't know if you know him - and he said something that comes to mind: "to pull the trigger to kill a black man is to be a hero: one less hungry mouth for welfare. first, send them drugs, let them distribute them among brothers, give them guns and let them kill each other. it seems that, like the blacks in the united states, it is not difficult to condemn the countries of the south and the workers of europe. the fiscal pact, the stability and growth pact, is like the leech that the old doctor used as the wrong remedy for the inevitability of circumstances and, moreover, has become the universal method that is dragging europe into the disaster of austerity, not to mention the threat of economic punishment to those who think of doing something different: again sucking people's blood. this european union, which has adopted rules which, having been agreed by a few and behind the backs of almost everyone, now appear to be written in stone, is nothing but a pretext for legalizing something which is no longer legitimate or effective in dealing with the crisis and its causes. so, in conclusion, i invite you to look in the mirror, in case your reflection has disappeared from it.
mr president, the fiscal crisis of spring 2010 made the union's economic problems apparent, and the need for better economic governance. from there came the six-pack and the two-pack, which we are discussing today and which are intended to control the fiscal policy of countries. however, it was not until the financial crisis in the first half of 2012 that europe assumed that its economic problems were even more serious and that it needed essentially to have a common economic policy, a project from which the banking union emerged. but this journey has only just begun. we need a strong fiscal union and i therefore want to denounce the fact that the fiscal rules we are discussing today are based on a purely national approach to budgetary policy. we cannot analyse the fiscal policy of each country by studying only the effect of its budgets on that member state. we need europe to internalize the effects of fiscal policy across the union, not just in individual countries. we must therefore review these fiscal rules and the whole of the coordination of the economic policy of the union to take account of this overall approach to national economic policies. and we also need to reform the stability and growth pact, not just to make the system more flexible but, essentially, to incorporate that european analysis, to incorporate that global approach to the effects of the budgetary policies of individual countries on the union as a whole. mr dombrovskis, we cannot say that the current system is working. the results don't support it. we need more flexibility and a european project for tax policy.
mr president, commissioner, i want to raise this matter from the political point of view of the credibility of europe and the european project, which is what many of us have been elected to do. the six-pack and the two-pack have to earn that credibility. it is true that this is not the time to reform something so recent, but it is the time to see some of its flaws, such as, for example, the discrimination in its application by country - which undermines european credibility in this respect - and also the lack of supervision, because it is a mistake to think that in spain, for example, there have been structural reforms: there have been patches and sacrifices. nor will there be any credibility, commissioner, if we do not also speak imperatively of more europe in terms of the energy union, the single market - which in spain does not even have a single market - the capital market, etc. and finally, solidarity will not be believed if we do not raise the issue of eurobonds while at the same time talking about control.
in writing. in the light of what the commission and the council have said in the course of the debate on the review of the economic governance package, i would like to say the following: (1) i disagree with the commission's assessment of the effectiveness of the so-called six-pack and two-pack rules, insofar as the reduction of government deficits has been achieved at the expense of growth and employment. since the onset of the crisis in 2007-2008, the gdp growth differential between the european union and the euro area, and the united states, has been on average higher than one percentage point per year. this regulatory package has also not served to ensure financial stability, which has been achieved thanks to economic integration (banking union) and the monetary policy of the ecb. 2) the commission should therefore propose a revision of these rules, so that they no longer focus on the obsessive pursuit of punitive tax adjustments and serve to boost economic growth and social welfare. the european council should also consider whether the stability and growth pact itself should be reformed.

in writing. ‒ this report on the proposal for a directive repealing council directive 93/5/eec on the assistance of the commission by the member states and their cooperation in the scientific examination of questions relating to foodstuffs is part of the commission's current programme for the adaptation and effectiveness of legislation (refit), in which the commission is committed to repealing obsolete and redundant legislation. the aim of the directive was to promote scientific support by member states and to organise cooperation with the national bodies competent in scientific matters relating to food safety, in order to ensure the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food, which was replaced in 2002 by the european food safety authority (efsa). as provided for in regulation (ec) no 178/2002, efsa becomes the competent body for the promotion of scientific cooperation, which makes directive 93/5/eec obsolete. since it is a purely technical report, i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the regulatory fitness and performance programme (refit) launched in 2012 to ensure a simple, clear, stable and predictable regulatory framework for businesses, workers and citizens, the commission has committed to repealing rules that have become redundant or obsolete. directive 93/5/eec was intended to ensure the effective functioning of the scientific committee for food by promoting scientific support from the member states and organising cooperation with the relevant national bodies on scientific questions relating to food safety. however, the scientific tasks entrusted to the scientific committee for food have been taken over by the european food safety authority (efsa), which has also become the competent body for promoting scientific cooperation with the member states and relevant national bodies operating in the areas covered by the authority's remit. directive 93/5/eec has become obsolete and i have therefore voted in favour of its repeal in the interests of simplifying, improving and making european legislation more effective.

in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is an international agreement whose objective is to ensure that international trade in endangered species does not threaten their survival, especially those with high commercial interest. the success of cites depends on the effective implementation of the agreed recommendations. the eu maintains an observer status with cites. the aim of this report is to approve the eu's accession to cites in order to allow it to participate fully in its work and to bind the eu and the member states to the implementation and enforcement of the convention itself. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as the purpose of the proposal for a council decision is to approve the accession of the european union to cites and to ask the president of the council to designate the person empowered to deposit, on behalf of the union, the instrument of accession provided for in article xxi (1) of the convention and the declaration of competence provided for in article xxi (3) thereof. the accession of the european union to cites will allow it to be adequately represented at the meetings of the convention and to play a full role in its work, in accordance with the treaties and established practices on external representation. it will enable the commission, on behalf of the european union, to lead the negotiations and act as a catalyst for compromise solutions balanced between the positions of the 28 member states. by becoming a party to cites, the european union will assume formal obligations and be held accountable to the other parties with regard to its implementation of the convention.
in writing. ‒ the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is a major international instrument whose objective is to protect endangered species of fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of these species. it has been in force since 1975 and currently has 178 parties, including all eu member states. it covers some 35 000 protected species and ensures that international trade in wild animal and plant specimens does not endanger their survival. all imports, exports, re-exports and introductions of species covered by the convention should be authorised through a licensing system. however, until the entry into force of the decision taken at the botswana conference (2013) to allow supranational bodies to accede to the convention, the eu had not been able to become a party and had only observer status to the convention. i voted in favour of the rapporteur's recommendation to approve the eu's accession to cites, which will allow the eu to participate and negotiate with one voice at the summits, strengthening our negotiating role and capacity.
in writing. ‒ single vote on the recommendation for the council decision on eu accession to cites. the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) is a highly relevant international instrument whose objective is to protect endangered species of fauna and flora by controlling international trade in specimens of those species. it entered into force in 1975 and now has 178 parties (including all eu member states). it covers some 35 000 species, listed in three appendices according to the degree of protection they need, and ensures that international trade in wild animal and plant specimens does not endanger their survival. all imports, exports, re-exports and introductions from species covered by the convention should be authorised through a licensing system. however, until the entry into force of a decision taken at the botswana conference (2013) to allow supranational bodies to accede to the convention, the eu had not been able to become a party and it was the sum of the member states that determined the european position.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because, with the accession of croatia to the eu and in order to allow its participation in the european economic area, there are council decisions under examination which aim to conclude certain texts. the eea agreement brings together the eu member states and three members of the european free trade association (iceland, liechtenstein and norway) in a single market. the eea agreement provides for the inclusion of eu legislation on the four freedoms (free movement of goods, services, persons and capital) in all eea countries. the agreement also covers cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture, known collectively as 'horizontal and complementary' policies. the agreement guarantees equal rights and obligations within the internal market for eea citizens and economic operators.
in writing. ‒ the european economic area (eea), in force since 1994, brings together the eu member states and three members of the european free trade association (iceland, liechtenstein and norway) in a single market. the eea agreement provides for the inclusion of eu legislation on the four freedoms (free movement of goods, services, persons and capital) in all eea countries. the agreement also covers cooperation in other important areas such as research and development, education, social policy, the environment, consumer protection, tourism and culture, known collectively as 'horizontal and complementary' policies. the agreement also guarantees equal rights and obligations within the internal market for eea citizens and economic operators. the participation of croatia in the eea is a natural consequence of its accession to the eu and therefore the conclusion of the agreement on the participation of croatia in the eea and the additional protocols thereto should be approved. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the commission is establishing a new legal framework for the 'insular arbitration' for the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2020, determining the products to which tax exemptions and reductions may be applied. while the products in the new list are essentially similar to those included in the annex to council decision 2004/162/ec, it should be noted that several new products have been introduced and others have been deleted. this report will serve to further stimulate economic activity and competitiveness in the outermost regions, without undermining the coherence of the internal market and the eu legal order.
in writing. ‒ until 1 july 2014, france was authorised to provide for exemptions or reductions from the 'insular arbitration' tax for certain products manufactured in the french outermost regions (except saint-martin), in order to compensate for the disadvantages they suffer and to support their competitiveness and social and economic development. the proposal now being tabled aims to establish a new legal framework for the 'insular arbitration' for the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2020, determining the products to which the tax exemptions and reductions may be applied. while the products in the new list are essentially similar to those included in the annex to council decision 2004/162/ec, several new products have been introduced and others have been removed. it seems a justified measure. the aim is to continue to stimulate economic activity and competitiveness in the outermost regions, without undermining the coherence of the internal market and the eu legal order, and i have therefore voted in favour, in accordance with the procedure proposed by the regi commission presidency, of adopting it without amendments, in accordance with article 50 of the regulation.

president of the commission. mr president, after the events in pakistan this morning, which you have justly condemned, it is difficult to speak calmly about the european commission's work programme. i have no difficulty in congratulating you on behalf of the commission on the award of the aachen charlemagne prize. i'm a double of the charles prize. the luxembourg people have received the charlemagne prize as a people once before in 1986, and i am still one of them, and i had the honour of receiving it myself in 2006. the line of the charles prize winners is made even more impressive by your appointment, mr president. (applause) as regards the programme of work of the new commission, let me say, mr president, that i had the impression, during the election campaign - during which you were my rival but nevertheless a friend, like guy verhofstadt and others - that european citizens wanted to see a new start in europe. i have the impression that i have visited some 20 countries and 33 european cities. i am thus falling in love with europe, because there are few moments when, in such a short space of time, one can discover so many sensibilities, see so many colours, meet so many men and women. we agreed, during the process of setting up the new commission, that it should concentrate on the essentials, on the grand subjects, defined by the guidelines which i had the honour to develop before you on 15 july and at the end of october. we agreed - i think - that every problem in europe is not necessarily a problem for the european union or for the commission. we were indeed very many to think that the principle of subsidiarity should be restored and that the task of solving this problem should be entrusted to the levels of power - namely the member states, the regions or the local authorities - which are best placed to provide a response to the problems facing europe. on the basis of these principles, and in accordance with the commission's guidelines, we have examined 452 legislative initiatives which are currently under consideration and are being debated. we have done so keeping in mind the major priorities which must be those of the european union. the great priority, which is beyond doubt, is based on the elements of growth and employment. that is why, some three weeks after its installation, the commission has proposed an ambitious investment plan which will occupy not only the minds, but also our meetings over the next six months, and i am grateful to the european parliament for associating closely, with courage and with a concern for the work well done, to the examination of these texts. mr president, we have tried to limit the number of new initiatives we are going to undertake and launch. there was a time when the commission announced 130 new initiatives per annum. we are announcing for our part twenty-three new initiatives for the year 2015; we are presenting the work programme for the year 2015 and not the work programme for the duration of the legislature. we limit the number of new initiatives by applying the often contested principle of discontinuity: we are going to withdraw, amend or modify 83 texts on the table of the legislator. on compte parmi les nouvelles initiatives, outre le programme d'investissement which has all its importance all those which have to do with taxation. i repeat in this connection that the commission will present within the first six months a directive on the automatic exchange of advance rulings, namely the tax rulings comme on dit en mauvais français. the commission will also present an action programme to combat tax evasion and fraud, in principle by making the country where the profit is made the place of taxation. (applause from the centre) this is done and i would like to say very amicably that i am sensitive to the fact that, day after day, people invite me to do what i said. i said it and it will be done in 2015. frans timmermans i congratulate him for the ardour with which he coordinated the work of the commission relating to its work programme i met each of the commissioners separately. the programme was prepared with the council of ministers and the european parliament. i should like to say to you, mr president, that i will leave it to the first vice-president to explain the commission's programme of work and its priorities. (applause from the centre)
first vice-president of the commission– mr president, let me briefly add my congratulations to those of president juncker. the charlemagne prize is something that is very close to you and me because we are from the region. aachen is the pivotal city in the region we are from, and the origins of the charlemagne prize are so intimately linked with the idea of healing the wounds after the second world war that to be honoured with the charlemagne prize is one of the highest distinctions any european can receive. i want to congratulate you on that. through you, mr president, i want to thank this house for the elaborate cooperation in preparing the commission work programme for 2015. as president juncker has just said, we want it to be focused on priorities for 2015, and we want it to be member states are able to do? will it be effective in changing things on the ground without adding unnecessary burdens? all the initiatives we are taking are well within the ten priorities president juncker agreed with your parliament upon his election. we have also asked the same question: ‘is it is necessary and useful?’ of the 400 or so pending proposals that are already on the table, applying the principle of political discontinuity that is set out in the framework agreement between our two institutions. it is very often set out as a principle but, in practical terms, it is very often the rapporteur. madam president, yes, the truth is that we have a bit of work to do in the committee on budgets and that is why we have so many reports to debate today and to vote tomorrow. the truth is that there was little or no sign that we would reach an agreement in time for the 2015 budget or for the much needed 2014 amendments. and this has been thanks to the work and involvement of many of the people here today, in this house. and so i would like to begin by thanking commissioner georgieva and her whole team, the italian presidency, with ambassador sannino at the head, and all my colleagues, because we have worked very hard over the last few months to get this agreement. and i said that there was nothing to suggest that we would have an agreement in time because there were very different positions between the initial proposal of the council and that of parliament, but also very different positions among the members of the european council itself, among the 28 countries themselves. they were distant poses. there were institutional doubts between institutions, between countries, doubts about the figures and, moreover, money in the middle, which is the budget. and so we had an explosive cocktail on the table. three major issues we had to solve: how to end 2014, how to face 2015 and, above all, a plan to solve the defaults in the medium term. i don't think anyone is satisfied with the outcome of the negotiation. and i can certainly say as rapporteur that i am not. neither the figures nor the way the negotiations were conducted nor the lack of political content in the debate. but i also know that, after a whole year of working to get this agreement and to get a budget, the last proposal we had on the table, and which i ask you to support today with your vote tomorrow, is the best agreement we have been able to get. because that agreement puts 4.7 billion more to pay for programs that were already running. that is, an extra 4.7 billion euros for ngos, so that they can continue to support those who need it most, for smes, so that they can continue to finance projects that are key to economic recovery, or for farmers who have been affected by the russian veto, for our municipalities and our regions, so that they can continue to serve the citizens. and because at the end of the day, that's what a budget is about, in this case the european one: serving citizens, whether it's through grants, whether it's through infrastructure improvements, whether it's providing quality food, whether it's helping five million refugees in the middle east, whether it's supporting an innovative project of a small and medium-sized business, whether it's funding food banks, whether it's collaborating with projects against female genital mutilation or female genital mutilation. that's what the budget is all about. and we have fought from the european parliament for these projects to continue to be funded. because the alternative to this was no deal. it was not having a budget for 2015. it was to lose the opportunity to use those extra 4.7 billion euros thanks to revenue not provided for in the union budget. a no-deal scenario would have put at risk the investment programme which the european commission has just presented to us, because it is based 100% on the european budget. we know that 4.7 billion is not enough, because the problem of non-payment is greater. and that's why we've put so much emphasis on seeking a commitment from the council so that we can work from the beginning of 2015 on a real plan to tackle this problem. a plan that should go to the root of the problem. because the union does not have a spending problem: it is only 1% of gross domestic product. we have a revenue problem. and the solution is not to cut payments or cut the budget. the solution is to increase the union's own resources and thus reduce national contributions. i regret that the financial transaction tax is currently frozen because no agreement has been reached at ecofin. that is why i believe that the high level group on own resources is more necessary than ever to be able to provide resources for a strong budget, properly financed and, above all, protected from purely accounting discussions which are sterile. that's what we really need for the future.

member of the commission.– mr president, i will take as my point of departure the very last words: we are in a tough situation. what we have is not a budget of joy. we may be on the eve of christmas, but what we have is no basis to feel completely relieved of the difficulties in front of us, because they are still there. but it is a budget of responsibility. for those who said ‘why do we not just jump into provisional twelfths, let us forget about this budget deal’, let us remember two things: firstly, provisional twelfths would bring us a lower level of budget simply because 2014 is a so much lower base. but secondly, and most importantly, the probability we now have to secure the amount of money from fines with dab 3 will be much lower when we cross into the new year. faced with this fiscal reality that we would be substantially worse—off – not only because provisional twelfths in the first months would mean a lower budget, but because the injection of fresh cash would be potentially lost or would be much smaller and unable to cure the problem in hand, which is to stabilise unpaid bills – i for one am relieved that the negotiators, the two arms of the budgetary authority, were able to secure this budget for us. this budget is not one of joy, but of responsibility. i want to stress four points here in closing. first, we are bringing the unpaid bills to a more manageable level. the accuracy of our projections still stands, we expect up to eur 25 billion at the end of 2014. this is eur 1.6 billion more than we had at the beginning of this year. we would have liked not to have it. we would have liked to stabilise the level, but at least we have a chance to step into the year less concerned about the mountain of bills than we would have been otherwise. secondly, to those who have been speaking about the accuracy of our data time and again in the negotiations: i am very proud of my team, some of whom are behind me. we have shown that we are very clear; we know the numbers, we understand the trends and we are going to use the clarity of our analysis to underpin the payment plan and to ensure that it becomes a reality. thirdly, i want to repeat once again to those who are worried about our farmers: we have found in this package a way not to dip into the crisis reserve. we are paying, without dipping into the crisis reserve, for the impact of the russian ban and other events in the agricultural markets. fourthly, some spoke about the solidarity fund. since we have a deal, we can provide help to croatia in the order of close to eur 9 million, to bulgaria for eur 10.5 million, and to serbia, a country that is eligible and is now in negotiations. but what is the most important point i want to convey? that i have heard from many of you a desire that we improve our budgetary process. that next year we do better, we engage earlier, we work harder and we reach a deal on a more structured, trust-based basis. if there is one thing i have been very concerned about during these negotiations, it is that they have shown a degree of erosion of trust, and we have – for the sake of our people – to restore trust. we have to build a budget that is more joyful. we need budget negotiations that are a more joyful event than those we are leaving behind. once again, i would like to thank the italian presidency for its sweat and tears. thank you to the negotiators in the parliament. what we have is a budget of responsibility.

will provide the country with an opportunity to diversify its trade and economy and improve the livelihoods of the population. we should support and encourage this choice, and it is in this perspective that we should consider the regulation as an important complement to the trade agreement. we proposed this regulation very rapidly after the conclusion of the negotiations in order to ensure that there would be no disruption in the preferences that ecuador is enjoying today. i welcome the european parliament and the rapporteur’s quick adoption, extending the preferences and thereby preventing a negative impact on the exports of ecuador. ecuador will, as you know, graduate from the gsp+ preferences at the end of this year, and around 60% of ecuadorian exports to the eu benefit from substantial preferences under this scheme. the regulation that we discussed today will bridge the gap until the agreement fully applies, and that provides certainty and predictability to producers and workers in the eu and, more importantly, in ecuador. if the gap between the graduation from gsp and the entry into force of the agreement were not bridged, ecuador would face a sudden increase in duties in january, only to see them fall back later on. a sudden increase in duties would be a lot when it comes to loss of market share, which is extremely difficult to recuperate later. we would be talking about increases in duties in excess of 20% for products such as tuna and shrimps, and an average increase of duties of more than 15% of all ecuador’s export under the gsp scheme. i am aware that many members in this house attach great importance to the implementation of this regulation, particularly when it comes to the requirement for effective implementation by ecuador of relevant human rights, ilo, environmental conventions and international agreements, as well as the procedure to be used in the event that a suspension of preferences is warranted. this is also important to me, and i raised this with the minister whom i met last week. rest assured that we will monitor this and we will keep parliament informed on the implementation of these provisions. we are ready to inform you, whenever requested to do so, and to ensure the required transparency in the implementation of the regulation, as well as to make use of the good practices that we are developing within the context of the gsp scheme.

in writing. in the light of what the commission and the council have said about the european investment plan in the course of the debate on the european council, i would like to say the following: 1) since the start of the crisis in 2007-2008, the gdp growth differential between the european union and the euro area, and the united states, has been on average higher than one percentage point per year, as a result of failed ultra-fast structural adjustment policies. the european investment plan will not be effective if it does not at least make the stability and growth pact more flexible (which will have to be reformed anyway). the economic governance package therefore needs to be revised as soon as possible to make it a useful tool for growth and jobs. 2) the european investment plan is expected to catalyse €252 billion of private investment with €63 billion in public loans, with only €21 billion in public guarantees. these estimates have been questioned by various experts. in addition to national contributions, the commission should make a proposal to link the financial transaction tax to the european fund for strategic investments.

mr. chairman, i also support the change of the autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova. i very much welcome the fact that this proposal has received a lot of support, because it is a clear signal that the republic of moldova is not alone alongside the russian federation and that when the russian federation sanctions a small country for wanting to be a partner of the european union, the european union clearly responds by opening its market to agricultural products and thus helping moldova in its struggle to prosper and survive economically and to have its own foreign policy independent of the russian federation. so i don't see it as just an economic decision, an economic advantage, but i see it as a clear political decision to help a small country that the russian federation is treating unfairly and punishing and sanctioning for wanting moldova to have a free, independent foreign policy. i therefore thank you for accepting this proposal and hope that it will greatly help moldova's economy and that moldova will be a strong partner of the european union in the future.
in writing. the autonomous trade preferences (atp) system was granted to moldova in january 2008 until december 2015. on 21 july 2014, as a result of the signature of the eu-moldova free trade agreement, russia imposed sanctions on moldovan agricultural products, which are damaging its economy, as agriculture in that country represents 40% of the economy. this sector employs 250,000 people. the commission therefore proposes to extend the atp regulation to three products: plums, apples and grapes. i have voted in favour of the report because the eu can easily absorb imports of these three products.
in writing. i voted in favour as an act of solidarity. in recent years, the eu and moldova have strengthened their relations with an association agreement which has been applied since 1 september 2014. as a result of this improvement in relations, russia has, for political reasons, decided to ban the import of products from moldova, affecting more than 250 000 people in small and mediumsized enterprises in the horticultural sector from rural areas. the moldovan authorities have asked for assistance and parliament has decided to amend the regulation by introducing three new free tariff quotas for apples, fresh plums and table grapes, hoping that these decisions will improve the moldovan economy.
in writing. in response to the intensification of the eu's political and economic relations with moldova, as outlined in the association agreement signed last june 2014, which also includes a deep and wide free trade area, russia has responded by banning imports of agricultural products from moldova, which has been in place since 21 july 2014. the pressure that russia is exerting on moldova is manifested in a significant loss of its economic resilience and the slowdown of its reform process. in order to support the ongoing reform process undertaken by moldova with a view to political association and further economic integration with the eu, i voted in favour of temporarily increasing the liberalisation of trade access for certain moldovan products to the eu - namely, apples, plums and table grapes - and thus reducing the economic impact of the russian ban. the imports of these three types of fruit from moldova represented 0,01% of the total eu imports in the year 2013, so the eu market will have no problems to easily absorb this increase in imports.
in writing. the s&d group supports providing economic support to moldova to strengthen its political will in the current reform process and its european path.
in writing. the autonomous trade preferences (atp) system was granted to moldova in january 2008 until december 2015. on 21 july 2014, as a result of the signature of the eu-moldova free trade agreement, russia imposed sanctions on moldovan agricultural products, which are damaging its economy, as agriculture in that country represents 40% of the economy. this sector employs 250,000 people. the commission therefore proposes to extend the atp regulation to three products: plums, apples and grapes. i have voted in favour of the report because the eu can easily absorb imports of these three products.
in writing. we voted in favour because this agreement will not affect the rest of the european agricultural sector and will help the sector in moldova, which employs 250 000 people (10% of the working population), who live mainly in rural areas and also work on small and medium-sized farms. these are certain quantities of apples, plums and grapes which will be exported mainly to romania and which will therefore not have a negative impact on the european agricultural sector. since the implementation of the preferential trade access (pta) which replaced gsp+, products originating in moldova are duty-free, except for some products from the agricultural sector. but with the embargo imposed by russia since 21 july 2014 on agricultural products, this sector has been severely damaged. therefore, in order to mitigate the social impact of this embargo, this agreement is proposed, which will allow small and medium-sized farmers to keep their jobs for the next year (this agreement would apply until december 2015, when the preferential trade access expires).

in writing. in 2008, tariff preferences were granted to moldova under the european neighbourhood policy. and last june 2014, the eu and moldova signed an association agreement, including a deep and wide-ranging free trade area, from which moldova has adopted an ambitious political agenda towards political association and further economic integration with the eu. unfortunately, in the face of the intensification of the eu's political and economic relations with moldova, russia has responded by banning imports of agricultural products from this country. the s&d group is in favour of providing economic support to moldova by extending these agreements in order to strengthen its political will in the current reform process and its european path.
in writing. the autonomous trade preferences (atp) system was granted to moldova in january 2008 until december 2015. on 21 july 2014, as a result of the signature of the eu-moldova free trade agreement, russia imposed sanctions on moldovan agricultural products, which are damaging its economy, as agriculture in that country represents 40% of the economy. this sector employs 250,000 people. the commission therefore proposes to extend the atp regulation to three products: plums, apples and grapes. i have voted in favour of the report because the eu can easily absorb imports of these three products.
in writing. the autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova were originally introduced by the eu by regulation (ec) no 55/2008 (the pca regulation), for a period ending on 31 december 2015. in recent years, the eu and moldova have intensified their relations by concluding an association agreement, which will lead to the creation of a deep and comprehensive free trade area (dcfta) between the two parties. on 21 july 2014, russia imposed a ban on the import of moldovan agricultural products, which is significantly affecting the moldovan economy. they have therefore turned to the eu for urgent support to reduce this impact, in particular for three products: apples, plums and table grapes. the commission proposed to amend the pca regulation by introducing three new duty-free tariff quotas for these products under the pca regulation in addition to the proposed quotas under the ccfta. the commission has also received comments from the moldovan authorities, which have not yet received any comments from the moldovan authorities. for these reasons, i am voting in favour of this proposal.
in writing. in response to the intensification of the eu's political and economic relations with moldova, as outlined in the association agreement signed last june 2014, which also includes a deep and wide free trade area, russia has responded by banning imports of agricultural products from moldova, which has been in place since 21 july 2014. the pressure that russia is exerting on moldova is manifested in a significant loss of its economic resilience and the slowdown of its reform process. in order to support the ongoing reform process undertaken by moldova with a view to political association and further economic integration with the eu, i voted in favour of temporarily increasing the liberalisation of trade access for certain moldovan products to the eu, namely 'apples, plums and table grapes', and thus reducing the economic impact of the russian ban. the imports of these three types of fruit from moldova represented 0,01% of the total eu imports in the year 2013, so the eu market will have no problems to easily absorb this increase in imports.
in writing. - we voted in favour because this agreement will not affect the rest of the european agricultural sector and will help the sector in moldova, which employs 250 000 people (10% of the working population), who live mainly in rural areas and also work on small and mediumsized agricultural holdings. these are certain quantities of apples, plums and grapes which will be exported mainly to romania and which will therefore not have a negative impact on the european agricultural sector. since the implementation of the preferential trade access (pta) which replaced gsp+, products originating in moldova are duty-free, except for some products from the agricultural sector. but with the embargo imposed by russia since 21 july 2014 on agricultural products, this sector has been severely damaged. therefore, in order to mitigate the social impact of this embargo, this agreement is proposed, which will allow small and medium-sized farmers to keep their jobs for the next year (this agreement would apply until december 2015, when the preferential trade access expires).

in writing. - the autonomous trade preference (atp) system was granted to moldova in january 2008 until december 2015. on 21 july 2014, as a result of the signature of the eu-moldova free trade agreement, russia imposed sanctions on moldovan agricultural products, which are damaging its economy, as agriculture in that country represents 40% of the economy. this sector employs 250,000 people. the commission proposes to extend the atp regulation to three products: plums, apples and grapes. i voted against this report because it is going to harm the farmers on both sides; it is an agreement to give cheap raw materials to the agricultural exporters.
in writing. in this report we voted to extend the gsp+ for ecuador from january 2015 on the condition that the eu-ecuador free trade agreement is signed before 31 december 2016. i cannot vote in favour of this report because, although i am not against the extension of the gsp+, i cannot accept that it be made conditional on the signing of the free trade agreement, since i am against it. that is why i abstained.
in writing. negotiations with ecuador for accession to the trade agreement concluded between the eu and colombia and peru were concluded on 17 july. the multilateral agreement will provide a new framework in relations between ecuador and the eu. a provisional time limit has been established to ensure that customs duties will not be increased on the date specified in the protocol in order to reduce the burden on eu importers of goods exported from ecuador. in short, it takes time to carry out all the internal procedures for the eu and also for ecuador before the accession protocol is applied. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal on the tariff treatment of goods originating in ecuador.
in writing. negotiations for the accession of ecuador to the eu-colombia/peru trade agreement were concluded on 17 july 2014. however, the entry into force of the eu-ecuador agreement will not be effective until late 2015 or early 2016, once the authentication and ratification procedures of the text are completed. taking into account that ecuador will lose, as from 1 january 2015, its status as a beneficiary of the generalised system of preferences plus (gsp+) which it has enjoyed until now, having been declared by the world bank as an upper-middle income country, it is necessary to freeze the customs duties currently applied and to ensure that no new duties are applied to products originating in ecuador, thus avoiding unnecessary disruption to trade until the completion of the procedures necessary for the application of the protocol of accession. i therefore voted without amendment for the commission's proposal for a regulation to apply from 1 january 2015 and until six months after the entry into force of the accession protocol or until 31 december 2016, whichever is the earlier.

in writing. we voted in favour. this is not a free trade agreement but a proposal for a regulation extending the export preferences of ecuador to the eu under the gsp+, which expires on 1 january 2015, until the future free trade agreement enters into force. although we are against the conditionality imposed by the european commission on ecuador in the wording of the text (which allows for the suspension of tariff preferences if ecuador adopts 'measures' which have some kind of effect on eu imports) and although we consider that any decisions the commission may take in this respect should be made under the framework of delegated acts so that parliament can make effective use of its monitoring functions (both issues to which we are submitting amendments, which were tabled in the inta committee by the right and the far right), we consider it important for the ecuadorian people that these tariff preferences be extended and that they be implemented as a matter of urgency.

in writing. i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it proposes a solution to ensure that the eu budget pays outstanding payments, it does not offer a sustainable solution. the defaults the eu is trying to cover with this mobilisation of funds are not unforeseen but are the debt of the past financial year which it has decided not to act on. the eu must establish a credible budgetary framework to deal with outstanding payments and not try to solve crises with patches that will aggravate the problem of arrears in the medium term. that is why i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of mobilising the contingency margin because, in the implementation of the mff 2014-2020, the backlog of payments and outstanding invoices increased, with a level of outstanding commitments above the amount envisaged when the mff 2007-2013 was adopted. this unsustainable situation must be resolved and the use of the flexibility mechanism must be included so as not to jeopardise the implementation of european policy and programmes and to reduce interest claims for late payments which would worsen the situation.
in writing. implementation of the mff 2014-2020 started with a huge backlog of payments, with outstanding invoices amounting to some eur 23 400 million at the end of 2013 in cohesion policy alone, while the level of outstanding commitments to be settled reached eur 221 700 million on the same date, i.e. eur 41 000 million above the amount initially planned when the mff 2007-2013 was adopted. this situation calls for urgent measures, such as the use of the flexibility mechanisms provided for in the mff regulation, in order not to jeopardise the implementation of eu policies and programmes. i have therefore voted in favour of mobilising the contingency margin in 2014 to make available an amount of eur 3 168 233 715 in payment appropriations above the payment ceiling of the multiannual financial framework.

mr president, i shall speak on the mediterranean issue as many times as necessary until we can have a satisfactory situation. the situation in the mediterranean is a matter of concern to us; 3 224 people have drowned in the mediterranean while trying to reach european soil, according to a recent report by the international organisation for migration. this tragedy is only one aspect of the complex phenomenon of immigration into our countries, which we in this institution must now tackle: analysing its causes and effects from a prudent and sensible standpoint, promoting legal migration flows, development aid in the countries of origin and an international policy to avoid humanitarian crises, the consequence of violence caused by totalitarianism, extreme greed, failed states and poverty. and of course we must constantly advocate that the management of immigration in the european union and at the borders is done with strict respect for the human rights and dignity of immigrants. think globally but act locally, your honours. it is inevitable that we will also have to deal with the local reality of immigration in the border areas of the european union. i believe that a comprehensive approach to immigration is essential.
in writing. i voted in favour of this draft amending budget because it points to the problem of reducing member states' contributions following the decision of the united kingdom to maintain its method of calculating gdp. this report shows the reduction in both payments and credit that certain european institutions will have to face as a result of this irresponsible decision. the proposal ensures that the necessary payments are made, while at the same time criticising the consequences of the reduction in the european union's own resources. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which is part of the overall agreement to approve the amending budget for 2014 and the budget for 2015. this chapter is intended in particular to revise the estimates of traditional own resources (customs duties and sugar levies) and to revise the estimates of other revenue from a set of fines which have become definitive and can therefore be entered in the budget. it is therefore part of the overall agreement which will allow the payment of outstanding invoices, for which the amount of eur 4,7 billion has been agreed for the period 2014-2015. in addition, the commission, the council and parliament have agreed on a payment plan aimed at reducing the level of unpaid invoices within the current multiannual framework. the agreed eur 4.7 billion will make it possible to meet part of the accumulated bills, thus helping to alleviate the situation of many smes, universities, local authorities and ngos. for 2015, eur 145 321.5 million has been agreed for commitment appropriations and eur 141 214.040 563 million for payment appropriations. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. in january 2014, i had the pleasure of being the rapporteur for the european parliament's report on the reform of regulation (ec) no 2012/2002 establishing and regulating the eu solidarity funds. the objective of the mobilisation of these funds is to minimise the immediate and direct impact of natural disasters. the funds are used to cover part of the costs of emergency services and the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the most necessary infrastructure and services. the floods in italy and croatia, the earthquake in greece and the frost in slovenia call for effective action. in this sense, the solidarity funds not only have an effect on the recovery of those most basic infrastructures, such as roads or railways, but also have a considerable impact on the recovery and stabilisation of economic and social activity in regions affected by natural disasters. the solidarity funds are a fundamental instrument for promoting and strengthening the bonds of cooperation and solidarity between member states.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report which is part of the overall agreement to approve the amending budget for 2014 and the budget for 2015. in particular, draft amending budget no 8/2014 seeks to record for the financial year 2014 the surplus of the financial year 2013, amounting to eur 1 005 million. the agreement reached will allow the payment of outstanding invoices, for which the amount of eur 4.7 billion has been agreed for the period 2014-2015. in addition, the commission, the council and parliament have agreed on a payment plan aimed at reducing the level of unpaid invoices within the current multiannual framework. over the course of this year, an unprecedented level of defaults has accumulated. the 4.7 billion agreed will allow some of the accumulated bills to be met, thus helping to alleviate the situation of many smes, universities, local authorities and ngos. for 2015, eur 145 321 500 000 has been agreed for commitment appropriations and eur 141 214 040 563 for payment appropriations. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. in the light of the latest statistical revisions approved by the member states, it appears that some states have not paid their contributions to the union budget in full for several years, while others have overpaid, and that these deviations have been determined by the significant statistical changes reported by the member states. some member states which in the past benefited from the underestimation of their gni have expressed reluctance to pay the additional amounts due before the legal deadline expires. in view of this situation, the council asked the commission to submit a proposal to take account of this situation by changing the relevant rules and allowing the deferral and payment in instalments of the amounts due. the new proposal introduces greater discretion for member states as regards the timing of their additional contributions to the union budget, resulting from the adjustments to gni. it is easy to see that this will create further difficulties for future eu budgets, which is why i could not vote in favour and abstained.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to provide european solidarity to the disaster-stricken regions of europe. the fund may provide financial assistance to member states and acceding countries in the event of a major natural disaster provided that the total direct damage exceeds eur 3 000 million in 2011 prices or 0,6% of the country's gross national income, whichever is the lower. article 10 of the mff regulation for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund within the annual ceiling of eur 500 000 000. this decision of the european parliament and of the council is not linked to any specific case of natural disaster. instead, it aims to enter eur 50 000 000 in commitment and payment appropriations in the 2015 budget, corresponding to advances that will have to be paid more quickly and efficiently in the event of a natural disaster next year. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this decision of the parliament and the council which will allow a total of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations to be entered in the 2015 budget for the european union solidarity fund.

in writing. in 2002, as a result of severe floods in central europe, the eu decided to create the solidarity funds to respond to major natural disasters, the basis of which was laid down in regulation (ec) no 2012/2002. the priority for the mobilisation of the solidarity funds is to minimise the immediate and direct impact of natural disasters. in this regard, in january 2014 i had the pleasure of being the rapporteur for the european parliament's report on the reform of the regulation establishing these funds with the aim of ensuring a rapid and effective mobilisation. the reform entered into force on 28 june 2014, ensuring greater efficiency and speed in the mobilisation of funds and simplification of the criteria for applying for aid. achieving the objectives of speed and efficiency is crucial to minimize the impact of natural disasters. the speed with which these funds can be made available to cover part of the rescue effort and to start the reconstruction and recovery of strategic infrastructure and services will be a major factor in the economic and social recovery of regions affected by natural disasters.

in writing. the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity through financial support to the regions affected by these disasters in europe. the eusf currently has a maximum budget of eur 500 million per year, but it has been noted that in many cases it would be desirable to create a mechanism to deal with cases of extreme urgency. to this end, 10% of the eusf's total funding - a €50 million fund - is set aside for early financing of disaster-affected areas, allowing for faster and more efficient response without waiting for the bureaucratic red tape to be completed. this is not just another form of eu financial support, but a clear political message of solidarity, while providing real assistance to the citizens concerned.
