in writing. i voted against the new eu budget for 2015 because it is a budget along the same lines as the previous ones. it continues to promote the neoliberal economic policies which have brought us into the crisis, it insists on memoranda and reform programmes for the member states, it insists on privatisation and liberalisation of public services, on austerity, on cuts and the deregulation of industrial relations. the amount of this budget has also been cut, at a time when public investment is most needed to create jobs and to guarantee public services for all european citizens.
in writing. following difficult negotiations, following the tripartite dialogue of 8 december 2014, the council position on the new draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2015 is adopted. we welcome the progress achieved in the negotiations which is in line with parliament's political priorities and reaffirm the utmost importance of the work of the high level group on own resources chaired by mr mario monti. it welcomed the increase of eur 244,2 million in the overall level of commitment appropriations compared to the original council position of 2 september 2014 and that the agreed overall level of payment appropriations for 2015 represents an increase of 1,6% compared to the 2014 budget. i also think that the implementation of the first phase of the cooperation agreement between parliament and the european economic and social committee and the committee of the regions is very satisfactory, as it is a good example of the search for synergies between the institutions. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. after difficult negotiations, parliament has managed to reverse the council's cuts and increase the budget in certain key areas. for example, an increase of eur 45 million has been achieved for heading 1a, namely for the cosme programme and for horizon 2020, and eur 16 million for erasmus+, as well as an additional eur 32 million for heading 4 (unwra and humanitarian aid). in total, commitment appropriations of eur 145 321 500 000 and payment appropriations of eur 141 214 040 563 have been agreed for 2015. in addition, an agreement has been reached to reduce the level of unpaid invoices within the current multiannual framework. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. the eu budget this year does not respond to the social and economic needs of the eu, which is why i am voting against it.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 1071/2009 aims at the completion of an internal market in road transport with fair conditions of competition, which requires the uniform application of common rules for access to the occupation of road haulage operator or road passenger transport operator. the commission's measure should have included a comprehensive list of both the harmonised infringements and the harmonised level of seriousness which may lead to the loss of the transporter's good repute. that is not the case, and that is why this report is opposed to the adoption of the commission's regulation, and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. the draft regulation, which parliament decided to reject, was intended to harmonise infringements which endanger road safety and can lead to the loss of the honour of road hauliers in the eu. i abstained on this motion for a resolution because, although the draft regulation could have been improved in certain social aspects, it represents a first step in the harmonization of sanctions and gives greater legal certainty to international carriers. it would put an end to the abuses of certain traffic authorities against foreign drivers, by imposing the same criteria for sanctioning infringements of such importance for road safety and social legislation as respect for drivers' working and rest times, the validity of the authorization and driving licence, and the fight against fraud in connection with driving licences or control mechanisms such as the tachograph or the speed limiter. we hope that the commission will be able to present a new draft regulation which will provide greater legal certainty and put an end to the excessive zeal of certain states against carriers from the periphery.
in writing. to practise as a road haulage operator in the eu, you must show that you have a fixed establishment in a member state, that you have the financial and professional capacity to practise the profession and that you can prove that you are a reputable haulage operator. the draft implementing regulation harmonises the infringements which can lead to the loss of the good name of road hauliers in the eu, in particular those which endanger road safety. until now, states were responsible for assessing the seriousness of infringements committed by carriers, with a wide disparity in penalties between them for the same infringement, which created legal uncertainty for international carriers. i believe that this draft regulation should have been adopted in order to make progress in the harmonization of penalties and, therefore, in the legal certainty of carriers, which is why i abstained in voting on this resolution, which prevents progress along both lines.
in writing. to practise as a road haulage operator in the eu, four essential elements must be demonstrated: a fixed establishment in the union, the financial and professional capacity to practise the profession and the ability to demonstrate good repute. this implementing regulation harmonises the offences which may lead to the loss of good repute. until now, the states were responsible for assessing the seriousness of infringements, with different penalties for the same infringement. this has created legal uncertainty for international carriers and also abuses by the traffic authorities with certain foreign carriers, with france even providing for prison sentences for the driver to take the weekly rest in the cabin. the regulation harmonises only those penalties which pose a high risk to road safety, typically overworking, driving without a valid licence, overweight, fraud in controls such as the tachograph, etc. but it does not go into detail on other types of infringement, such as the rules on international cabotage.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 1071/2009 aims at the completion of an internal market in road transport with fair conditions of competition, which requires the uniform application of common rules for access to the occupation of road haulage operator or road passenger transport operator. the commission's measure should have included a comprehensive list of both the harmonised infringements and the harmonised level of seriousness which may lead to the loss of the transporter's good repute. that is not the case, and that is why this report is opposed to the adoption of the commission's regulation, and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - we vote in favour of this motion for a resolution which opposes the adoption of the draft commission regulation on the classification of serious infringements of the union which may lead to the loss of the honour of the carrier. the proposal calls on the commission to withdraw the draft and to submit a new list of infringements, as it does not meet the objective of creating fair conditions of competition, does not improve the service and harms the already deteriorated working conditions of hauliers, by not explicitly referring to illegal cabotage, an abusive practice that significantly affects the living and working conditions of the haulier and therefore carries a high potential to create a risk of death or serious injury.

in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it opposes the adoption of the draft council directive, as i consider that this draft directive is not compatible with the objective and content of directive 98/70/eu. i think the commission should withdraw its draft council directive and present a new one to the committee based on the obligation to declare the default mean values of greenhouse gas emission intensity broken down by type of raw material in relation to petrol and diesel, while allowing suppliers to declare the actual values. since the motion for a resolution calls for exactly this, i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted against the resolution and in favour of the commission proposal because the objective of the commission proposal was to establish a methodology which is clear and effective for measuring the 6% reduction in emissions from transport fuels, as set out in article 7 of directive 98/70, and always based on the types of raw materials used in 2010. the resolution of the parliament went further and wanted to restrict a type of crude oil that can be used in the eu and this would have very negative consequences for the european industry which has made large investments to achieve the 6% co2 reduction target and which agrees to apply the proposed methodology.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution calling on the commission to withdraw the implementing act concerning the new calculation methods of the fuel quality directive. the calculation method proposed by the commission does not adequately address the needs for more information and traceability. it is necessary to indicate the greenhouse gas emission intensity, not for the overall product, but for each component of the fuel, so that for each gasoline, diesel, etc. to be used in the eu, its contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is known and therefore whether the product meets the requirements and objectives of the quality directive (6% less intensity by 2020) and other derivative directives on emission limits. the commission should continue to work towards finding a measurement method that will encourage the use of more sustainable fuels by the production companies and the progressive abandonment of the most environmentally harmful unconventional fuels and raw materials.
in writing. the commission's proposal is to measure the greenhouse gas emission intensity of the sum total of the fuel components so that for each petrol, diesel, etc. to be used in the eu, its contribution to greenhouse gas emissions is known and therefore whether the product meets the requirements and objectives of the quality directive (6% less intensity by 2020) and other derivative directives on emission limits. to this end, although the origin of each and every component of the product is analysed in such a way as to have access to sensitive data such as the inclusion of material from tar sands, the method proposed by the commission does not specify the quantity used in the product as a whole for each component. in other words, there is a record of the generic use but not of the quantity used. the delegation, like the group, supported the resolution tabled with objections to the commission's proposal, believing that the commission should work further on the calculation method before it could be finally adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it opposes the adoption of the draft council directive, as i consider that this draft directive is not compatible with the objective and content of directive 98/70/eu. i think the commission should withdraw its draft council directive and present a new one to the committee based on the obligation to declare the default mean values of greenhouse gas emission intensity broken down by type of raw material in relation to petrol and diesel, while allowing suppliers to declare the actual values. since the motion for a resolution calls for exactly this, i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. - we voted to ban the use of tar sands and shale gas. the eu is siding with oil interests with the commission's proposal to implement article 7a of the fuel quality directive, which does not discriminate against the consumption of the dirtiest fuels, thus hindering the objective for which it was created: the reduction of greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by 2020. scientific studies show that unconventional oils cause higher ghg emissions than conventional oils: 23% more for oil from tar sands and 50% more for oil from oil shale. the american oil companies, and also repsol, together with the governments of canada and the usa, were opposed to differentiation by type of oil and to the penalization of the most polluting. after eight years of delay, due to pressure from canada, the usa and the big oil companies, a regulation in their interests is finally adopted. the eu is thus putting trade agreements (cfta-fta) ahead of its already unambitious climate commitments.

in writing. the opinion of stecf scientists supports the idea of reducing the reference size of cod in the baltic sea. given that the size of this species has been reduced and that it is therefore mature at 35 centimetres, i voted against the motion for a resolution by the ecr group to support the decision of the stecf and the baltic sea advisory council.
in writing. the commission has presented a delegated act on the baltic discard plan which provides for the reduction of the tac for cod from the current 38 cm to 35 cm. the ec justifies this reduction on the grounds that cod is very dense in the baltic sea and is therefore suffering from certain problems of reduced growth, increased parasites, etc., which has increased discards and reduced the size of mature specimens. the proposal to reduce the rtmc does not imply an increased mortality, because the characteristics of the permitted networks do not change. according to stecf, this reduction does not affect the fry, because spawning occurs below 35 cm. the reduction will have a positive effect on the economic returns of cod fisheries, as the current discards of between 30 and 35 cm represent 83% in number and weight. the baltic member states and the baltic raf also support it. in addition, the reduction in size will bring coherence with other regions, for example the north sea, where it is already 35 cm. i therefore voted against the proposal for a commission delegated act.
in writing. the european commission has presented a delegated act on the baltic sea discard plan. the plan envisages reducing the minimum conservation reference size (mcrs) of cod from the current 38 centimetres to 35. the ec justifies this reduction in the minimum conservation reference size on several grounds; the spanish delegation is particularly interested in the point on the reduction in size, which will bring coherence with other regions, for example the north sea, where it is already 35 cm. this sets a precedent in the approval of minimum sizes which will benefit spain when it applies the same for other species such as hake in future demersal plans for north-western and south-western waters.

in writing. i voted in favour of this because i believe that the reduction of the minimum reference size from 38 cm to 35 cm proposed by the commission for the conservation of cod in the baltic sea could weaken the reproductive capacity of this stock, encourage the creation of a market for fry and remove an important incentive to implement improvements in the use of more selective gear. in addition to all this, i am mindful of the council decision on the total allowable catch (tac) for cod stocks which foresees a reduction in the quota (7% in the western baltic and 22% in the eastern baltic) in 2015 in order to protect this species. i therefore voted in favour of these objections being raised.

in writing. i have not voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the preparation of a new internal security strategy for the next four years because it is based on the same principles as before, basing security on a purely repressive approach and ignoring the radical approach, that is, the root causes of these new threats. that is why i voted against.
in writing. the current security challenges in europe are cross-border, making it difficult for member states to respond individually. in 2010, the eu's internal security strategy (iss) was adopted, setting out guidelines for tackling security threats in europe where the eu can bring added value: international networks of cross-border crime, prevention of terrorist attacks, cyber security, border security or resilience to natural disasters. the commission presented its new proposal for the esi 2015-2019 in march. the resolution adopted recognises that the security situation in europe has changed dramatically due to new conflicts and calls for more effective cooperation between member states through greater use of valuable existing instruments such as joint investigation teams. it also calls for a future strategy focusing on both existing and emerging threats, with a holistic approach covering as many areas as possible, such as foreign fighters and cybersecurity threats. always in accordance with fundamental rights and data protection. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. the text recognises that the security situation in europe has changed dramatically due to new conflicts and calls for more effective cooperation between member states through greater use of valuable existing instruments such as joint investigation teams. in addition, a future strategy focusing on both existing and emerging threats is required, with a holistic approach including as many areas as possible, such as foreign fighters and cybersecurity threats. it is important to note that this is a balanced text which emphasises the need to ensure that security measures are always carried out in accordance with fundamental rights and which refers in particular to the court of justice decision on data retention and the proposal for a data protection directive. the motion for a resolution and the oral question have been studied by all the political groups and, after much negotiation, agreement has been reached on a text.
in writing. i have not voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the preparation of a new internal security strategy for the next four years because it is based on the same principles as before, basing security on a purely repressive approach, ignoring the radical approach, that is, the root cause of these new threats. that is why i voted against.
in writing. the current security challenges in europe are cross-border, making it difficult for member states to respond individually. in 2010, the eu's internal security strategy (iss) was adopted, setting out guidelines for tackling security threats in europe where the eu can bring added value: international networks of cross-border crime, prevention of terrorist attacks, cyber security, border security or resilience to natural disasters. the commission presented its new proposal for the esi 2015-2019 in march. the resolution adopted recognises that the security situation in europe has changed dramatically due to new conflicts and calls for more effective cooperation between member states through greater use of valuable existing instruments such as joint investigation teams. it also calls for a future strategy focusing on both existing and emerging threats, with a holistic approach covering as many areas as possible, such as foreign fighters and cybersecurity threats. always in accordance with fundamental rights and data protection. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. i have not voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the preparation of a new internal security strategy for the next four years because it is based on the same principles as before, basing security on a purely repressive approach and ignoring the radical approach, that is, the root causes of these new threats. that is why i voted against.
in writing. i consider it vital that the new internal security strategy (iss) for 2015-2019 is thoroughly prepared. we should focus on both existing and emerging security threats, highlighting priority areas such as cybersecurity, human trafficking and counter-terrorism, and related issues such as organised crime, money laundering and corruption. the transit between europe and conflict zones of european citizens who have joined terrorist groups poses a risk to the internal security of the eu. we must therefore set up mechanisms to analyse and counter this phenomenon, promoting political and religious tolerance, as well as fostering the development of social cohesion, inclusion and facilitating reintegration, and thus discouraging terrorism. to meet all these challenges, i believe that greater interinstitutional and crossborder cooperation is imperative, in which the right balance between prevention policies and repressive measures is never compromised, since the aim is to preserve freedom, security and justice. that is why i am voting in favour of this proposal.

mr president, this is not our resolution. this is not a perfect resolution. we are missing, for example, a clear condemnation of israel's constant violations of international law. we have voted for it, however. we voted for it and, moreover, with a certain amount of enthusiasm, quite a lot of enthusiasm, because of the consensus it has generated. and above all because it unreservedly and unconditionally recognises the will of this parliament - and therefore the will of european citizens - to support the building of a palestinian state. it recognises the need and the right of the palestinian people, who have lived for centuries in their territories, to create a modern state, a state which can be recognized and internationally recognized, in order to ensure the welfare, social justice and future of their population. and it also means that europe is once again on the international front line. it involves europe in this peace process, in which we have not been heard for a long time, and it was time for us to return to it.
in writing. recognition of the palestinian state is a necessary, but not sufficient, step towards achieving peace between israel and palestine. i believe that the only way to resolve this conflict is through a two-state solution based on the 1967 borders, with jerusalem as the capital of both states. in this way, the state of israel could live in peace and security alongside an independent, democratic and viable palestinian state. i support this motion for a resolution as a compromise solution and because of the high value of both the broad consensus reached by all the groups in this parliament and the important message we have sent with it. i want to express my firm support for the recognition of a palestinian state, since the right of the palestinians to have their own state is as unquestionable as the right of israel to exist within secure borders. i also value the leadership of high representative federica mogherini in this process, as i believe that the eu must play a more effective and genuine role in the peace process, and i believe it is necessary for eu member states to be united in their support for this legitimate process.

in writing. - we voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because we consider it a step forward for a majority of the european parliament to take a position in favour of a basic demand such as the creation and international recognition of a palestinian state with its capital in jerusalem. this is nothing more than a reaffirmation of what the un already demands in its 1947 resolution 181, paradoxically the only one that israel partially complies with, as regards the partition of palestine. we also believe that the recognition of the palestinian state should be only one step in the process of achieving a just peace which, taking into account the demands of civil society itself, should include the end of the occupation (in compliance with un resolution 242 of 1967), the right of return of refugees (resolution 194 of 1948) and a state guaranteeing full equality for all its citizens. we also believe that, in order to enforce the content of the resolution, the eu should use pressure mechanisms, at least the suspension of the eu-israel bilateral agreement, in accordance with article 2 thereof, in view of the flagrant violation of human rights that the continuation of the blockade of the gaza strip entails.

mr president, we have supported the motion for a resolution by the group of the european united left because we believe that the serious situation in the steel sector in europe is the result of selling the industry to the highest bidder and not a matter of 'competitiveness', as the majority groups would have us believe. in spain, high value-added and geographically rooted enterprises face the threat of relocation by large multinational groups. these impose very harsh adjustments which the policies of the european union only exacerbate. on the one hand, europe remains unmoved by the serious abuses of the energy and financial oligopolies which are suffocating industry. it also encourages competition between member states, reinforcing the tendency for the production of higher value added products to be concentrated in a few european regions. we believe that the answer to the industrial crisis is, among other things, to regain public control of the strategic sectors on which the sector depends, by opting for a programme of investment and public aid that preserves employment in dynamic and efficient sectors such as the spanish steel industry and auxiliary companies. from this point of view, we stand in solidarity with the workers of alcoa, thyssenkrupp, elcogas and bosal, who are fighting for their jobs, for their future and for the future of the industry.
in writing. the serious situation of the steel sector in europe is the result of selling the industry to the highest bidder and not a matter of competitiveness as the majority groups' motion for a resolution advocates. high value-added businesses across the eu are constantly threatened by relocations by large multinational groups that impose very harsh adjustments that eu policies only exacerbate. on the one hand, europe remains unmoved by the gross abuses of the energy and financial oligopolies which are suffocating industry. and it also encourages competition between member states, reinforcing the tendency for higher value-added production to be concentrated in certain regions of the eu. the response to the industrial crisis is to regain public control of the strategic sectors on which the sector depends, by focusing on investment and public aid to preserve employment in the sector. since none of this is included in the joint resolution, i could not vote in favour of it and i abstained.
in writing. i voted in favour of this joint resolution and not as my group voted because i consider the steel sector to be a strategic sector of the european union, which the eu should support in order to remove obstacles and threats to its competitiveness, increase its capacity and respond to changing conditions in europe and the world by strengthening its support for innovation, technology and research through the horizon 2020 programme and spire, as well as with a stronger role for the eib by investing in riskier projects. we must commit ourselves so that the sector can, through innovation, make possible quality and energy-efficient products.
in writing. the resolution underlines the role that the steel industry, recognised as one of the strategic sectors of european industry, must play in the reindustrialisation of europe. the resolution calls on the commission to present as soon as possible a roadmap for the industrial recovery of europe and the integration of the steel industry into it. parliament called on the commission to relaunch the high level group on steel and to speed up the implementation of the 40 measures of the steel plan, but also to prevent unfair competition from third countries. it also stresses the need to invest in research and development in the european economy in general and in the steel industry in particular. the resolution also calls on the commission to ensure that the current system of state aid does not distort the internal market and to ensure a level playing field for companies, as industry needs a stable framework for its investments in order to maintain employment. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the resolution underlines the role which the steel industry is called upon to play in the reindustrialisation of europe. the commission is also asked to give its views on the steel plan, in particular on its financing, timing and implementation of the 40 measures. the resolution addresses the competitiveness of the steel industry in the internal and global markets, the need for investment in research and innovation, concrete measures to reduce the high energy costs facing the sector and the need to urgently modernise trade defence instruments to protect the european industry from social and environmental dumping by third countries. an amendment tabled by the spanish socialist members of the itre committee has been incorporated, requesting that measures be taken to ensure that the current scheme of state aid to energy-intensive industries does not create distortions in the internal market, so that a level playing field is guaranteed for companies and that energy-intensive industries can have a stable framework for their investments and guarantee employment.

in writing. in june 2013, the european commission presented an action plan for the european steel industry with the aim of helping the sector to lay the foundations for future competitiveness by fostering innovation, generating growth and creating jobs. the european commission also committed itself to reducing costs for industry, in particular those arising from eu regulation. the action plan also provided for specific measures to support employment in the sector in europe. however, the action plan has not yet been translated into concrete initiatives by the commission. i would like to stress the importance of the resolution we have adopted today, which stresses the need to achieve these objectives, and the fact that, at the initiative of the socialist group, the resolution includes the need for europe to have a stable european framework for supporting energy-intensive industries, avoiding distortions in the internal market, accelerating the renewal of trade defence instruments to combat unfair competition, continuing to support ccs pilot projects and boosting investment in the modernisation of european-based plants.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution bearing in mind that, although the steel industry is fundamental to growth and prosperity in europe, it is a sector in crisis. the european steel industry has for years been an important source of wealth for the economies of the member states and must remain competitive in european and non-european markets. we must prevent the sector from losing jobs any further, given that it provides 350 000 direct jobs. the steel sector is a good example of how an economic sector with a long history has been able to adapt to new technologies, reducing their environmental impact. eu steel products meet stricter social, environmental and economic standards than elsewhere, and the sector must be protected by measures to prevent its outsourcing outside the eu. the commission has also taken the view that the measures proposed by the member states should be implemented in a manner that is compatible with the common market.

in writing. more than a year ago, after the lampedusa tragedy, the ep adopted a resolution on migration flows in the mediterranean and the council was to set up a special group. this was followed by several communications from the commission. last month the council adopted measures to better manage migration flows and at the last plenary we expressed the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration. despite all this, deaths have continued to occur and the desired change in approach to immigration is not seen, the victim of a negative look that ignores the opportunities it offers and does not give alternatives to legal immigration. this resolution sets out the elements which a comprehensive approach must contain and calls on the libe commission to submit a strategic report on the subject. it also raises issues such as the exercise of solidarity and fair burden-sharing as required by article 80 tfeu, rescue and anti-mafia obligations, extension of the mandate of frontex, establishment of safe routes for immigration, improved resettlement and improved policies and management of immigration funds. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. i could not vote in favour of this motion for a resolution because its purpose, which is to give a mandate to the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs of this house to set up a committee of inquiry into the situation of migration in the mediterranean, has been very much diluted. but, more importantly, the resolution does not reject the fundamental pillar of eu immigration policy: frontex. it is a migration policy based on a repressive view of migration, ignoring its root causes: the phenomenon of migration from the countries of the southern mediterranean to the eu countries exists because we in europe continue to plunder the natural resources of those countries, thus preventing them from economic prosperity and a future for their peoples. if migrants from africa continue to arrive on our shores, it is because we continue to encourage wars in their countries that push them to leave. i have therefore voted against this motion for a resolution.

in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a holistic eu approach as it represents a humanitarian drama which the eu must address to prevent tragedies like lampedusa from happening again. according to the international organization for migration, in the first nine months of 2014, at least 3,072 people have died in the mediterranean sea while trying to reach european shores. we must be determined to put an end to the smugglers and traffickers of human beings who exploit irregular immigration and who pose a serious risk to the lives of migrants. the eu must recognise that irregular immigration is a problem affecting the whole union and that a comprehensive approach to this issue is therefore essential. the member states must provide frontex with the necessary means and cooperate closely to ensure the proper control of the eu's borders, especially in the mediterranean sea. similarly, it is essential to continue to cooperate with countries of origin and transit in order to address the causes of migration.

in writing. - i voted against because the text does not address several crucial issues to deal with the dramatic and desperate situation in the mediterranean faced by migrants trying to reach europe. on the one hand, it does not agree to set up a committee of inquiry, which is a priority for me. the text talks about providing more resources for ad hoc hearings and delegations, which means an investment of those resources to have a theoretical approach through experts, but it does not specify the creation of a commission of inquiry. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat illegal immigration, including the introduction of a new system of national criminal law. the idea of europe as a fortress is thus strengthened.

mr president, this parliament must reopen the committee of inquiry which, during 2006 and 2007, tried to establish what happened to the cia flights. the end does not justify the means and democracies must be accountable for both the ends and the means. we recognize the exemplary work that the us senate has done, but we cannot stand alone in recognizing that exemplary work. this parliament investigated the cia flight programme in 2006 and 2007 - i was a member of that non-permanent committee - with great difficulty. in view of the report by the us senate, this report by the european parliament is no longer useful to us. that is why we must reopen that committee of inquiry. we must do so, as the us senate has done, without fear of knowing the truth, to clear up the responsibilities that would result. we owe it to this house, which has worked with great difficulty. and we owe it to the european citizens who are watching us. you see, ladies and gentlemen, in order to be able to give lessons - as we are going to do this week - on human rights to sudan, mauritania, venezuela and egypt, we must first be able to set an example. and this debate, today's debate, must be the beginning - not the end - of a work that this parliament has to complete, which began in 2006 and was unable to complete. that is what we are asking from the socialist group. we need to reopen the investigation committee. i'm sorry mr brok is not here. guantanamo has to be shut down. beyond whether or not countries host guantanamo detainees. because when they opened guantanamo, they didn't ask anyone's permission.
mr president, the subject is the use of torture by the cia, but it links directly to member states of the european union, both because of their complicity in the cia's plan for detention centres in europe and because torture is also practised here in the european union. the commissioner has recalled this when he stressed that the european commission is fighting for the eradication of torture both in the european union and in the rest of the world. and he also spoke of prosecuting the guilty - not like in the united states, where president obama has just given an official certificate of impunity. here in europe, in a political trial taking place in madrid against 28 young basques, it has been established, on the basis of the application of the istanbul protocol, that they were subjected to torture and, just two months ago, the european court of human rights condemned, once again, the spanish state for failing to investigate allegations of torture made by basque or catalan citizens.
madam president, the actions against journalists and the free press in turkey deserve our full condemnation, as is happening in this parliament, not only because they are an attack on freedom of expression, but because they send a message that we do not like at all about where erdoğan is leading his country. the space for the opposition and the space for the people protesting is getting smaller and smaller in turkey, and even the rhetoric of the government is becoming more and more intolerant. the socialist group in this house and, of course, the spanish socialists have always defended the need for a european turkey. we thought that would be a good thing and that we could find common ground. it would be good for europe, it would be good for turkey, it would be good for that whole region of the world that is so important for our stability. but that also requires the turkish government to play its part and to dispel any doubts, any doubts that may be raised about its willingness to undertake democratic reforms, and lately it is generating a great deal of doubt. every crime must be condemned, but within the framework of the rule of law, and we will have to follow very closely the actions of the erdoğan government. we need a european turkey, but we have the impression that turkey is moving away from europe.

president of the council. - madam president, i thank the honourable members who have spoken and participated in this debate, also for the relevance of the speeches and arguments and for the concerns expressed which i believe are to a large extent absolutely common concerns. it was appropriate to take this opportunity to acknowledge the serious concerns about the latest events in order to formulate an unambiguous position and to convey it with absolute clarity and consistency to our turkish partners. we must continue to monitor the situation with the utmost care. the european union must continue to promote freedom of expression, opinion, assembly and association, both online and offline, because a democracy cannot exist without these rights. turkey is a privileged partner with whom we are negotiating accession; and we can and must communicate with her frankly. as president schulz said, the relationship with the applicant countries must be honest and open. i would just like to take up the point raised by the honourable member concerning funding, which is certainly one that deserves attention. the european union does not finance the turkish budget but mainly ngos and institutions promoting the rule of law and human rights, mainly through two instruments, namely the pre-accession instrument and the european instrument on human rights. the commission is looking at how to make this form of assistance more effective and i would point out, among other things, that the per capita allocations to turkey are still the lowest among the applicant countries. the enlargement framework is the right one for us to engage in the process of deepening and consolidating democratic reforms. further commitment in the context of chapter 3 would be an important encouragement. we have done a lot to intensify this engagement with turkey, a candidate country and a partner of the european union. we must continue along this road.
member of the commission. - madam president, honourable members, let me first of all thank mr andrejs mamikins for his report, which contains many important recommendations and shows that we have a high degree of consensus on our policy with georgia. the european parliament’s strong support will be an important message for the reinforcement of our ties with georgia and it will create excellent conditions for closer cooperation with georgia. georgia is one of the frontrunners of the european union’s eastern partnership policy. the association agreement before you today is the result of georgia’s european aspirations. it is also the result of our determination to promote building a democratic, stable and prosperous country in a region that is of key strategic importance to us. georgia will transform itself as we implement our joint agenda. georgia will, as a result, move closer to the european union, deepening its political association and economic integration with the eu. georgia will introduce reforms that will build into its public life core european values such as a pluralist democracy and a deeper respect for due process and the rule of law. following the signature and the provisions of application of the agreement, we have had our first eu-georgia association council under the agreement exactly one month ago in brussels – the first step for the implementation of this agreement. on the same day we concluded that georgia meets the first phase requirements of the visa dialogue and that the second implementation phase of the action plan could be launched. this was yet another important step in the process that will bring georgia closer to its goal of a visa-free regime with the european union. it is difficult to say that georgia has made important progress in its democratic development following parliamentary and presidential elections in 2012 and 2013 as well as local elections in 2014. but this message was also given and was well received. the political climate in the country needs improving. political confrontation and polarisation should be avoided and space for opposition and cross-party dialogue needs to be ensured. in the same vein, georgia needs to continue efforts to reform the judiciary and ensure the rule of law. i am pleased to report that the provisional application of the deep and comprehensive free trade area of the association agreement since 1 december is already showing first results. trade statistics for september are positive and stable. the effect of the agreement is yet to be confirmed but the september 2014 figures indicate a 50% increase in imports from georgia into the european union, mainly in nuts and mineral products. the european union will further assist reforms in georgia and help small and medium enterprises adapt to the new regulatory framework with a eur 51 million programme under the annual action programme of this year. let me now turn to the most recent developments in the georgian breakaway regions, mainly the so-called strategic partnership treaty between the russian federation and the abkhazia de facto authorities. reports on a similar undertaking with the south ossetian de facto authorities are equally disconcerting. just like earlier agreements signed between the russian federation and abkhazia, this so-called treaty questions the sovereignty and integrity of georgia. it is also detrimental to ongoing efforts to stabilise the security situation in the region, and it does not contribute to de-escalation. it also contradicts principles of international law and commitments taken by the russian federation. let me reconfirm the european union’s unwavering support for georgia’s territorial integrity. we remain fully committed to supporting conflict resolution in georgia including through our co-chairmanship of the geneva international talks and our monitoring mission in georgia. let me also, again, underline our appreciation for georgia’s contribution to the european union’s mission in the central african republic on the basis of our framework agreement for georgia’s participation in the european union’s common security and defence policy missions. to conclude, let me say that the partnership between the european union and georgia is a strong one. it will become even stronger with the european parliament’s verification of our association agreement.
on behalf of the alde group. madam president, this is a strategic, fundamental and important agreement, because we are saying several things. first of all, that georgia is europe. secondly, that as europe, it has the absolute right to decide what its national wishes, criteria and objectives are, including full association with the european union, in accordance with article 49 of our treaty. thirdly, it is not a complacent statement. it is not a statement in which the merits of the georgian state are simply determined. the european union is also calling for the release of all political prisoners, including those who have been held in custody for more than two years. it is a resolution which establishes respect for peace, a fundamental issue which means respect for borders, and which consequently condemns any act which constitutes an attack on peace and security, specifically the invasions, or the alleged annexations, in this case of abkhazia, and the presence of south ossetia as a secessionist zone with russian presence. it is also something that is fundamental. it is not against anyone, it does not mean any contradiction with what are the legitimate interests of any country, and in this case - let us say it by its name - of a great country, which is russia, which has to be more than a great neighbor: it has to be a great friend too, a great friend of europe. because russia is also europe. and so this is another building block for european unity and is directed towards peace, not towards contradiction against anyone.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i firmly believe that it is essential to establish a continuous and balanced dialogue with the countries of the horn of africa. the question is not whether we should cooperate with these countries, but how we can do so to avoid migrants falling victim to the networks that facilitate their illegal entry into europe by sea. the khartoum process is only one element of a global strategy. i share your concerns about the objectives of this initiative. however, i want to make it clear that our policy does not legitimize regimes in the region: the aim is to engage states and make them face up to their responsibilities to save lives and fight those responsible for human trafficking. they must keep their word and their commitments. i assure you we will be following this process closely. on the other hand, one of my priorities is to strengthen the links between the internal and external policies of the european union, in order to deal, in a coherent and comprehensive way, with the migratory pressures we are facing. i want to develop this point in the european agenda on migration which was launched yesterday as part of the commission's work programme for 2015. there is also no doubt that we must offer safer solutions to people who need international protection to reach europe. the commission is currently exploring all possibilities, including the development of a common approach to the issuing of humanitarian visas for refugees to come to europe and seek asylum. at the moment, the relocation of refugees is the main way to enter europe legally. this is an act of solidarity which the commission encourages, because for every refugee welcomed into europe, a life is saved. i am pleased that the union is supporting african countries to ensure that they receive refugees in the best possible conditions. in any case, as i said earlier, we will be following closely the development of this process and the application of its terms.

unauthorised rally, charged with disturbing the peace, insulting the authorities and belonging to an unrecognised organisation. according to its organizers, the rally was held to denounce the lack of respect for the traditional land rights of mauritanian people, mostly black, in the south of the country, near the border with senegal. at the same time, the mauritanian authorities state that biram is now in the hands of the judges, subject to judicial proceedings. we're very concerned about these latest arrests. through our delegation in mauritania, we are in regular contact with biram's organisation, we are kept informed of his situation in prison and the progress of the judicial proceedings. we take every opportunity to talk to the authorities about this. the european union's action. we've been informed that the trial may take place today. the european union delegation in the field is following developments and will be closely monitoring the process, which in any case should take place as soon as possible. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union has entered into a regular dialogue with mauritania on the question of human rights. we are also supporting the government in its efforts to strengthen institutions and bring legislation into line with human rights standards, but more needs to be done. in march 2014, mauritania adopted a un-backed roadmap with a set of recommendations to eradicate slavery in all its forms. it also agreed to set up a special criminal court to deal with slavery cases. the european union is strongly in writing. i have voted against this resolution objecting to the granting of gsp+ status to the philippines. the philippines, currently a beneficiary of the generalised system of preferences, has formally requested gsp+ treatment from the eu and meets the eligibility criteria set out in general terms in eu regulation no 978/2012. however, the parliamentary handling of this concession comes at a time when the commission's dg mare has opened a file and issued an ultimatum to the philippines, by means of a 'yellow card', for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing practices. this regrettable situation of lack of coordination of policy actions by the commission entails the risk that, from the approval of the gsp+ to the possible ban on imports of fishery products from the philippines, products obtained through illegal fishing practices will be imported into the eu duty free. if the philippines is confirmed as being guilty of illegal fishing with a 'red card', the european commission will have to assess the damage caused to european producers during the period of application of the gsp+ and fair compensation.
in writing. - this motion for a resolution by parliament calls for the system of generalized preferences not to be granted until the philippines has put an end to illegal fishing, trafficking of minors, etc. the eu grants gsp+ to third countries on the condition that they ratify and comply with 27 international conventions, some of which the philippines is not complying with. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because it calls for the gsp+ system not to be granted until guarantees are given by the philippines.
in writing. i have voted in favour of this recommendation for a european parliament decision, submitted in accordance with article 105 (6) of the regulation, not to raise objections to the commission delegated regulation of 21 october 2014 supplementing directive 2014/59/eu of the european parliament and of the council of 15 may 2014 with regard to ex ante contributions to the resolution financing arrangements (c2014) 07674 2014/2923 (dea)). i consider, as expressed in the recommendation itself, that the agreement in the council on the implementing regulation specifying uniform conditions for the application of regulation (eu) no 806/2014 of the european parliament and of the council as regards ex ante contributions to the single resolution fund, reached following the informal involvement of parliament, is consistent with the aforementioned delegated regulation, among other factors also expressed in this recommendation.
in writing. i voted against this report which approves the conclusion of an association agreement with georgia, which means the creation of a large free trade area between the eu and georgia. i have always voted against the creation of free trade areas between the eu and third countries, because i believe that these always benefit large companies and european big capital, to the detriment of local production in third countries. in this case, it couldn't be otherwise. it has also become clear that in the case of georgia the intention is to bring the country closer to the eu and nato and to remove it as far as possible from the influence of russia, which means interference in georgia's internal affairs. i have therefore voted against.
in writing. i support this motion for a resolution, which accompanies the recommendation on the association agreement with georgia, in which, among other issues, we welcome the progress made in abkhazia and south ossetia, as well as in relations with russia.
in writing. in short, the s&d group supports the association agreement with georgia as a tool for further democratisation and european integration. the reform of the judicial system to bring it into line with eu standards must be a priority for the georgian government. the group also strongly supports the territorial integrity of georgia and welcomes the steps taken by the government to improve dialogue with russia.

in writing. - we abstained on the vote on the eu-georgia association agreement for the following reasons. we respect the decision of the georgian people, who have shown their support for the european project, and we are in favour of the eu fostering cooperation ties with neighbouring countries. however, we are critical of the content of the agreement, which, among other things, imposes on georgia a gradual process of adaptation to the european framework without clear financial support and without the right to participate in the political process that could lead to its future full membership of the eu. the resolution also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism.

in writing. the agreement with georgia is the third in a new series of association agreements, after those signed with ukraine and moldova, which must be ratified by parliament. i have given my assent to the association agreement between the european union and georgia which will lead to greater political association and economic integration between the two parties, including the progressive opening up of their respective markets.
